chunks.section: Cover and document control
chunks.text:
TECHNICAL DIAGNOSTIC KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENT

Operating Conditions and Performance Standards

Stamping press 01 (press-stamp-01) | Main drive and lubrication circuit

| Machine | Stamping press 01 (machine ID press-stamp-01, type press, area Press shop, site vit-lab), stamping press in a car plant |
|---|---|
| Sensors | MAIN_MOTOR_CURRENT (A), LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE (bar), BEARING_VIBRATION_RMS (mm/s) and the 64-bin spectrum BEARING_SPECTRUM (mm/s); sensor IDs PRESS-STAMP-01.<CHANNEL_KEY> |
| Components / subsystem | Press main drive and its pressure lubrication circuit: main drive motor, lubrication unit (gear pump, reservoir, lube filter) and main bearing housing; planned agent tags main_drive_motor, lube_filter, lubrication_unit, main_bearing_housing |
| Document title | Operating Conditions and Performance Standards |
| Document ID | PS01-DOC-01 |
| Revision / date | 1.0 / 2026-10-08 |
| Purpose | Defines normal operation of press-stamp-01 (main drive motor current, lube oil pressure, bearing vibration RMS and the bearing spectrum) and the limits needed to decide whether telemetry is normal, watch, warning, alarm, critical or a sensor and data problem. |
| Scope | Normal behaviour, ranges, limits, operating states, load dependence, environment, transients, rate of change and alert escalation for the three scalar channels and the spectrum. Fault signatures are in Document 02, the diagnostic procedure in Document 03, maintenance in Document 04 and simulated cases in Document 05. |

Provenance tags used throughout this document

| [P] | Project value: taken from the repository or CONTEXT_PRESS_STAMP_01.md (catalog limits, simulation equations, topics, runbook stubs, tests). |
|---|---|
| [D] | Derived value: computed from the repository's own simulation model (seed 1, 2 Hz, 600 s per case) or algebraically from its equations, as recorded in the context file. |
| [E] | Engineering reference: general industrial practice for press drives, lubrication circuits and vibration diagnostics. Not a manufacturer value and not taken from the repository. |
| [I] | Illustrative / proposed prototype value: chosen by the authors for this knowledge base and meant to be refined with real plant data. |

Important: the telemetry for this machine is simulated. There is no physical press or transducer. An ESP32 gateway (or a software simulator) plays the press controller and generates values from documented equations. The repository describes its limits as illustrative constants chosen for the demo, not vendor values, and its runbooks as not an OEM manual. Values tagged [P] are therefore prototype values, not OEM specifications; values tagged [E] and [I] are not manufacturer-certified.

chunks.section: 1. Document Control and Retrieval Guide > 1.3 How to use this document; 1.4 Terms and abbreviations
chunks.text:
• For a single reading, go to Table 17 (master limits) and Table 18 (open and clear rules). A reading

is classified on a 10 s window, not on a single sample (Section 6.3).

• For a trend, use the rate-of-change and time-to-threshold tables in Section 16.

• For a pattern across channels, use Document 02 (signatures) and Document 03 (decision logic).

This document only classifies levels.

• Every number carries a provenance tag. A [P] number is a prototype value from the repository, not

an OEM specification.

RULE: never describe a [P] limit as a manufacturer value. The repository calls its limits "illustrative constants chosen for the demo, not vendor values".

Table 3. Terms
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| I, P, V | Motor current (A), lube oil pressure (bar), bearing vibration RMS (mm/s) |
| r | Fault ramp, 0 to 1, linear over rampSec, then held. Published only in diag.sim (ground truth); diagnostic reasoning uses channel evidence instead |
| V60, P60, I60 | 60 s window means of V, P and I (120 samples at 2 Hz) |
| V10, P10, I10 | 10 s window means (20 samples) |
| Ipk | Peak current in one 4.6 s stroke |
| PF60 | Fraction of samples in the last 60 s that are at or beyond the warning limit |
| HB300 | Mean spectrum bin amplitude above 300 Hz (bins 24 to 63) |
| PMR300 | Peak-to-median ratio of the bins above 300 Hz |
| 1X, 2X | Shaft frequency 24.7 Hz and its second harmonic (about 49 Hz) |
| Levels | L0 normal, L1 watch, L2 warning, L3 alarm, L4 critical, LS sensor or data suspect |

chunks.section: 2. Machine and Subsystem Overview > 2.1 Machine; 2.2 Lubrication circuit and sensor placement
chunks.text:
press-stamp-01 is a stamping press in a car plant (press shop, site vit-lab) [P]. The monitored subsystem is the press main drive and its pressure lubrication circuit [P]. The repository does not state the press make, model, tonnage, drive type, die or serial number [P]; none is assumed here.

Table 4. Machine data
| Field | Value | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| Machine type | press (typeCode 2) | [P] |
| Stroke time | 4.6 s (sim.cycleSec); about 13 strokes per minute | [P] |
| Working stroke | p = 0.38 to 0.60 of the stroke, that is 1.75 to 2.76 s into each 4.6 s cycle; load is a sin-squared pulse over this window | [P] / [D] seconds |
| Main motor speed | About 1480 rpm; shaft frequency 24.7 Hz (1X) | [P] |
| Gateway | ESP32 running cdo-edge-gateway with MACHINE_TYPE 2, firmware 1.0.0 in contract examples; stands in for a real controller reached by OPC UA or MTConnect | [P] |
| Make, model, tonnage, die, oil grade, bearing type | Not specified in repository | [P] |

A gear pump draws oil from the reservoir and pushes it through the lube filter to the main bearings. The pressure transducer is fitted downstream of the filter, in the distribution line that feeds the bearings [P]. Consequence: a blocked filter makes the pressure reading fall. A rising reading would point to a blockage in a nozzle or line after the transducer, which is a different fault and is not modelled [P].

Table 5. Flow path and what each sensor sees
| Element | Role | Sensor effect |
|---|---|---|
| Reservoir | Oil supply | Level not measured [P] |
| Gear pump | Produces flow; causes 1 Hz pulsation of about 0.12 bar [P] | Visible as pressure ripple |
| Lube filter | Removes particles | Clog lowers downstream pressure (P falls up to 45 percent) |
| Pressure transducer | Reads distribution line downstream of the filter | LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE |
| Main bearings | Carry the main shaft; need an oil film | Starved film raises vibration (BEARING_VIBRATION_RMS rises) |
| Main drive motor | Drives the press at about 1480 rpm | MAIN_MOTOR_CURRENT, friction raises it slightly |

chunks.section: 2. Machine and Subsystem Overview > 2.3 Sensor-to-component relationships
chunks.text:
Table 6. Channels, components and twin binding
| Channel | Component (binding label) | Planned component tag | Suggested mesh | Binding sensorType |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MAIN_MOTOR_CURRENT | Main drive motor | main_drive_motor | 090-stamping-press/0 | current |
| LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE | Lubrication unit | lube_filter, lubrication_unit | 090-stamping-press/1 | pressure |
| BEARING_VIBRATION_RMS | Main bearing housing | main_bearing_housing | 090-stamping-press/ram/ste el | vibration |
| BEARING_SPECTRUM | Same vibration seen by frequency | none | no binding (not bindable) | n/a |

The twin asset (Car Factory, Assembly Hall, car_factory.glb) contains a stamping press but no lubrication unit, drive motor or bearing housing as separate parts. An operator binds a mesh and the label says what it stands for. docs/demo-bindings.json records meshName null for all three channels, so no binding has been captured [P]. One mesh carries one sensor.

Causal link stated in the repository: a clogged filter starves the bearings, so ignoring it is how bearing damage eventually happens [P]. The channels are therefore related: LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE can lead BEARING_VIBRATION_RMS in a real degradation, although in the simulator the clogged-filter vibration rise is imposed directly.

Figure 1. Healthy MAIN_MOTOR_CURRENT and LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE from the noise-free equations [D]. The current pulse peaks near 150 A in the working stroke; the pressure ripple is 0.12 bar at 1 Hz.

chunks.section: 3. Operating States
chunks.text:
The repository models one running machine state. Other states exist in a real press and are listed as engineering reference [E] so the agent can reason about them without inventing numbers. The states are of three kinds: machine, gateway and fault.

Table 7. Operating states and expected telemetry
| State | Kind | Expected telemetry | Source / tag |
|---|---|---|---|
| Running, outside working stroke | Machine | I about 88 A with 4 A ripple; P 4.5 bar; V breathing 1.0 to 1.7 mm/s | [P] |
| Running, working stroke (p 0.38 to 0.60) | Machine | I rises up to +62 A (peaks about 150 A); V swells (structural energy 62.5 to 150 Hz); P unchanged | [P] |
| Stopped / main motor off | Machine | I near 0 A, V near 0 mm/s, P falls (pump stops) [E]. Not modelled, so do not compare with the healthy band | [E] |
| Start-up and warm-up | Machine | Inrush current above running level, P builds up within seconds, cold-oil pressure above normal [E] | [E] |
| Idle / slide stopped, motor running | Machine | I at idle level about 88 A [P]; no working-stroke pulse (not modelled as a separate state) | [P] / [E] |
| Die change, setup, jog | Machine | Not modelled. Suppress diagnosis; load and vibration unrepresentative [E] | [E] |
| Gateway online, status online | Gateway | telemetry every 500 ms, spectrum every 2 s, synced true | [P] |
| Stale | Gateway | No telemetry for max(5 s, 4 x intervalMs): 5 s at the default interval | [P] |
| Offline | Gateway | status offline (Last Will about 15 s after power loss) | [P] |
| Rebooted | Gateway | New bootId, seq back at 0; simulated fault cleared by cmd/reboot | [P] |
| Fault ramp (NORMAL, CLOGGED_FILTER, BEARING_WEAR) | Fault | r rises linearly from 0 to 1 over rampSec then holds; NORMAL resets | [P] |

chunks.section: 3. Operating States > 3.1 State rules used by the diagnosis; 3.2 Gateway health as a precondition
chunks.text:
• IF status is not online or the device is stale THEN do not diagnose mechanical faults; classify LS and

follow the data-path rules (Document 04, Section 21).

• IF the machine is stopped, in setup or in die change [E] THEN suppress limit-based diagnosis; the

repository has no state signal, so the agent must obtain it from the operator or controller.

• IF a cmd/scenario acknowledgement (ack ok true) was seen within the window THEN the

abnormality is an injected simulation event; record it as such.

• IF the machine runs normally THEN evaluate all channels with the limits in Section 6.

Table 8. Gateway health fields (diag, every 15 s)
| Field | Healthy expectation | Abnormal meaning |
|---|---|---|
| uptimeS | Increases | Reset to small value: reboot |
| rssi | Stable (example -58 dBm) | Falling: Wi-Fi quality, gaps in seq |
| heapFree / heapMin | Stable minimum over a 30 minute soak | Falling minimum: gateway memory leak |
| reset | Reason of last reset (example POWERON) | Unexpected reset reasons |
| wifiReconnects, mqttReconnects, restarts, publishFailures | Low and stable | Rising: link or broker problem; data gaps |
| tls, insecure | tls true, insecure false in the contract example | insecure true: not a production-grade link |

chunks.section: 4. Measurement Definitions > 4.1 Scalar channels; 4.2 Spectrum
chunks.text:
Table 9. Channel catalog (firmware/catalog.json)
| # | Channel key | Label | Type | Unit | Min | Ma x | Decim als | warn | alarm |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | MAIN_MOTOR_CURRENT | Main motor current | current | A | 0 | 250 | 1 | warnHigh 175 | alarmHigh 195 |

chunks.section: 4. Measurement Definitions > 4.3 Sampling facts that affect interpretation
chunks.text:
Table 11. Sampling and timing
| Fact | Value | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Telemetry rate | 2 Hz (500 ms) | 9.2 samples per 4.6 s stroke; the sample phase relative to the stroke repeats every 5 strokes (23 s, 46 samples) [D] |
| Samples inside the working stroke | About 2 per stroke (1.01 s window) | A single 500 ms sample can miss the current peak; use the stroke peak over several strokes [D] |
| Current ripple | 4 A, eight cycles per stroke = 1.74 Hz | Above the 1 Hz Nyquist limit of a 2 Hz series: it aliases to about 0.26 Hz in the published samples [E] |
| Pump pulsation | 1 Hz | Exactly at the Nyquist limit: the sampled amplitude depends on the sample phase, so use 10 s means [E] |
| Persistence | One last sample per channel per second stored | History is served bucketed; 48 h TTL [P] |
| Timestamps | SNTP epoch ms; if synced false or off by more than 2 minutes the backend stamps its own receive time | Do not trust ts ordering when synced is false [P] |

chunks.section: 5. Normal Operating Signature > 5.1 Healthy spectrum signature
chunks.text:
The model is identical in the firmware (simulation.h) and in the JavaScript simulator (sim-models.mjs) [P]. p is the stroke phase and load the working-stroke pulse sin-squared(pi (p - 0.38) / 0.22) for 0.38 < p < 0.60.

Table 12. Healthy model equations [P] current = 88.0 + 62.0*load + 4.0*sin(16*pi*p) + 1.8*gaussian() [A] pressure = 4.5 + 0.12*sin(2*pi*t) + 0.03*gaussian() [bar] rms = sqrt(sum of squared spectrum bins) [mm/s]

Table 13. Healthy behaviour per channel
| Channel | Healthy behaviour | Observed 600 s (seed 1) | Margin to warning | Tag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MAIN_MOTOR_CURRENT | Idle about 88 A, 4 A ripple, 1.8 A noise, pulse up to +62 A in the working stroke | 79.4 to 152.4 A, mean 94.8 A | Peak 152.4 A against 175 A: 22.6 A (13 percent of the limit) | [P] / [D] |
| LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE | 4.5 bar, 0.12 bar pump pulsation at 1 Hz, 0.03 bar noise; single readings wander about 0.1 bar | 4.40 to 4.59 bar, mean 4.50 bar | Minimum 4.40 bar against 3.6 bar: 0.80 bar | [P] / [D] |
| BEARING_VIBRATION_RMS | Breathes with the stroke between about 1.0 and 1.7 mm/s, mean near 1.3 mm/s (model constant 1.31) | 1.18 to 1.72 mm/s, mean 1.31 mm/s | Peak 1.72 mm/s against 2.5 mm/s: 0.78 mm/s | [P] / [D] |
| Status | Always normal on all three channels over 600 s (asserted by test) | normal | Not applicable | [P] |

Table 14. Healthy BEARING_SPECTRUM features
| Feature | Frequency (bin) | Amplitude | Meaning | Tag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1X peak | 24.7 Hz (bin 2) | About 1.05 mm/s | Strongest bin; a test asserts the largest bin is bin 2 | [P] |
| 2X peak | About 49 Hz (bin 4) | About 0.45 mm/s | Second shaft harmonic | [P] |
| Stroke-rate band | Bins 0 and 1 | About 0.08 mm/s | Energy at the stroke rate | [P] |
| Structural impact energy | 62.5 to 150 Hz (bins 5 to 12) | 0.25 x (0.4 + 1.2 x load) mm/s | Swells during the working stroke | [P] |
| Quiet floor | All other bins | About 0.03 mm/s | Healthy HB300 = 0.030 mm/s | [P] / [D] |

Figure 2. Healthy spectrum (top) and the two fault shapes. The healthy peak is at 1X; the clogged filter adds a flat floor above 300 Hz; bearing wear adds a harmonic family at non-integer orders. Schematic [I].

chunks.section: 6. Threshold System > 6.1 Level model; 6.2 Master limits: Minimum, Normal, Watch, Warning, Alarm, Critical
chunks.text:
Three of the four levels below exist in the repository; two are added here. The platform classifies each sample as normal, warn or alarm [P]. This knowledge base adds a Watch level before warning and a Critical level beyond alarm, both [I], because a plain threshold alarm is not enough (Document 02).

Table 16. Levels
| Level | Name | Origin | Meaning | Typical response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L0 | Normal | [P] | Inside the healthy band | None |
| L1 | Watch | [I] | Feature has moved from baseline but no limit is reached | Trend, add to next planned inspection |
| L2 | Warning | [P] warn limits | Warn limit reached on the persistence rule | Investigate at next planned stop; lubrication first when mixed |
| L3 | Alarm | [P] alarm limits | Alarm limit reached on the persistence rule | Intervene this shift; plan the repair |
| L4 | Critical | [I] | Value beyond the alarm limit by a margin, or rapid progression | Stop in a controlled way and inspect |
| LS | Sensor / data suspect | [E] / [I] | Signal or data path implausible | Resolve data and sensor first; do not diagnose a mechanical fault |

Table 17. Master threshold table (evaluated on 10 s window means unless stated)
| Parameter | Minimum | Normal | Watch [I] | Warning [P] | Alarm [P] | Critical [I] | Unit | Action at warning or above |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MAIN_MOTOR_CURRENT, stroke peak Ipk | 0 (catalog); below 60 while cycling = LS [I] | 79 to 153 (sample band) [D] | above 160 | at or above 175 | at or above 195 | at or above 220 | A | Check drive and load; compare friction trend with V and P (Doc 03) |
| MAIN_MOTOR_CURRENT, 60 s mean I60 | 0 | 94.8 baseline, band 90 to 99 [I] | above 99.5 (1.05 x baseline) | not defined | not defined | not defined | A | Corroborating feature only: bearing wear raises it about 8 percent |
| LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE, P10 / P60 | 0 (catalog) | 4.40 to 4.59 sample; P60 4.35 to 4.65 [I] | P60 at or below 4.30 | at or below 3.6 | at or below 3.0 | at or below 2.5 | bar | Replace lube filter after confirming trend and spectrum shape |
| BEARING_VIBRATION_RMS, V10 | 0 (no low limit); flat zero = LS | 1.18 to 1.72 sample; V60 1.2 to 1.45 [D]/[I] | V60 at or above 1.50 | at or above 2.5 | at or above 4.0 | at or above 7.0 | mm/s | Check spectrum shape: broadband versus discrete lines |
| Spectrum HB300 | 0 | 0.030 healthy [D] | at or above 0.12 | 8 x healthy (0.24) [P] test | not defined | not defined | mm/s | Broadband floor means lubrication first |
| Spectrum PMR300 | not defined | Healthy value not specified in repository | not defined | above 3 with discrete lines = bearing family [P] test | not defined | not defined | ratio | Discrete lines mean bearing inspection |

The repository defines only the Warning and Alarm columns for the three scalar channels. Minimum is the catalog minimum. Watch and Critical are proposals [I]. Spectrum rows are feature tests taken from the repository's own test suite [P], not alarm limits.

chunks.section: 6. Threshold System > 6.3 Persistence, hysteresis and debounce
chunks.text:
Today's platform logic classifies each sample, reaching a limit counts as breached (>= for a high limit, <= for a low limit), alarm wins over warn, and there is no hysteresis, delay or latching [P]. A cyclic signal therefore flickers across a limit. The planned detector adds hysteresis (beyond the alarm limit for 10 s opens, back inside for 10 s clears), drift detection and a debounce of one open investigation per machine with a 10 minute cooldown [P] planned. This document adopts the same 10 s timing for every level.

Table 18. Open and clear rules per level [I]
| Channel | Warning opens | Warning clears | Alarm opens | Alarm clears | Critical opens |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MAIN_MOTOR_CURRENT | Ipk at or above 175 A in 2 of 3 strokes | Ipk below 170 A for 10 s | Ipk at or above 195 A in 2 of 3 strokes | Ipk below 190 A for 10 s | Any 10 s mean at or above 220 A, or a sample at or above 240 A |
| LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE | P10 at or below 3.6 bar for 10 s | P10 above 3.8 bar for 10 s | P10 at or below 3.0 bar for 10 s | P10 above 3.2 bar for 10 s | P10 at or below 2.5 bar for 10 s |
| BEARING_VIBRATION_RMS | V10 at or above 2.5 mm/s for 10 s | V10 below 2.3 mm/s for 10 s | V10 at or above 4.0 mm/s for 10 s | V10 below 3.7 mm/s for 10 s | V10 at or above 7.0 mm/s for 10 s |

Why a 10 s mean: the vibration RMS breathes with the 4.6 s stroke and the pressure pulsates at 1 Hz, so a 10 s window (about two strokes) averages both cycles. A per-sample rule would flicker, as the platform does for BEARING_WEAR at r = 0.6 to 0.8 (Section 15).

chunks.section: 7. Feature-Based Thresholds > 7.1 Feature definitions; 7.2 Severity index from the channels
chunks.text:
Limits on the raw channels alone miss a bearing that wears while RMS stays under 4.0 mm/s [P]. Features computed from windows, trend and spectrum shape catch it. The ratios below follow from the simulation equations [D]; the numeric bands are [I].

Table 20. Features
| Feature | Definition | Healthy value | Watch band [I] | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| V60 | Mean of BEARING_VIBRATION_RMS over 60 s | 1.31 mm/s | 1.50 to 2.49 mm/s | [D] |
| V ratio | V60 / 1.31 mm/s (the channel's own baseline) | 1.00 | 1.15 or more | [D] |
| P60 | Mean of LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE over 60 s | 4.50 bar | 4.30 down to 3.61 bar | [D] |
| P ratio | P60 / 4.50 bar | 1.00 | 0.955 or less | [D] |
| I60 / I ratio | Mean current over 60 s / 94.8 A | 94.8 A / 1.00 | 1.05 or more | [D] |
| Ipk | Maximum current in one 4.6 s stroke | About 150 A | Above 160 A | [D] |
| PF60 | Share of samples at or above 2.5 mm/s in 60 s | 0 percent | Above 0 percent | [D] |
| HB300 | Mean amplitude of bins 24 to 63 (300 to 787.5 Hz) | 0.030 mm/s | 0.12 mm/s or more | [P] test uses 8 x healthy |
| PMR300 | Peak divided by median of bins above 300 Hz | Not specified in repository | Below 2.5 flat, above 3 peaked | [P] tests |
| Defect lines | Amplitude at bins 7, 14, 21, 28, 35 relative to healthy | Healthy | At least 4 x healthy in each bin | [P] test |

Because the ramp r is hidden ground truth, the diagnosis estimates severity from the channels. For CLOGGED_FILTER: r from pressure = (4.50 - P60) / 2.03; r from vibration = (V60 - 1.31) / 3.68. For BEARING_WEAR: r from vibration = (V60 - 1.31) / 1.58; r from current = (I60 - 94.8) / 7.6. Agreement between the two estimates (within 0.15 [I]) supports the hypothesis [D].

| P60 | Mean of LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE over 60 s | 4.50 bar | 4.30 down to 3.61 bar | [D] |
| P ratio | P60 / 4.50 bar | 1.00 | 0.955 or less | [D] |
| I60 / I ratio | Mean current over 60 s / 94.8 A | 94.8 A / 1.00 | 1.05 or more | [D] |
| Ipk | Maximum current in one 4.6 s stroke | About 150 A | Above 160 A | [D] |
| PF60 | Share of samples at or above 2.5 mm/s in 60 s | 0 percent | Above 0 percent | [D] |
| HB300 | Mean amplitude of bins 24 to 63 (300 to 787.5 Hz) | 0.030 mm/s | 0.12 mm/s or more | [P] test uses 8 x healthy |
| PMR300 | Peak divided by median of bins above 300 Hz | Not specified in repository | Below 2.5 flat, above 3 peaked | [P] tests |
| Defect lines | Amplitude at bins 7, 14, 21, 28, 35 relative to healthy | Healthy | At least 4 x healthy in each bin | [P] test |

Because the ramp r is hidden ground truth, the diagnosis estimates severity from the channels. For CLOGGED_FILTER: r from pressure = (4.50 - P60) / 2.03; r from vibration = (V60 - 1.31) / 3.68. For BEARING_WEAR: r from vibration = (V60 - 1.31) / 1.58; r from current = (I60 - 94.8) / 7.6. Agreement between the two estimates (within 0.15 [I]) supports the hypothesis [D].

| Estimated r | CLOGGED: P60 (bar) | CLOGGED: V60 (mm/s) | CLOGGED: I60 (A) | BEARING: V60 (mm/s) | BEARING: I60 (A) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.00 | 4.50 | 1.31 | 94.8 | 1.31 | 94.8 |
| 0.10 | 4.30 | 1.68 | 95.1 | 1.47 | 95.6 |
| 0.20 | 4.09 | 2.05 | 95.4 | 1.63 | 96.3 |
| 0.30 | 3.89 | 2.41 | 95.7 | 1.78 | 97.1 |
| 0.40 | 3.69 | 2.78 | 95.9 | 1.94 | 97.8 |
| 0.50 | 3.49 | 3.15 | 96.2 | 2.10 | 98.6 |
| 0.60 | 3.29 | 3.52 | 96.5 | 2.26 | 99.4 |
| 0.70 | 3.08 | 3.89 | 96.8 | 2.42 | 100.1 |
| 0.80 | 2.88 | 4.25 | 97.1 | 2.57 | 100.9 |
| 0.90 | 2.68 | 4.62 | 97.4 | 2.73 | 101.6 |
| 1.00 | 2.48 | 4.99 | 97.6 | 2.89 | 102.4 |

The numbers come from the equations (pressure and current) and from a linear fit to the 600 s derived table (vibration, within about 0.05 mm/s of the tabulated means) [D].

chunks.section: 8. Lube Oil Pressure: Detailed Standards > 8.1 Interpretation of LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE; 8.2 Pressure notes
chunks.text:
Table 22. Pressure bands
| Band (P10 or P60) | Level | Typical meaning | Evidence to check | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4.35 to 4.65 bar | L0 | Healthy circuit, pump pulsation 0.12 bar | None | None |
| 4.30 to 3.61 bar (P60 at or below 4.30) | L1 | Early clog or a slow loss of pressure; V rises 3.68 mm/s per unit r | V60, HB300, spectrum floor | Trend; plan filter inspection |
| 3.6 to 3.01 bar | L2 | Filter clogged, r about 0.44 to 0.74 in the model | V above 2.5, broadband floor | Replace filter at next stop |
| 3.0 to 2.51 bar | L3 | Severe restriction, r about 0.74 to 0.99 | V above 4.0 mm/s | Replace filter this shift |
| 2.5 bar or lower | L4 | Oil starvation of the bearings likely | V over 4.5 mm/s, current rise | Controlled stop |
| Rising above the healthy band [E] | LS / other | Blockage after the transducer or a stuck relief valve: not modelled; a different fault [P] | Pressure above 5.0 bar with normal vibration | Inspect nozzles and lines |
| Flat value with no pulsation | LS | Transducer or channel fault: healthy P has 0.03 bar noise and 0.12 bar ripple [P] | Std dev near 0 | Check sensor and data path |
| Zero | LS | Pump stopped, sensor disconnected or decoding fault | Gateway and state | Check state first |

• Single readings wander by about 0.1 bar from pump pulsation, so never act on one reading; use

the hourly trend and window means [P].

• Pressure is independent of load (no term in the stroke phase), so a pressure change is not

explained by the working stroke [P].

• The pressure falls up to 45 percent at full severity: 4.5 to about 2.47 bar [P].

• Warning (3.6 bar) is reached at r of about 0.44 and alarm (3.0 bar) at r of about 0.74 [P].

chunks.section: 9. Bearing Vibration: Detailed Standards > 9.1 Interpretation of BEARING_VIBRATION_RMS
chunks.text:
Table 23. Vibration bands
| Band (V10 or V60) | Level | Typical meaning | Evidence to check | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0 to 1.7 mm/s (V60 1.2 to 1.45) | L0 | Healthy breathing with the stroke | None | None |
| V60 1.50 to 2.49 mm/s | L1 | Rising baseline; CLOGGED_FILTER r above 0.05 or BEARING_WEAR r above 0.12 | P60, spectrum shape, I60 | Trend; check pressure first |
| 2.5 to 3.99 mm/s | L2 | Both faults possible: clog at r about 0.33 to 0.74, bearing at r about 0.8 or more | Broadband versus discrete lines | Lubrication first; inspect at next stop |
| 4.0 to 6.99 mm/s | L3 | Alarm; only the clogged filter reaches it (about 5.0 mm/s at r = 1) | P60 below 3.0 bar | Filter swap now |
| 7.0 mm/s or more | L4 | Severe: no simulated fault reaches it; treat as real damage or sensor fault | Mount, cable, impact events | Controlled stop |
| Flat zero or saturated at 12 mm/s | LS | Sensor or decoding fault | Spectrum agreement with RMS | Check sensor |

BEARING_WEAR peaks at about 3.2 mm/s at full severity and never reaches the 4.0 mm/s alarm [P] (asserted by test). A worn bearing can therefore be badly damaged at level L2 or below. Use trend and shape, not the alarm.

chunks.section: 10. Motor Current: Detailed Standards > 10.1 Interpretation of MAIN_MOTOR_CURRENT
chunks.text:
Table 24. Current bands
| Band | Level | Typical meaning | Evidence to check | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ipk up to 153 A, I60 94.8 A | L0 | Healthy working stroke | None | None |
| Ipk 160 to 174 A or I60 above 99.5 A | L1 | Friction or load rise; bearing wear at r above 0.62 gives I60 of about 99.5 A | V60 and spectrum lines | Trend |
| Ipk 175 to 194 A | L2 | Overload or strong friction; neither simulated fault reaches it (max 164.1 A) | Die, process, drive | Check load and drive |
| Ipk 195 to 219 A | L3 | Heavy overload | Stroke profile, die setup | Reduce load; inspect |
| Ipk 220 A or more | L4 | Possible jam or short | Drive protection | Stop |
| I near 0 A with press cycling, or flat | LS | Current sensor or data fault; motor off | State | Check state and sensor |

Current is a weak, late and slow corroborating channel in this model: CLOGGED_FILTER raises it about 3 percent (to about 97.6 A mean) and BEARING_WEAR about 8 percent (to 102.3 A mean, maximum 164.1 A), and neither reaches the 175 A warning [P]. chunks.section: 11. Spectrum Standards
chunks.text:
Table 25. Spectrum bands and their use
| Band | Bins | Frequency | Healthy content | Fault content |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stroke rate | 0 to 1 | 0 to 12.5 Hz | About 0.08 mm/s | Not specifically modified |
| Shaft 1X | 2 | About 25 Hz | 1.05 mm/s peak | Sidebands of bearing lines at plus and minus 1X (24.7 Hz) |
| Shaft 2X | 4 | About 50 Hz | 0.45 mm/s | None |
| Structural band | 5 to 12 | 62.5 to 150 Hz | 0.25 x (0.4 + 1.2 x load) mm/s | Bearing lines at 88 and 175 Hz sit near or above it |
| Mid band | 13 to 23 | 162.5 to 287.5 Hz | About 0.03 mm/s | Bearing lines at 175, 263 Hz |
| High band (HB300) | 24 to 63 | 300 to 787.5 Hz | 0.030 mm/s floor | Clog: flat floor 0.28 to 0.75 mm/s; bearing: lines at 351 and 439 Hz |

Table 26. Bearing defect orders and bins [P] / [D]
| Order x 1X | Frequency (Hz) | Bin | Relative weight | Sidebands |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3.55 | 87.7 | 7 (87.5 Hz) | 1.00 | Plus and minus 1X at 0.4 of the carrier (about 2 bins, 25 Hz) |
| 7.1 | 175.4 | 14 (175 Hz) | 0.80 | Same |
| 10.65 | 263.1 | 21 (262.5 Hz) | 0.60 | Same |
| 14.2 | 350.7 | 28 (350 Hz) | 0.45 | Same |
| 17.75 | 438.4 | 35 (437.5 Hz) | 0.30 | Same |

The orders are non-integer multiples of the shaft frequency, which is the signature of a rolling-element outer-race defect [E]; the repository does not state the bearing type or designation [P]. A 12.5 Hz bin spans less than the 24.7 Hz sideband spacing, so the sidebands appear two bins either side [D].

Table 27. Spectrum feature tests from the repository [P]
| Test | Healthy | CLOGGED_FILTER | BEARING_WEAR |
|---|---|---|---|
| High-band mean above 300 Hz | 0.030 mm/s | More than 8 x healthy (above 0.24 mm/s); 0.283 at r = 0.25, 0.749 at r = 1 | Not a discriminator |
| Peak-to-median above 300 Hz | Not specified in repository | Below 2.5 (flat, no discrete family) | Above 3 (discrete peaks) |
| Defect bins 7, 14, 21, 28, 35 | Healthy amplitude | Not raised as a family | Each more than 4 x healthy |
| Largest bin | Bin 2 (1X) | Not required | Not required |

chunks.section: 12. Startup and Shutdown Behaviour
chunks.text:
The simulator has no start-up or shutdown state: after a boot or a cmd/reboot the model runs with r = 0 (NORMAL) at once, and the gateway publishes status online [P]. A real press has start-up and shutdown behaviour that the repository does not specify. The table is engineering reference [E] and must be replaced by plant data.

Table 28. Start-up and shutdown behaviour
| Phase | MAIN_MOTOR_CURRENT | LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE | BEARING_VIBRATION_RMS | Diagnostic treatment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gateway boot (simulator) | Model starts at normal | Model starts at normal | Model starts at normal | Wait for status online and synced true [P] |
| Motor start [E] | Inrush above running level for seconds | Rises as the pump fills the lines | Run-up transient through resonance | Suppress limit checks for the start-up window set by the plant |
| Warm-up [E] | Slightly higher friction with cold oil | Higher with cold, viscous oil | Slightly different | Compare with a warm baseline only after warm-up |
| Steady running | See Section 5 | See Section 5 | See Section 5 | Full diagnosis |
| Controlled shutdown [E] | Falls to zero | Falls as the pump stops; no alarm expected | Falls to near zero | Suppress low-pressure alarms when the motor is off |
| Power loss | status offline about 15 s later [P] | Last values retained until stale | Same | Classify as data state, not a fault |

IF the main motor is off THEN pressure below 3.0 bar is not a lubrication alarm. The repository has no motor-run signal, so the agent must obtain the machine state from outside the three channels (current near zero is a hint, not proof) [E].

chunks.section: 13. Load-Dependent Behaviour
chunks.text:
Table 29. Dependence of each channel on load (stroke phase)
| Channel | Depends on load? | Behaviour | Evaluation rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| MAIN_MOTOR_CURRENT | Yes, strongly | +62 A sin-squared pulse over p 0.38 to 0.60; ripple 4 A across the stroke | Evaluate stroke peak Ipk and the 60 s mean separately; compare the idle level to 88 A |
| BEARING_VIBRATION_RMS | Yes, moderately | Breathes 1.0 to 1.7 mm/s; structural energy 62.5 to 150 Hz swells with load | Use V60 and compare against the healthy breathing band; do not judge one stroke peak |
| LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE | No | 4.5 bar plus 1 Hz pulsation | Evaluate directly on P10 and P60 |
| BEARING_SPECTRUM | Partly | Impact band varies with load; 1X and 2X stable | Use the 2 s spectrum; bins above 300 Hz are load independent in the healthy model |

Table 30. Stroke phase table for the 4.6 s cycle [P] / [D]
| Phase p | Time in stroke (s) | Load | Expected current (noise-free) | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.00 to 0.38 | 0 to 1.75 | 0 | 88 A plus 4 A ripple | Non-working part |
| 0.38 to 0.49 | 1.75 to 2.25 | Rising | Up to 150 A | Pulse rises |
| 0.49 | 2.25 | 1.0 | About 150 A (88 + 62) | Peak load |
| 0.49 to 0.60 | 2.25 to 2.76 | Falling | Down to 88 A | Pulse falls |
| 0.60 to 1.00 | 2.76 to 4.6 | 0 | 88 A plus ripple | Return |

IF the current peak per stroke exceeds 160 A while V60 and P60 are healthy THEN suspect a process or die load change (Document 03 rule for load) rather than a lubrication fault [E].

chunks.section: 14. Environmental Influences
chunks.text:
The repository does not model ambient or oil temperature, supply voltage, die or material changes, or foundation vibration, and it gives no environmental limits [P]. The influences below are engineering reference [E]; they explain why a baseline must be recomputed and why a reading can move without a fault.

Table 31. Influences and their expected effect
| Influence | Channel affected | Expected effect | Treatment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Oil temperature or viscosity | LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE | Colder oil raises pressure; hot thin oil lowers it | Compare to the same operating temperature; temperature is not measured |
| Ambient temperature | P, I | Moves oil temperature and friction slightly | Seasonal baseline update |
| Supply voltage variation | I | Current changes for the same load | Check supply if I moves without V or P |
| Die weight, material or blank thickness | I | Changes the working-stroke pulse and the stroke peak | Re-baseline after a die change |
| Neighbouring machine or foundation vibration | V | Adds broadband or line energy | Compare with the stopped-machine reading |
| Electrical noise near the vibration cable | V, spectrum | Adds spikes or mains-frequency lines | Check shielding |
| Oil contamination | P | Faster filter clogging; repository: minutes to days depending on oil cleanliness [P] | Oil analysis |
| Network quality | All | Gaps in seq, stale device | Data-path rules |

chunks.section: 15. Normal Transients and False Alarms
chunks.text:
Table 32. Normal transients versus abnormal behaviour
| Observation | Normal transient? | Why | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| Single current sample near 150 A | Yes | Working-stroke pulse peaks at 88 + 62 = 150 A [P] | Judge Ipk against 175 A |
| Pressure reading 0.1 bar from 4.5 | Yes | Pump pulsation 0.12 bar at 1 Hz [P] | Use window means |
| Vibration RMS between 1.0 and 1.7 mm/s | Yes | Breathes with the stroke [P] | Use V60 |
| Vibration single sample at 2.5 mm/s while V60 is 1.3 | Unlikely in the healthy model (max 1.72 mm/s) | Healthy 600 s maximum 1.72 mm/s [D] | Treat as spike or data error; confirm with the next spectrum |
| V flickers across 2.5 mm/s | Abnormal | BEARING_WEAR at r about 0.6 to 0.8 flickers across warn [P] | Use PF60 and V60 |

chunks.section: 17. Abnormal Conditions and Interpretation > 17.1 Reasoning rules
chunks.text:
Table 36. Abnormal conditions and first interpretation
| Condition | Threshold evidence | Interpretation | Level | Next step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P10 at or below 3.6 bar and V60 at or above 2.5 mm/s | Both | CLOGGED_FILTER likely (Document 02 F01) | L2 | Confirm broadband spectrum; replace filter |
| P10 at or below 3.0 bar and V60 at or above 4.0 mm/s | Both alarm | CLOGGED_FILTER severe | L3 | Replace filter now; inspect bearings after |
| V60 rising from 1.3 toward 3 mm/s with P normal | No limit reached | BEARING_WEAR drift [P] | L1 to L2 | Handheld analyser; plan replacement |
| V60 at or above 2.5 mm/s, P normal, discrete lines | Warn | BEARING_WEAR | L2 | Plan bearing inspection at next stop |
| Ipk at or above 175 A with V60 and P60 normal | Warn on current | Load or drive, not a modelled fault | L2 | Check die, process, drive |
| V10 at or above 7.0 mm/s | Critical | Severe fault or sensor fault | L4 | Stop; inspect |
| P rising above healthy | Not defined | Blockage after the transducer [P] (not modelled) | LS / other | Inspect nozzles and lines |
| Implausible values or gaps | None | Sensor or data fault | LS | Resolve data path |

• IF pressure is normal and the spectrum shows discrete peaks THEN it is not a filter problem; use

the bearing procedure [P].

• IF the evidence is mixed THEN check the lubrication first: a clogged filter is the cheap fault and it

causes bearing damage if left [P].

• IF V60 climbs steadily from 1.3 toward 3 mm/s THEN treat it as drift whatever the limit says [P].

• IF P60 falls and HB300 rises together THEN lubrication starvation is the leading hypothesis [P] [D].

chunks.section: 1. Purpose and Method > 1.1 What this document contains; 1.2 Evidence vector used in every profile
chunks.text:
The repository models exactly two faults for press-stamp-01: CLOGGED_FILTER and BEARING_WEAR [P]. They share a symptom, high bearing vibration, and differ in evidence. This document explains how to tell them apart from the telemetry and adds engineering-reference failure modes (F03 to F16) so that the diagnosis can say "a different fault" when the evidence does not fit. The repository states that no other press failure mode and no combination of the two faults is modelled [P]; every profile for F03 to F16 is therefore [E] and its numbers, where given, are [I].

RULE: a fault name from the repository (CLOGGED_FILTER, BEARING_WEAR) is a simulation scenario. The scenario label is hidden ground truth (diag.sim) and must not be used as evidence; reason from channel evidence [P].

Table 1. Evidence vector
| Evidence | Symbol | Healthy | Source of the value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lube oil pressure, 60 s mean | P60 | 4.50 bar | LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE [P] |
| Vibration RMS, 60 s mean | V60 | 1.31 mm/s | BEARING_VIBRATION_RMS [P] |
| Motor current, 60 s mean and stroke peak | I60, Ipk | 94.8 A, about 150 A | MAIN_MOTOR_CURRENT [P] / [D] |
| Mean bin amplitude above 300 Hz | HB300 | 0.030 mm/s | BEARING_SPECTRUM [P] |

[Machine: press-stamp-01 (Stamping press 01) | Document 02: Failure Modes and Fault Signatures | Section: 1. Purpose and Method > 1.1 What this document contains; 1.2 Evidence vector used in every profile]
The repository models exactly two faults for press-stamp-01: CLOGGED_FILTER and BEARING_WEAR [P]. They share a symptom, high bearing vibration, and differ in evidence. This document explains how to tell them apart from the telemetry and adds engineering-reference failure modes (F03 to F16) so that the diagnosis can say "a different fault" when the evidence does not fit. The repository states that no other press failure mode and no combination of the two faults is modelled [P]; every profile for F03 to F16 is therefore [E] and its numbers, where given, are [I].

RULE: a fault name from the repository (CLOGGED_FILTER, BEARING_WEAR) is a simulation scenario. The scenario label is hidden ground truth (diag.sim) and must not be used as evidence; reason from channel evidence [P].

| Bearing defect lines (bins 7, 14, 21, 28, 35) | DL | Healthy amplitude | tests [P] |

chunks.section: 2. Failure-Mode Classification > 2.1 Reading the classification
chunks.text:
• F01 and F02 carry [P] numerical signatures; use them as the reference patterns.

• F03 to F06 are lubrication faults that move LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE; F01 differs by being the only one

whose pressure fall is accompanied by a flat broadband floor in the spectrum [E].

• F08 to F11 move current or the spectrum without a pressure fall.

• F12 to F15 are measurement or data faults and are always checked first (Document 03, step 2).

• F16 is not modelled: the agent must treat mixed evidence as lubrication first [P].

chunks.section: 3. Signature Consistency Ratios
chunks.text:
Because the simulated faults follow fixed equations, the telemetry of each fault obeys relations that a measurement fault, a different physical fault or a mix of faults does not. The relations below are [D]; they are tested as consistency checks in Document 03.

Table 3. Equations and the relations they imply [P] / [D]
| Quantity | CLOGGED_FILTER | BEARING_WEAR |
|---|---|---|
| Pressure | P = 4.5 x (1 - 0.45 r) + 0.06 r x noise: falls to 2.47 bar | Unchanged |
| Current | I x (1 + 0.03 r): mean 94.8 to 97.6 A | I x (1 + 0.08 r): mean 94.8 to 102.3 A (max 164.1 A) |
| Vibration | Floor above 300 Hz: RMS scales by (1 + 2.75 r); V60 about 1.31 + 3.68 r (4.98 at r = 1) | Lines at 3.55 to 17.75 x 1X with sidebands: V60 about 1.31 + 1.58 r (2.89 at r = 1) |
| Spectrum shape | Flat floor, 18 percent jitter per bin, no discrete lines | Five lines with weights 1.0, 0.8, 0.6, 0.45, 0.3 and sidebands at 0.4 of the carrier |
| Delta V60 / Delta P60 | -1.8 mm/s per bar | Undefined |
| Delta I60 / Delta V60 | 0.77 A per mm/s | 4.8 A per mm/s |
| HB300 | 0.030 to 0.749 mm/s | Small change; lines at 351 and 439 Hz |
| Alarm reached at full severity | Yes: V above 4.0 mm/s and P below 3.0 bar | No: V peaks about 3.2 mm/s; P normal |

Table 4. Consistency checks for the diagnosis [I]
| Check | Passes for | Fails means |
|---|---|---|
| Estimated r from P60 within 0.15 of r from V60 (clog formulae) | CLOGGED_FILTER | Not a pure clog: pressure sensor fault, other lubrication fault or mixed |
| Estimated r from V60 within 0.15 of r from I60 (bearing formulae) | BEARING_WEAR | Not a pure bearing fault: process or drive fault, current sensor fault |
| RMS equals the square root of the summed squared spectrum bins | Any valid data | Decoding or data fault (F13, F15) |
| V60 rise matches HB300 rise (broadband) for a clog | CLOGGED_FILTER | Vibration sensor fault or another cause |

Figure 1. Progression of vibration, pressure and current means against the fault ramp r for the two simulated faults (derived table [D]); dashed lines are the warn and alarm limits [P].

chunks.section: 4. Detailed Fault Profiles > 4.1 F01 CLOGGED_FILTER: clogged lubrication filter
chunks.text:
Table 5. F01 profile
| Attribute | Description |
|---|---|
| Fault | CLOGGED_FILTER (clogged lube filter) |
| Affected component | Lube filter in the lubrication unit; consequence at the main bearing housing |
| Physical mechanism | Filter media loads with debris; the pressure transducer sits downstream of the filter, so the reading falls. A starved bearing loses its oil film and vibration rises [P] |
| Sensor behaviour | P falls up to 45 percent (4.5 to about 2.47 bar). V rises, 4.98 mm/s mean at r = 1. Current up about 3 percent. Spectrum gains a broadband floor above 300 Hz [P] |
| Expected telemetry pattern | Smooth monotonic fall of P60 with a simultaneous rise of V60 and HB300; no discrete lines; I60 rises about 2.8 A per unit r [D] |
| Thresholds crossed | V samples reach warn from r about 0.25; V60 reaches 2.5 at r about 0.33; P60 reaches 3.6 bar at r about 0.44; P60 3.0 bar and V60 4.0 mm/s at r about 0.74 [P] / [D] |
| Severity | Medium when found early (a short cartridge swap); High if ignored (bearing damage, unplanned stop of days) [P] |
| Likely causes | Dirty oil, filter at end of life, wrong or poor cartridge, contamination ingress; develops over minutes to days depending on oil cleanliness [P] |
| Symptoms | Rising bearing noise, pressure gauge reading low (if fitted), warning on vibration and pressure [E] |
| Alternative explanations | Pump wear (F03), leak (F04), relief valve (F06), transducer fault (F12), cold-oil or hot-oil effect (F07) [E] |
| Differentiating evidence | Pressure falls while the spectrum floor is flat and broadband above 300 Hz (PMR300 below 2.5) and current rises only about 3 percent [P] |
| Inspection requirements | Confirm P trend over the last hour, spectrum shape and that other channels are normal; check filter cartridge [P] |
| Corrective action | Replace the filter cartridge (a short task, in the order of minutes); follow the OEM procedure with lock-out and tag-out and relieve line pressure [P] |
| Expected post-repair behaviour | P returns to about 4.5 bar and V settles to about 1.3 mm/s; HB300 back to about 0.03 mm/s [P] |
| Provenance | [P] runbook and equations; severity and symptoms [E] |

chunks.section: 4. Detailed Fault Profiles > 4.2 F02 BEARING_WEAR: main bearing outer-race defect
chunks.text:
Table 6. F02 profile
| Attribute | Description |
|---|---|
| Fault | BEARING_WEAR (main bearing outer-race defect) |
| Affected component | Main bearing housing; main drive motor loading is secondary |
| Physical mechanism | A defect in the outer race produces repetitive impacts at non-integer multiples of the shaft frequency; narrow lines carry the energy, so overall RMS stays modest [P] |
| Sensor behaviour | V rises slowly to about 2.9 mm/s mean (peaks about 3.2 mm/s); current up about 8 percent; pressure unchanged [P] |
| Expected telemetry pattern | Discrete lines at about 88, 175, 263, 351 and 439 Hz (bins 7, 14, 21, 28, 35) with sidebands at plus and minus 1X; PMR300 above 3; P normal [P] / [D] |
| Thresholds crossed | V samples flicker over 2.5 mm/s from r about 0.6 and are over it most of the time from r about 0.8; the 4.0 mm/s alarm is never reached; the current warn limit is never reached (max 164.1 A) [P] / [D] |
| Severity | High: planned change costs hours, a bearing that fails in service costs days [P] |
| Likely causes | Fatigue, lubricant starvation or contamination history, misalignment, overload, installation damage [E] |
| Symptoms | Rising noise at the drive end, slight warming [E] |
| Alternative explanations | Imbalance or misalignment (F10, integer orders), looseness (F11), process load (F09), vibration sensor fault (F13) [E] |
| Differentiating evidence | Pressure normal; discrete family at non-integer orders (3.55, 7.1, 10.65, 14.2, 17.75); defect bins each more than 4 times healthy; I60 up about 4.8 A per mm/s of V rise [P] / [D] |
| Inspection requirements | Schedule an inspection at the next planned stop and confirm the defect frequencies with a handheld analyser [P] |
| Corrective action | Plan a bearing replacement; use the specified bearings and fits; lock-out and tag-out before opening the main drive [P] |
| Expected post-repair behaviour | V settles to about 1.3 mm/s; the harmonic family disappears; current returns to about 94.8 A mean [P] / [D] |
| Provenance | [P] runbook, equations and tests; symptoms and causes [E] |

chunks.text:
Table 7. F03 profile
| Attribute | Description |

| Fault | Lube pump wear or failure |
| Affected component | Gear pump in the lubrication unit |
| Physical mechanism | Internal wear lowers delivery; worn or failed gears reduce pressure and change the 1 Hz pulsation |
| Sensor behaviour | P falls, pulsation amplitude and shape change; V rises later through starvation; I may fall slightly with the pump load |
| Expected telemetry pattern | P60 falls with irregular or reduced ripple; no HB300 rise early; V60 rises only after the pressure has fallen |
| Thresholds crossed | P crosses 3.6 and 3.0 bar; V follows [I] |
| Severity | High (loss of lubrication) |
| Likely causes | Wear, cavitation, coupling failure, low oil level |
| Symptoms | Low pressure, pump noise [E] |
| Alternative explanations | Clogged filter (F01), leak (F04), relief valve (F06) |
| Differentiating evidence | Pressure fall without an early broadband floor; ripple amplitude below 0.12 bar or irregular; filter swap does not restore pressure |
| Inspection requirements | Pump drive and coupling, delivery test, suction line, filter delta-P with a gauge (not specified in repository) |
| Corrective action | Repair or replace the pump per OEM; check suction |
| Expected post-repair behaviour | Ripple 0.12 bar at 1 Hz and P about 4.5 bar return |
| Provenance | [E]; numbers [I] |

| Attribute | Description |

| Expected post-repair behaviour | Stable P about 4.5 bar with 0.03 bar noise |

chunks.section: 4. Detailed Fault Profiles > 4.5 F05 Blocked nozzle or line after the transducer; 4.6 F06 Relief valve stuck or setpoint drift
chunks.text:
Table 9. F05 profile
| Attribute | Description |
|---|---|
| Fault | Blocked nozzle or line after the transducer |
| Affected component | Distribution line or nozzle downstream of LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE sensor |
| Physical mechanism | A restriction after the transducer raises the pressure the transducer sees while less oil reaches the bearing |
| Sensor behaviour | P rises above the healthy band; V may rise later; spectrum like starvation if flow is lost |
| Expected telemetry pattern | P60 above 4.65 bar and rising, V60 rising slowly; the opposite direction to F01 |
| Thresholds crossed | No project high limit; proposed watch above 5.0 bar [I] |
| Severity | Medium to high |
| Likely causes | Contaminated oil, collapsed hose, blocked nozzle |
| Symptoms | Bearing noise despite apparently good pressure [E] |
| Alternative explanations | Relief valve stuck closed (F06), cold oil (F07), transducer offset (F12) |
| Differentiating evidence | P rises while V rises; the repository calls this a different fault from the clog [P] |
| Inspection requirements | Nozzles and lines after the transducer |
| Corrective action | Clear or replace the restricted element |
| Expected post-repair behaviour | P returns to about 4.5 bar and V to about 1.3 mm/s |
| Provenance | [P] named; signature [E] |

Table 10. F06 profile
| Attribute | Description |
|---|---|
| Fault | Relief valve stuck or setpoint drift |
| Affected component | Pressure relief valve in the lubrication unit |
| Physical mechanism | A valve stuck open dumps oil and holds pressure low; stuck closed raises pressure |
| Sensor behaviour | P steps to a new steady level; V and spectrum unchanged at first |
| Expected telemetry pattern | Step change in P with no gradual ramp and no change in spectrum shape |
| Thresholds crossed | P below 3.6 bar (open) or above 5.0 bar (closed) [I] |
| Severity | Medium |
| Likely causes | Contamination, spring fatigue, wrong setting |
| Symptoms | Pressure reading off the usual value [E] |
| Alternative explanations | Pump wear (F03), clogged filter (F01) |
| Differentiating evidence | Step-like change rather than a ramp; no broadband floor; filter swap ineffective |
| Inspection requirements | Valve and its setting |
| Corrective action | Clean, reset or replace the valve per OEM |
| Expected post-repair behaviour | P returns to about 4.5 bar |
| Provenance | [E]; numbers [I] |

chunks.section: 4. Detailed Fault Profiles > 4.7 F07 Oil temperature or viscosity effect; 4.8 F08 Main drive motor or supply fault
chunks.text:
Table 11. F07 profile
| Attribute | Description |
|---|---|
| Fault | Oil temperature or viscosity effect |
| Affected component | Oil in the circuit |
| Physical mechanism | Viscosity changes with temperature, shifting the pressure at the same flow |
| Sensor behaviour | P follows a slow temperature cycle; V and spectrum unchanged |
| Expected telemetry pattern | Slow periodic P variation with the ambient or warm-up cycle; no V rise |
| Thresholds crossed | Possible low-pressure warn on a cold start [I] |
| Severity | Low |
| Likely causes | Cold start, hot ambient, cooler fault |
| Symptoms | Pressure differing between morning and afternoon [E] |
| Alternative explanations | Clogged filter (F01), pump wear (F03) |
| Differentiating evidence | Reversible with temperature; V unchanged; HB300 unchanged |
| Inspection requirements | Oil temperature (not measured in the repository) |
| Corrective action | No repair if within normal swing; fix cooler if hot |
| Expected post-repair behaviour | P returns when temperature normalises |
| Provenance | [E]; numbers [I] |

Table 12. F08 profile
| Attribute | Description |
|---|---|
| Fault | Main drive motor or supply fault |
| Affected component | Main drive motor and its supply |
| Physical mechanism | Winding, supply imbalance or drive faults change the current waveform and add electromagnetic vibration |
| Sensor behaviour | I rises or the idle level shifts; ripple changes; spectrum shows lines at twice the supply frequency and 1X sidebands; P normal |
| Expected telemetry pattern | I60 up by more than 8 percent with V60 rising; lines near 100 Hz (50 Hz supply) [E] |
| Thresholds crossed | I crosses 175 A at advanced stage [I] |
| Severity | High |
| Likely causes | Winding degradation, phase imbalance, drive tuning |
| Symptoms | Motor heating, trips [E] |
| Alternative explanations | Process load (F09), bearing wear (F02) |
| Differentiating evidence | Current rises disproportionately to V (more than 4.8 A per mm/s) and line-frequency lines appear |
| Inspection requirements | Insulation test, supply balance, drive parameters |
| Corrective action | Repair or replace motor or correct the supply |
| Expected post-repair behaviour | I back to 94.8 A mean |
| Provenance | [E]; numbers [I] |

chunks.text:

| Attribute | Description |
|---|---|

| Provenance | [E]; limits [P] |

| Expected telemetry pattern | Bin 2 and bin 4 grow, no non-integer family, no broadband floor |
| Thresholds crossed | V60 may reach 2.5 mm/s [I] |
| Severity | Medium |

| Inspection requirements | Coupling, alignment, balance |
| Corrective action | Re-align or balance |
| Expected post-repair behaviour | 1X amplitude about 1.05 mm/s |
| Provenance | [E]; numbers [I] |

chunks.section: 7. Discrimination of the Two Simulated Faults > 7.1 Discrimination table; 7.2 Quantitative thresholds for differentiation; 7.3 Discriminator matrix across the fault library
chunks.text:
Table 28. Evidence that separates CLOGGED_FILTER from BEARING_WEAR (both runbooks) [P]
| Evidence | Clogged lube filter | Bearing wear |
|---|---|---|
| Lube oil pressure | Falls | Normal |
| Spectrum above 300 Hz | Broadband floor, no discrete peaks | Harmonic family at fixed multiples of 1X, with sidebands |
| Motor current | Up about 3 percent | Up about 8 percent |
| Vibration RMS at full severity | Above alarm (about 5 mm/s) | Below alarm (peaks about 3.2 mm/s) |
| Cheapest next step | Replace the filter cartridge | Plan a bearing replacement |

Table 29. Differentiating bands [D] / [I]
| Quantity | Points to F01 | Points to F02 | Ambiguous |
|---|---|---|---|
| P60 | At or below 4.30 bar | 4.45 to 4.55 bar | 4.30 to 4.45 bar |
| PMR300 | Below 2.5 | Above 3 | 2.5 to 3 |
| HB300 | At or above 0.24 mm/s | Near 0.03 to 0.10 mm/s | 0.10 to 0.24 mm/s |
| Delta I60 / Delta V60 | About 0.8 A per mm/s | About 4.8 A per mm/s | 1.5 to 3.5 A per mm/s |
| V60 above 4.0 mm/s | Yes | Never | Not applicable |
| Defect bins at least 4 x healthy | No | Yes (all five) | Some only |

Codes: U up, D down, S same as healthy, F flat or implausible, P present, A absent, ? depends. Faults F03 to F16 are [E].

chunks.section: 8. Pattern-to-Fault Mapping
chunks.text:
Table 31. Sensor pattern, possible fault, evidence, severity, inspection and action
| Sensor pattern | Possible fault | Evidence | Severity | Inspection | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P60 falling, V60 rising, flat high-band floor | F01 CLOGGED_FILTER | HB300 up, PMR300 below 2.5, I60 up 3 percent | Medium to high | Filter cartridge, line pressure | Replace cartridge |
| V60 rising slowly, P normal, discrete lines | F02 BEARING_WEAR | Lines at 88, 175, 263, 351, 439 Hz; I60 up about 8 percent | High | Handheld analyser at the housing | Plan bearing change |
| V60 at 2.5 to 3.5 mm/s, P normal, no lines | F10 or F11 or F13 | Integer orders or RMS mismatch | Medium | Alignment, fasteners, sensor mount | Correct |
| P low, V normal | F12, F03, F04 or F06 | No broadband floor, no V rise | Medium | Transducer then pump and leak | Verify sensor first |
| P high | F05 or F06 | P above 5.0 bar [I] | Medium | Nozzles and lines, relief valve | Clear restriction |
| Ipk at or above 175 A, idle level normal | F09 | Increase only in working stroke | Medium | Die, material | Correct setup |
| I60 up more than 8 percent, line-frequency lines | F08 | I per mm/s above 4.8 A | High | Motor and supply | Repair motor |
| Pressure low and discrete lines both | F16 | Mixed evidence | High | Lubrication first, then bearing | Filter, then plan bearing |
| Flat or implausible channel | F12, F13, F14 | No cross-channel confirmation | Low (data) | Sensor and wiring | Repair sensor |

chunks.section: 11. Alternative Explanations and Inspection Requirements
chunks.text:
Table 35. Alternatives that must be excluded before confirming a fault
| Leading hypothesis | Alternative | How to exclude | Inspection that confirms |
|---|---|---|---|
| F01 | F03 pump wear | Pulsation 0.12 bar present and a flat broadband floor; fall consistent with delta V / delta P of -1.8 | Filter cartridge appearance; pressure after replacement |
| F01 | F12 transducer | V60 and HB300 confirm the fall | Reference gauge reading |
| F02 | F10 or F11 | Lines at non-integer orders only | Handheld analyser order analysis |
| F02 | F13 sensor | RMS equals spectrum; current moves with V | Re-mount sensor and compare |
| F02 | F01 early | P60 at or above 4.45 bar; HB300 below 0.10 mm/s | Pressure trend over the last hour |
| F09 | F08 | Idle level unchanged | Current at idle and in stroke |
| F05 | F12 | V rising too | Reference gauge, nozzle check |
| F16 | F01 plus noise | Lines above floor, PMR300 between 2.5 and 3 | Filter then re-check spectrum |

Table 36. Inspection requirements by fault
| Fault | Inspection | Tool | Pass criterion [I] |
|---|---|---|---|
| F01 | Filter cartridge, line pressure | OEM service tools | Clean cartridge; pressure returns to 4.5 bar |
| F02 | Bearing frequencies, housing condition | Handheld analyser | No lines at the defect orders; V 1.3 mm/s |
| F03 to F04 | Pump, reservoir level, leaks | OEM tools | Level correct, no leaks |
| F08 | Insulation and supply balance | Electrical test set | Within OEM limits |
| F12 to F14 | Sensor against a reference | Reference gauge, clamp meter, analyser | Agrees within tolerance |

| F02 | F10 or F11 | Lines at non-integer orders only | Handheld analyser order analysis |
| F02 | F13 sensor | RMS equals spectrum; current moves with V | Re-mount sensor and compare |
| F02 | F01 early | P60 at or above 4.45 bar; HB300 below 0.10 mm/s | Pressure trend over the last hour |
| F09 | F08 | Idle level unchanged | Current at idle and in stroke |
| F05 | F12 | V rising too | Reference gauge, nozzle check |
| F16 | F01 plus noise | Lines above floor, PMR300 between 2.5 and 3 | Filter then re-check spectrum |

| Fault | Inspection | Tool | Pass criterion [I] |
|---|---|---|---|
| F01 | Filter cartridge, line pressure | OEM service tools | Clean cartridge; pressure returns to 4.5 bar |
| F02 | Bearing frequencies, housing condition | Handheld analyser | No lines at the defect orders; V 1.3 mm/s |
| F03 to F04 | Pump, reservoir level, leaks | OEM tools | Level correct, no leaks |
| F08 | Insulation and supply balance | Electrical test set | Within OEM limits |
| F12 to F14 | Sensor against a reference | Reference gauge, clamp meter, analyser | Agrees within tolerance |

chunks.section: 12. Summary, Safety, References and Revision > 12.1 Diagnostic summary; 12.2 Key thresholds; 12.3 Safety and escalation notes; 12.4 References and engineering basis; 12.5 Revision notes
chunks.text:
• Two simulated faults, one shared symptom (high bearing vibration): pressure, spectrum shape,

current ratio and alarm behaviour tell them apart [P].

• CLOGGED_FILTER: P60 falls to about 2.47 bar, V60 reaches about 5 mm/s, flat high-band floor, I up

3 percent.

• BEARING_WEAR: P normal, V60 reaches about 2.9 mm/s (peaks 3.2), discrete family at 88, 175,

263, 351, 439 Hz, I up 8 percent, alarm never reached.

• Mixed evidence means lubrication first [P]. F03 to F16 are engineering reference [E]; numbers [I].

Table 37. Key thresholds for fault recognition
| Quantity | Value | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| V warn / alarm | 2.5 / 4.0 mm/s | [P] |
| P warn / alarm | 3.6 / 3.0 bar | [P] |
| I warn / alarm | 175 / 195 A | [P] |
| HB300 test | above 0.24 mm/s (8 x healthy) | [P] test |
| PMR300 | below 2.5 flat; above 3 peaked | [P] tests |
| Defect bins | 7, 14, 21, 28, 35 at least 4 x healthy | [P] test |
| Critical (V, P, I) | 7.0 mm/s, 2.5 bar, 220 A | [I] |

chunks.section: 1. Prerequisites and Feature Definitions > 1.1 Inputs; 1.2 Feature computation
chunks.text:
Table 1. Inputs to the procedure
| Input | Source | Rate | Tag |
|---|---|---|---|
| MAIN_MOTOR_CURRENT, LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE, BEARING_VIBRATION_RMS | telemetry topic (m object) | 500 ms | [P] |
| BEARING_SPECTRUM, 64 bins | spectrum topic | 2000 ms | [P] |
| status, seq, ts, synced | status, telemetry | each message | [P] |
| diag (uptimeS, rssi, heap, reconnects) | diag topic | 15 s | [P] |
| ack of cmd/scenario | ack topic | on command | [P] |
| Machine state (running, stopped, setup) | Not available in the repository; operator or controller | n/a | [E] |
| Baseline values | Document 01 healthy values or a recorded baseline | per repair | [D] / [I] |

The scenario label and the ramp r are ground truth held in diag.sim and served only by a protected endpoint. The agent must not use them. The procedure reasons from channel evidence only [P].

Table 2. Feature definitions [D] / [I] V10 = mean(BEARING_VIBRATION_RMS over last 10 s) V60 = mean over last 60 s P10 = mean(LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE over last 10 s) P60 = mean over last 60 s I60 = mean(MAIN_MOTOR_CURRENT over 60 s) Ipk = max over each 4.6 s stroke; use 3 strokes (13.8 s) PF60 = share of samples in 60 s with V >= 2.5 HB300 = mean(amp[24..63]); PMR300 = max(amp[24..63]) / median(amp[24..63]) DL = amp[b] / healthy[b] for b in 7, 14, 21, 28, 35 RMSchk = | V - sqrt(sum(amp^2)) | / V dI/dV = (I60_now - I60_base) / (V60_now - V60_base) (A per mm/s) r_clog_P = (4.50 - P60) / 2.03 ; r_clog_V = (V60 - 1.31) / 3.68 r_bear_V = (V60 - 1.31) / 1.58 ; r_bear_I = (I60 - 94.8) / 7.6

Window lengths follow the 4.6 s stroke and the 1 Hz pump pulsation: a 10 s window holds about two strokes, a 60 s window about thirteen. The 2 Hz publication rate gives 20 and 120 samples respectively.

chunks.section: 2. Procedure Overview
chunks.text:
Figure 1. Diagnostic workflow from intake to post-maintenance verification (steps 1 to 13; step 14 is the report). Prototype logic [I].

Table 3. Fourteen-step procedure
| Step | Name | Question answered | Output | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Initial telemetry assessment | Is the data valid and is the machine running? | Valid / LS / suppressed | 3 |
| 2 | Baseline comparison | How far is each feature from its own baseline? | Deviations, ratios | 4 |
| 3 | Threshold evaluation | Which level does each channel reach? | L0 to L4 per channel | 4 |
| 4 | Persistence and duration | Is the level held for 10 s? | Opened or cleared level | 5 |
| 5 | Rate of change | How fast is it moving, and is it drift? | Slope, time to alarm | 5 |
| 6 | Machine operating state | Is the state valid for diagnosis? | State gate | 6 |
| 7 | Load conditions | Is the change confined to the working stroke? | Load attribution | 6 |
| 8 | Candidate fault generation | Which faults fit? | Candidate list | 7 |
| 9 | Fault differentiation | Which candidate is best supported? | Scores, margin | 8 |
| 10 | Inspection prioritisation | What is checked first? | Ordered inspection list | 9 |
| 11 | Severity classification | How serious is it? | S1 to S4 | 9 |
| 12 | Escalation | Who must act and by when? | Notification | 9 |
| 13 | Corrective action | What should be done? | Action | 10 |
| 14 | Post-maintenance verification | Did it work? | Pass / fail | 10 |

chunks.section: 3. Steps 1 to 3: Assessment, Baseline and Thresholds > 3.1 Step 1: initial telemetry assessment
chunks.text:
Table 4. Initial assessment rules
| Rule | IF condition | THEN classif ication | CHECK | Possible diagnosis | Recommended action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-01 | status is not online, or no telemetry for max(5 s, 4 x intervalMs) | LS data state | gateway diag (uptimeS, rssi, mqttReconnects), status topic | F15 data-path fault | No mechanical diagnosis; follow the data-path table |
| R-02 | bootId changes with seq back at 0 | LS information | uptimeS, reset reason, recent cmd/reboot | Gateway reboot (a simulated fault is cleared by cmd/reboot) | Restart the window and recompute the baseline |
| R-03 | Standard deviation of a channel is near zero over 60 s while the others vary | LS | Healthy P has 0.03 bar noise and 0.12 bar ripple; I and V breathe with the stroke | F12 (P), F13 (V) or F14 (I) | Inspect the sensor against a reference |
| R-04 | Received RMS differs from the square root of the summed squared spectrum bins by more than 2 percent [I] | LS | Latest spectrum within 2 s; decoding | F13 or F15 | Resolve data before any mechanical diagnosis |
| R-05 | An ack with ok true for cmd/scenario was seen in the window | Injected simulation event | ack detail, cmdId | Operator fault injection | Record as injected; do not escalate as a plant fault |
| R-31 | Machine stopped, in setup or die change [E] | Suppress | State input | No limit-based diagnosis | Wait for production |

Order matters: data and sensor questions are answered before mechanical ones, because a flat signal or a stale device mimics a fault. The repository's data-path table (Document 04) lists the likely causes of each data symptom.

chunks.section: 3. Steps 1 to 3: Assessment, Baseline and Thresholds > 3.2 Step 2: baseline comparison; 3.3 Step 3: threshold evaluation
chunks.text:
Table 5. Baseline comparison table [D] / [I]
| Feature | Baseline | Watch ratio or band | Flag as drifting |
|---|---|---|---|
| V60 | 1.31 mm/s | at or above 1.15 x (1.50 mm/s) | Rising 0.3 mm/s in 10 minutes |
| P60 | 4.50 bar | at or below 0.955 x (4.30 bar) | Falling 0.3 bar in 10 minutes |
| I60 | 94.8 A | at or above 1.05 x (99.5 A) | Rising 2 A in 10 minutes |
| Ipk | about 150 A | above 160 A | Three strokes in a row |
| HB300 | 0.030 mm/s | at or above 0.12 mm/s | Rising |
| PMR300 | not specified in repository | above 2.5 and rising | Above 3 with defect bins |

• Use the channel's own baseline, not a fleet average; the repository states a steady climb from 1.3

towards 3 mm/s is a drift whatever the limit says [P].

• Recompute the baseline after any repair, die change or oil change (Document 01 Section 19).

Table 6. Threshold classification rules
| Rule | IF condition | THEN classif ication | CHECK | Possible diagnosis | Recommended action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-06 | P10 at or below 3.6 bar for 10 s | L2 warning | V60, HB300, PMR300, I60 ratio | F01 candidate (also F03, F04, F06, F12) | Run differentiation; replace filter if F01 confirmed |
| R-07 | P10 at or below 3.0 bar for 10 s | L3 alarm | V60 at or above 4.0 mm/s and a broadband floor | F01 severe, or F03, F04 | Intervene this shift; filter swap if broadband |
| R-08 | P10 at or below 2.5 bar for 10 s [I] | L4 critical | V10, I60, state | Oil starvation of the bearings | Controlled stop and inspect |
| R-09 | V10 at or above 2.5 mm/s for 10 s | L2 warning | P60, PMR300, HB300 | F01 if P60 falls, F02 if P60 normal with lines | Lubrication first; inspect at next stop |
| R-10 | V10 at or above 4.0 mm/s for 10 s | L3 alarm | P60 at or below 3.0 bar? | F01 (bearing wear never reaches 4.0 mm/s in the model [P]) | Filter swap now; inspect bearings afterwards |
| R-11 | V10 at or above 7.0 mm/s for 10 s [I] | L4 critical | Mount and cable, impacts, other channels | Severe fault or F13 | Controlled stop; check sensor |
| R-12 | Ipk at or above 175 A in 2 of 3 strokes | L2 warning | Idle level 88 A? V60 and P60 normal? | F09 process or F08 motor | Check die, process, drive |
| R-13 | Ipk at or above 195 A in 2 of 3 strokes | L3 alarm | Stroke profile, drive protection | F09 or F08 severe | Reduce load; inspect |
| R-14 | Ipk at or above 220 A, or a sample at or above 240 A [I] | L4 critical | Jam or short | Overload or electrical fault | Stop |
| R-15 | V60 at or above 1.50 mm/s with every limit clear | L1 watch [I] | P60, PMR300, HB300, I60 | Early F02 or early F01 | Trend; check pressure first |
| R-16 | P60 at or below 4.30 bar with every limit clear | L1 watch [I] | V60 and HB300 rising? | Early F01 | Trend; plan filter inspection |

Table 7. Threshold classification table
| Channel | L0 Normal | L1 Watch [I] | L2 Warning [P] | L3 Alarm [P] | L4 Critical [I] | Unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ipk | up to 153 | above 160 | at or above 175 | at or above 195 | at or above 220 | A |
| I60 | 90 to 99 | above 99.5 | not defined | not defined | not defined | A |
| P60 / P10 | 4.35 to 4.65 | at or below 4.30 | at or below 3.6 | at or below 3.0 | at or below 2.5 | bar |
| V60 / V10 | 1.2 to 1.45 (V60) | at or above 1.50 | at or above 2.5 | at or above 4.0 | at or above 7.0 | mm/s |
| HB300 | 0.03 | at or above 0.12 | at or above 0.24 | not defined | not defined | mm/s |

| Channel | L0 Normal | L1 Watch [I] | L2 Warning [P] | L3 Alarm [P] | L4 Critical [I] | Unit |

| I60 | 90 to 99 | above 99.5 | not defined | not defined | not defined | A |
| P60 / P10 | 4.35 to 4.65 | at or below 4.30 | at or below 3.6 | at or below 3.0 | at or below 2.5 | bar |
| V60 / V10 | 1.2 to 1.45 (V60) | at or above 1.50 | at or above 2.5 | at or above 4.0 | at or above 7.0 | mm/s |
| HB300 | 0.03 | at or above 0.12 | at or above 0.24 | not defined | not defined | mm/s |

chunks.section: 4. Steps 4 to 7: Persistence, Rate, State and Load > 4.1 Step 4: persistence and duration; 4.2 Step 5: rate of change
chunks.text:
Table 8. Persistence rules
| Rule | IF condition | THEN classif ication | CHECK | Possible diagnosis | Recommended action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-28 | Value beyond a limit for 10 s (open) or inside for 10 s (clear) | Persistence | Window means | Level change | Apply to every level [P] planned |
| R-35 | Single sample outside a limit with window mean inside | Transient | Next 10 s | Spike or data error | Do not alarm |

Table 9. Why persistence is needed for each channel
| Channel | Cyclic content | Effect on per-sample status | Window used |
|---|---|---|---|
| V | Breathes with the 4.6 s stroke | BEARING_WEAR at r 0.6 to 0.8 flickers across 2.5 mm/s (2 percent to 88 percent of samples) | 10 s mean for status, PF60 for flicker [D] |
| P | 1 Hz pulsation, 0.03 bar noise | Near 3.6 bar the status flickers (P at r = 0.44 has mean 3.61 and range 3.48 to 3.72) | 10 s mean |
| I | Working-stroke pulse and 4 A ripple | Single samples hit 150 A in every stroke | Ipk over 3 strokes |

Table 10. Rate rules
| Rule | IF condition | THEN classif ication | CHECK | Possible diagnosis | Recommended action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-21 | V60 climbs steadily from about 1.3 toward 3 mm/s over hours | Drift | P60, shape | F02 or F01 | Treat as drift whatever the limit says [P] |
| R-27 | P60 falls by 0.3 bar or V60 rises by 0.3 mm/s within 10 minutes [I] | Drift L1 | Both features | F01 or F02 | Open a watch investigation |
| R-25 | Delta V60 / Delta P60 about -1.8 mm/s per bar over 10 minutes | Consistent with clog | HB300 | F01 consistency pass | Raise confidence |
| R-29 | Estimated time to alarm below 15 minutes of real time [I] | Escalation +1 | 60 s slope | Rapid progression | Raise one level |

Table 11. Rate thresholds at a glance [D] / [I]
| Feature | Healthy slope | Drift L1 | Rapid (escalate) |
|---|---|---|---|
| P60 | 0 bar/min | Falls 0.3 bar in 10 minutes | Estimated time to 3.0 bar under 15 minutes |
| V60 | 0 mm/s/min | Rises 0.3 mm/s in 10 minutes | Estimated time to 4.0 mm/s under 15 minutes |
| I60 | 0 A/min | Rises 2 A in 10 minutes | n/a |

Time to alarm = (limit - current value) / slope of the 60 s mean over the last 10 minutes. For the model at rampSec 120 s the clog slopes are -1.01 bar/min and +1.84 mm/s/min [D]; at 600 s they are one fifth of that. The repository planned detector also uses a rolling z-score above 3 for 30 s or a sustained positive slope of the 60 s mean over 10 minutes [P] planned.

chunks.section: 4. Steps 4 to 7: Persistence, Rate, State and Load > 4.3 Steps 6 and 7: operating state and load
chunks.text:
Table 12. State and load rules
| Rule | IF condition | THEN classif ication | CHECK | Possible diagnosis | Recommended action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-26 | Current evaluation | Stroke gating | Use Ipk over at least 3 strokes (13.8 s) | Single samples are not diagnostic | Never judge on one sample |
| R-23 | Ipk at or above 160 A with idle current about 88 A and V60, P60 normal | Process load | Die, material | F09 | Check die setup |
| R-31 | Machine stopped, in setup or die change [E] | Suppress | State input | No limit-based diagnosis | Wait for production |

Table 13. Load attribution
| Observation | Attribution | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Ipk up, idle 88 A unchanged, V60 and P60 normal | Process load (F09) | Increase is confined to the working stroke |
| I60 and idle both up, V60 up | Friction or bearing (F02, F01) or motor (F08) | Whole-cycle change |
| V up only in the 62.5 to 150 Hz structural band, in the working stroke | Impact or process | Band swells with load [P] |
| P changes | Never load | Pressure has no stroke-phase term [P] |

chunks.section: 5. Steps 8 and 9: Candidate Generation and Differentiation > 5.1 Step 8: candidate generation; 5.2 Evidence-weight matrix
chunks.text:
Table 14. Candidate generation from the leading observation
| Leading observation | Candidates (in order) | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| V10 at or above 2.5 mm/s, P60 falling | F01, F16, F03, F04 | Lubrication faults lower the pressure |
| V10 at or above 2.5 mm/s, P60 normal | F02, F10, F11, F13 | No pressure change |
| P10 at or below 3.6 bar, V60 normal | F12, F03, F04, F06, F01 early | Vibration has not followed |
| P rising | F05, F06, F07 | Different fault [P] |
| Ipk at or above 175 A | F09, F08, F14 | Current limit |
| V60 at 1.5 to 2.4 mm/s with no limit | F02 early, F01 early, F10 | Watch level |
| Flat or implausible channel | F12, F13, F14, F15 | Data first |

Each piece of evidence adds points to every candidate (negative points contradict it). The scores are prototype values [I]; the evidence definitions come from the repository signatures [P].

Table 15. Evidence-weight matrix
| ID | Evidence | F01 | F02 | F03/04 | F09 | F12 | F13 | F16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | P60 at or below 4.30 bar and falling | +3 | -3 | +3 | -2 | +1 | -1 | +3 |
| E2 | P60 within 4.45 to 4.55 bar | -3 | +2 | -3 | +1 | 0 | +1 | -3 |
| E3 | V60 at or above 1.50 mm/s and rising | +2 | +2 | +1 | 0 | -2 | +1 | +2 |
| E4 | HB300 at or above 0.24 mm/s with PMR300 below 2.5 (flat floor) | +3 | -2 | +1 | -1 | -3 | 0 | 0 |
| E5 | Discrete non-integer lines: PMR300 above 3, defect bins at least 4 x healthy | -3 | +4 | -2 | -1 | -1 | -1 | +3 |
| E5n | No discrete lines (PMR300 below 2.5) | +1 | -3 | +1 | +1 | 0 | 0 | -3 |
| E6 | V60 at or above 4.0 mm/s | +2 | -3 | +1 | 0 | -1 | +1 | +2 |
| E7 | Delta I60 / Delta V60 about 0.8 A per mm/s | +2 | -2 | 0 | -1 | 0 | 0 | +1 |
| E8 | Delta I60 / Delta V60 about 4.8 A per mm/s | -2 | +3 | -1 | +1 | 0 | -1 | +1 |
| E9 | Ipk at or above 160 A with idle level about 88 A | -1 | -1 | -1 | +4 | 0 | 0 | -1 |
| E10 | RMS differs from the spectrum root-sum-square, or V flat or implausible | -3 | -3 | -2 | -2 | 0 | +4 | -3 |
| E11 | Pressure ripple 0.12 bar missing or P flat | -2 | 0 | +1 | 0 | +4 | 0 | -2 |
| E12 | Step change instead of a ramp | -2 | -2 | -1 | +1 | +2 | +3 | -2 |
| E13 | P falling and discrete lines both present | -1 | -1 | 0 | -2 | -1 | -1 | +4 |
| E14 | V60 and HB300 do not move with P (P fall alone) | -3 | 0 | +2 | 0 | +3 | 0 | -3 |

Table 16. Decision from scores [I]
| Quantity | Rule | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Margin 4 or more | Top score minus second | Clear: act on the top candidate |
| Margin 2 to 3 | Top minus second | Ambiguous: apply R-20 (lubrication first) and gather more evidence |
| Margin 0 to 1 | Top minus second | Unresolved: inspection only; no corrective action |
| Top score 9 or more | Confidence | High |
| Top score 6 to 8 | Confidence | Medium |
| Top score 3 to 5 | Confidence | Low |

Table 17. Fault differentiation rules

| R-17 | HB300 at or above 0.24 mm/s and PMR300 below 2.5 | Flat floor evidence | P60 | F01 (broadband floor above 300 Hz) | Lubrication first |

chunks.section: 6. Decision Matrix and Inspection Priority > 6.1 Inspection priority
chunks.text:
Table 18. Diagnostic decision matrix: observation to action
| Observation | Classification | Check | Diagnosis | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P60 falling, V60 rising, flat floor, dI/dV about 0.8 | L2 to L3 | Filter cartridge, line pressure | F01 | Replace cartridge |
| V60 rising, P60 normal, lines at 88, 175, 263, 351, 439 Hz | L1 to L2 | Handheld analyser | F02 | Plan bearing replacement |
| V60 at 3 mm/s, P60 3.9 bar, floor with some lines | L2, ambiguous | Filter first | F16 or F01 | Replace filter; re-check spectrum |
| P low, V normal, ripple missing | LS | Transducer vs reference | F12 | Fix sensor |
| Ipk 180 A, idle 88 A | L2 | Die and process | F09 | Check setup |
| V10 8 mm/s, P and I normal, RMS differs from spectrum | LS / L4 | Sensor mount | F13 | Refit sensor |
| P rising to 5.5 bar | Other | Lines after transducer | F05 or F06 | Inspect |
| stale, offline | LS | diag | F15 | Fix link |

Table 19. Inspection prioritisation
| Priority | Item | Why first | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Data path and sensor against a reference | Cheapest and removes false alarms | Any LS or flat signal |
| 2 | Lube filter and line pressure | Cheap fault that causes bearing damage if left [P] | P60 falling or mixed evidence |
| 3 | Lube oil level, pump, leaks | Next lubrication causes | Pressure falls but filter swap does not help |
| 4 | Bearing frequencies with a handheld analyser | Confirms outer-race family | Pressure normal and lines present |
| 5 | Motor, supply and drive | Electrical causes | Current ratio above 4.8 A per mm/s or line lines |
| 6 | Die, alignment, fasteners | Process and mechanical looseness | Ipk up with idle normal; integer orders |
