chunks.section: 7. Steps 11 and 12: Severity and Escalation
chunks.text:
Table 20. Severity classification and escalation matrix
| Level | Severity | Notify | Time to act [I] | Condition for stop |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 Watch | S1 to S2 | Planner | Next planned inspection | None |
| L2 Warning | S2 | Technician | Next planned stop | None |
| L3 Alarm | S3 | Supervisor and maintenance | This shift | Supervisor decides |
| L4 Critical | S4 | Manager | Immediate | Controlled stop |
| LS | S1 | Instrumentation / IT | Within shift | Not a machine stop |

Table 21. Escalation modifiers
| Rule | IF condition | THEN classif ication | CHECK | Possible diagnosis | Recommended action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-29 | Estimated time to alarm below 15 minutes of real time [I] | Escalation +1 | 60 s slope | Rapid progression | Raise one level |
| R-30 | Two channels at L2 or above | Escalation +1 | Both channels | Compound condition | Raise one level (max L4) |

Table 22. Severity score [I]
| Component | Points | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| Level | 1 to 4 | L1 to L4 |
| Progression | +1 | Estimated time to alarm below 15 minutes |
| Compound | +1 | Two channels at L2 or above |
| Fault class | +1 | F02, F03, F04, F08 or F16 (high consequence) |
| Data suspect | cap 1 | LS |

Severity score 1 to 2 is S1 or S2, 3 to 4 is S3, 5 or more is S4. The repository's consequence statements anchor the classes: a clogged filter is a short cartridge swap, a bearing that fails in service costs days [P].

chunks.section: 8. Steps 13 and 14: Corrective Action and Verification > 8.1 Post-maintenance verification criteria
chunks.text:
Table 23. Corrective action by diagnosis
| Diagnosis | Action | Safety condition | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| F01 | Replace the filter cartridge (a short task, in the order of minutes) | OEM procedure; lock-out and tag-out; relieve line pressure; specified cartridge | [P] |
| F02 | Inspect at next planned stop with a handheld analyser; plan bearing replacement | OEM procedure; lock-out and tag-out before opening the main drive; specified bearings and fits | [P] |
| F03, F04 | Repair pump or leak; refill with the specified oil | OEM procedure | [E] |
| F05, F06 | Clear restriction or service the valve | OEM procedure | [E] |
| F08, F09 | Electrical test or process correction | Qualified electrician | [E] |
| F10, F11 | Align, balance or tighten | OEM procedure | [E] |
| F12 to F15 | Sensor or data repair | Instrument technician | [E] |

Table 24. Verification criteria after a repair [P] / [I]
| Quantity | Pass | Fail means | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| P60 | 4.35 to 4.65 bar, ripple present | Pressure not restored: other lubrication cause or transducer | [P] acceptance about 4.5 bar |
| V60 | 1.20 to 1.45 mm/s (baseline about 1.3) | Residual defect or another fault | [P] / [I] |
| HB300 | At most 0.06 mm/s (twice healthy) | Floor remains | [I] |
| PMR300 and defect bins | Defect bins below 4 x healthy | Bearing defect remains | [P] test |
| I60 | Within 3 percent of 94.8 A | Load or friction remains | [I] |
| Duration | 60 minutes of steady running with no L1 or above [I] | Reopen investigation | [I] |

| Rule | IF condition | THEN classif ication | CHECK | Possible diagnosis | Recommended action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

chunks.section: 10. Checklists, Report Template and Pseudo-code > 10.1 Checklists; 10.2 Report template; 10.3 Pseudo-code
chunks.text:
Table 35. Pre-diagnosis checklist
| Check | Done when |
|---|---|
| Data valid | status online, no gaps, RMS matches spectrum |
| State known | Machine running, not in setup |
| Baseline available | Healthy or recorded baseline |
| Window complete | At least 60 s of data |
| No injected event | No ack of cmd/scenario in the window |

Table 36. Pre-maintenance checklist
| Check | Done when |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis confidence | Medium or High, or lubrication-first rule applied |
| Safety | Lock-out and tag-out plan, OEM procedure available |
| Parts | Specified cartridge or bearings identified from the OEM documents |
| Verification plan | Criteria of the verification table |

Table 37. Report fields [P] planned
| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Observation | Channel, value, window, level, persistence |
| Diagnosis | Fault ID and name, confidence tier, score margin |
| Evidence | Features and their values against the baseline |
| Recommended action | Action, urgency, verification criteria |
| Confidence | Computed in code from signature matches, never from the model's impression |
| Citations | Document and section identifiers |
| Caveat | Follow the OEM procedure and apply lock-out and tag-out; the agent cannot act on the machine |

Table 38. Decision pseudo-code [I] if not valid(data): return LS(reason) # R-01 to R-04 if state in (stopped, setup): return SUPPRESSED # R-31 levels = {ch: level(window_mean(ch)) for ch in channels} # R-06 to R-16 if all(l == L0 for l in levels.values()) and no drift: return L0 cands = generate(levels, features) # Section 7 scores = sum_evidence(cands) # evidence-weight matrix top, second = rank(scores) if top - second < 2: apply R-20 (lubrication first) severity = score(levels, rate, compound, fault_class) return report(observation, top, evidence, action, confidence, citations)

chunks.section: 11. Edge Cases and Special Situations
chunks.text:
Table 39. Edge cases
| Situation | Treatment | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| V flickers across 2.5 mm/s with V60 below 2.5 | Use PF60; treat as L1 if PF60 above 0, L2 if V60 reaches 2.5 | BEARING_WEAR flicker at r 0.6 to 0.8 [P] |
| P crosses 3.6 bar only on single samples | No alarm; check P10 | Noise 0.03 bar and ripple 0.12 bar |
| Both channels warn simultaneously | Compound, lubrication first | Clog warns on V before P |
| Fault ramp very fast (5 s) | Rules operate on 10 s windows: expect L3 within 10 s of the ramp end | Ramp allowed 5 to 600 s [P] |
| Fault ramp very slow (600 s) | Drift rules and slope matter; limits come late | Slope one fifth of default |
| Reboot clears the fault | Treat as reset; recompute baseline | cmd/reboot [P] |
| Spectrum older than 2 s | Use latest; do not mix with older RMS | spectrum interval |
| Current high only at one stroke | Do not alarm | R-26 |
| P rising | Not a filter fault | R-22 |

chunks.section: 13. Consolidated Rule Library
chunks.text:
All IF/THEN rules used in this document. Rule identifiers are cited in the report so that a reader can find the rule here.

Table 41. Rules R-01 to R-18
| Rule | IF condition | THEN classif ication | CHECK | Possible diagnosis | Recommended action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-01 | status is not online, or no telemetry for max(5 s, 4 x intervalMs) | LS data state | gateway diag (uptimeS, rssi, mqttReconnects), status topic | F15 data-path fault | No mechanical diagnosis; follow the data-path table |
| R-02 | bootId changes with seq back at 0 | LS information | uptimeS, reset reason, recent cmd/reboot | Gateway reboot (a simulated fault is cleared by cmd/reboot) | Restart the window and recompute the baseline |
| R-03 | Standard deviation of a channel is near zero over 60 s while the others vary | LS | Healthy P has 0.03 bar noise and 0.12 bar ripple; I and V breathe with the stroke | F12 (P), F13 (V) or F14 (I) | Inspect the sensor against a reference |
| R-04 | Received RMS differs from the square root of the summed squared spectrum bins by more than 2 percent [I] | LS | Latest spectrum within 2 s; decoding | F13 or F15 | Resolve data before any mechanical diagnosis |
| R-05 | An ack with ok true for cmd/scenario was seen in the window | Injected simulation event | ack detail, cmdId | Operator fault injection | Record as injected; do not escalate as a plant fault |
| R-06 | P10 at or below 3.6 bar for 10 s | L2 warning | V60, HB300, PMR300, I60 ratio | F01 candidate (also F03, F04, F06, F12) | Run differentiation; replace filter if F01 confirmed |
| R-07 | P10 at or below 3.0 bar for 10 s | L3 alarm | V60 at or above 4.0 mm/s and a broadband floor | F01 severe, or F03, F04 | Intervene this shift; filter swap if broadband |
| R-08 | P10 at or below 2.5 bar for 10 s [I] | L4 critical | V10, I60, state | Oil starvation of the bearings | Controlled stop and inspect |
| R-09 | V10 at or above 2.5 mm/s for 10 s | L2 warning | P60, PMR300, HB300 | F01 if P60 falls, F02 if P60 normal with lines | Lubrication first; inspect at next stop |
| R-10 | V10 at or above 4.0 mm/s for 10 s | L3 alarm | P60 at or below 3.0 bar? | F01 (bearing wear never reaches 4.0 mm/s in the model [P]) | Filter swap now; inspect bearings afterwards |
| R-11 | V10 at or above 7.0 mm/s for 10 s [I] | L4 critical | Mount and cable, impacts, other channels | Severe fault or F13 | Controlled stop; check sensor |
| R-12 | Ipk at or above 175 A in 2 of 3 strokes | L2 warning | Idle level 88 A? V60 and P60 normal? | F09 process or F08 motor | Check die, process, drive |
| R-13 | Ipk at or above 195 A in 2 of 3 strokes | L3 alarm | Stroke profile, drive protection | F09 or F08 severe | Reduce load; inspect |
| R-14 | Ipk at or above 220 A, or a sample at or above 240 A [I] | L4 critical | Jam or short | Overload or electrical fault | Stop |
| R-15 | V60 at or above 1.50 mm/s with every limit clear | L1 watch [I] | P60, PMR300, HB300, I60 | Early F02 or early F01 | Trend; check pressure first |
| R-16 | P60 at or below 4.30 bar with every limit clear | L1 watch [I] | V60 and HB300 rising? | Early F01 | Trend; plan filter inspection |
| R-17 | HB300 at or above 0.24 mm/s and PMR300 below 2.5 | Flat floor evidence | P60 | F01 (broadband floor above 300 Hz) | Lubrication first |
| R-18 | PMR300 above 3 and defect bins 7, 14, 21, 28, 35 at least 4 x healthy | Discrete family evidence | P60 normal? | F02 bearing wear | Handheld analyser; plan replacement |

chunks.section: 13. Consolidated Rule Library
chunks.text:
Table 42. Rules R-19 to R-35
| Rule | IF condition | THEN classif ication | CHECK | Possible diagnosis | Recommended action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-19 | Pressure normal and the spectrum shows discrete peaks | Not a filter problem | Bearing procedure | F02 | Use the bearing runbook [P] |
| R-20 | Evidence is mixed between a lubrication fault and a bearing fault | Lubrication first | Filter and pressure trend | F01 or F16 | Replace the filter first, then re-check the spectrum [P] |
| R-21 | V60 climbs steadily from about 1.3 toward 3 mm/s over hours | Drift | P60, shape | F02 or F01 | Treat as drift whatever the limit says [P] |
| R-22 | P60 rises above 4.65 bar, or above 5.0 bar [I] | Different fault | V60, state, temperature | F05 or F06 (not modelled) | Inspect after the transducer; not a filter problem [P] |
| R-23 | Ipk at or above 160 A with idle current about 88 A and V60, P60 normal | Process load | Die, material | F09 | Check die setup |
| R-24 | Delta I60 / Delta V60 above 3.5 A per mm/s | Bearing or electrical | Lines, line-frequency content | F02 or F08 | Bearing inspection; motor test if line lines |
| R-25 | Delta V60 / Delta P60 about -1.8 mm/s per bar over 10 minutes | Consistent with clog | HB300 | F01 consistency pass | Raise confidence |
| R-26 | Current evaluation | Stroke gating | Use Ipk over at least 3 strokes (13.8 s) | Single samples are not diagnostic | Never judge on one sample |
| R-27 | P60 falls by 0.3 bar or V60 rises by 0.3 mm/s within 10 minutes [I] | Drift L1 | Both features | F01 or F02 | Open a watch investigation |
| R-28 | Value beyond a limit for 10 s (open) or inside for 10 s (clear) | Persistence | Window means | Level change | Apply to every level [P] planned |
| R-29 | Estimated time to alarm below 15 minutes of real time [I] | Escalation +1 | 60 s slope | Rapid progression | Raise one level |
| R-30 | Two channels at L2 or above | Escalation +1 | Both channels | Compound condition | Raise one level (max L4) |
| R-31 | Machine stopped, in setup or die change [E] | Suppress | State input | No limit-based diagnosis | Wait for production |
| R-32 | After a repair | Verify | P60 4.35 to 4.65 bar, V60 1.2 to 1.45 mm/s, HB300 at most 0.06 mm/s, I60 within 3 percent of baseline | Repair successful or not | Return to service or reopen |
| R-33 | Report is produced | Content rule | Observation, diagnosis, evidence, action, confidence, citations, OEM and lock-out caveat | Planned guard [P] | Reject reports without the caveat |
| R-34 | Transducer-like signature: P flat or offset with V and HB300 unchanged | Sensor suspect | Reference gauge | F12 | Verify sensor before filter work |
| R-35 | Single sample outside a limit with window mean inside | Transient | Next 10 s | Spike or data error | Do not alarm |

• Validate data first, classify levels on 10 s and 60 s windows, then generate candidates and score

them with the evidence-weight matrix.

• Pressure, spectrum shape, current ratio and alarm behaviour separate the two simulated faults;

mixed evidence means lubrication first [P].

• Never rely on a threshold alarm alone: BEARING_WEAR never reaches 4.0 mm/s [P].

| I warn / alarm / critical | 175 / 195 / 220 A | [P] / [P] / [I] |
| Persistence | 10 s open, 10 s clear | [P] planned |
| Margin rule | 4 clear, 2 to 3 ambiguous, 0 to 1 unresolved | [I] |

| Scope | Condition-based maintenance for the main drive and its pressure lubrication circuit and for the data path of the three channels. The repository holds only two runbook stubs; everything else here is engineering reference [E] to be replaced or confirmed by the OEM manual. Levels are in Document 01, signatures in Document 02, decisions in Document 03, cases in Document 05. |

| [I] | Illustrative / proposed prototype value: chosen by the authors for this knowledge base and meant to be refined with real plant data. |

An ESP32 gateway (or a software simulator) plays the press controller and generates values from documented equations. chunks.section: 1. Maintenance Philosophy > 1.1 Condition-based approach
chunks.text:
The repository gives no inspection or service intervals, filter or bearing part numbers, oil specification, differential-pressure limits, torque values, replacement procedures, tools, spares, mean time between failures or OEM references [P]. This document therefore does not invent intervals. Work is triggered by condition: the Document 01 level (L1 to L4, LS), the diagnosis and the verification result. Routine inspection follows the OEM schedule and the site plan, which are referenced but not reproduced.

PRINCIPLE (press runbooks [P]): do not run a drifting bearing to alarm; schedule an inspection at the next planned stop. The cheap filter fix is only cheap while it is early.

Table 1. Condition-based maintenance triggers
| Telemetry condition | Level | Maintenance response | Timing basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| All features inside healthy bands | L0 | Routine inspection per OEM schedule | OEM schedule (not specified in repository) |
| V60 at or above 1.50 mm/s or P60 at or below 4.30 bar, no limit | L1 | Add to next planned inspection; check filter and oil records; trend | Next planned inspection |
| V or P at warn (2.5 mm/s or 3.6 bar) | L2 | Filter inspection; bearing inspection if lines present | Next planned stop |
| V at 4.0 mm/s or P at 3.0 bar | L3 | Filter swap or intervention; plan bearing check | This shift [I] |
| P at or below 2.5 bar, V at or above 7.0 mm/s, Ipk at or above 220 A | L4 | Controlled stop and full inspection | Immediate |
| Flat, implausible or stale data | LS | Sensor and data-path inspection first | Within the shift |

chunks.section: 2. Safety Considerations > 2.1 Pre-work checklist
chunks.text:
This document is a capstone prototype. It does not replace the OEM manual, the plant lock-out and tag-out procedure or site safety rules. Follow the manufacturer's procedure. Apply lock-out and tag-out before opening the lubrication circuit or the main drive and relieve the line pressure. Only qualified persons may do the work.

Table 3. Hazards and controls [E]
| Hazard | Where | Control |
|---|---|---|
| Stored energy in the slide, flywheel and clutch | Press | Isolate and block the slide per OEM; verify zero energy |
| Pressurised oil | Lube circuit downstream of the pump | Lock-out; relieve line pressure; open slowly |
| Hot oil and surfaces | Reservoir, housing, motor | Allow cooling; gloves, eye protection |
| Unexpected start | Main drive | Lock-out and tag-out; personal locks; try-out test |
| Electrical shock, stored charge | Motor, drive | Qualified electrician; verified isolation; rated meters |
| Rotating parts | Shaft, coupling, flywheel | Guards in place; no work while rotating except approved vibration measurement |
| Crush at the die | Ram and die | Die blocks, safety props |
| Oil spill and slips | Floor | Absorbents; clean up; safety data sheets |
| Manual handling | Cartridge, bearings | Lifting aids |
| Restart after work | Controller | Verification run per Section 14; clear the area |

• Confirm the machine ID (press-stamp-01), the level and the diagnosis from the report.

• Obtain the OEM manual, the permit to work and the lock-out and tag-out plan.

• Record baseline readings before work: P60, V60, I60, HB300 and a spectrum snapshot.

• Identify the specified cartridge, bearings and oil from OEM documents, not from this document.

• Check that no cmd/scenario test is running (a simulated fault must not be mistaken for a plant

fault).

| Oil spill and slips | Floor | Absorbents; clean up; safety data sheets |
| Manual handling | Cartridge, bearings | Lifting aids |
| Restart after work | Controller | Verification run per Section 14; clear the area |

• Confirm the machine ID (press-stamp-01), the level and the diagnosis from the report.

• Obtain the OEM manual, the permit to work and the lock-out and tag-out plan.

• Record baseline readings before work: P60, V60, I60, HB300 and a spectrum snapshot.

• Identify the specified cartridge, bearings and oil from OEM documents, not from this document.

• Check that no cmd/scenario test is running (a simulated fault must not be mistaken for a plant

fault).

chunks.section: 4. Mechanical Inspection > 4.1 Main bearing housing; 4.2 Handheld vibration measurement procedure
chunks.text:
Table 6. Main bearing housing inspection criteria [E]
| Check | Method | Acceptable | Action if not |
|---|---|---|---|
| Defect lines | Handheld analyser, spectrum to 800 Hz | No lines at about 88, 175, 263, 351, 439 Hz with sidebands at 24.7 Hz | Plan bearing replacement [P] |
| Overall vibration | Handheld RMS at the housing | Agrees with BEARING_VIBRATION_RMS within the sensor tolerance | Check sensor |
| Housing temperature | Touch or contact thermometer | No local hot spot | Check lubrication |
| Noise | Listen | No rumble or clicking | Analyser |
| Mounting and fasteners | Visual, torque check per OEM | Marks intact | Tighten per OEM |
| Oil film evidence | Oil at the bearing drain | Clean oil, no metal | Check filter first |

Table 7. Handheld vibration measurement [E]
| Step | Action | Pitfall to avoid |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Measure with the press running steadily, not during a die change | Transient state gives unrepresentative amplitudes |
| 2 | Place the probe at the housing in the same position and direction as the installed sensor | Different position changes amplitude |
| 3 | Set the span to at least 800 Hz and a resolution that separates 24.7 Hz sidebands | Too coarse a resolution merges lines |
| 4 | Record the overall RMS and the spectrum | Not recording the file |
| 5 | Mark 1X (24.7 Hz) and the defect orders 3.55, 7.1, 10.65, 14.2, 17.75 x 1X [P] | Confusing integer orders with defect orders |
| 6 | Compare with the channel value and with the healthy signature | Comparing across different operating states |

chunks.section: 5. Lubrication Circuit Inspection > 5.1 Circuit elements; 5.2 Oil sampling and analysis; 5.3 Interpreting what the filter looks like
chunks.text:
Table 9. Lubrication circuit inspection
| Element | Inspection | Acceptable | Telemetry link |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reservoir | Level, temperature, condition | Between marks; clean | None (level not measured [P]) |
| Gear pump | Noise, coupling, delivery | Smooth; pressure about 4.5 bar with 0.12 bar pulsation | Pulsation in LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE |
| Lube filter | Cartridge condition, delta-P if gauge | Clean; no bypass | P60 falling with V60 rising when clogged |
| Pressure transducer | Reading against a reference gauge | Agrees | LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE |
| Distribution line and nozzles | Leaks, blockage | Free flow | P rising when blocked after the transducer |
| Relief valve | Setting, sticking | Within OEM | Pressure step |

Table 10. Oil sampling [E]
| Item | Method | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Sample point | Per OEM, from the circuit while running | Representative sample |
| Particle count | Laboratory | High counts support a clogging filter (F01) |
| Metals | Laboratory | Iron or bearing alloys support bearing wear (F02) |
| Water | Laboratory | Degradation and corrosion |
| Viscosity | Laboratory | Affects pressure (F07) |
| Interval | Not specified in repository | Take a sample when a lubrication condition is suspected |

Table 11. Filter condition assessment [E]
| Observation | Grade | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Clean media, normal delta-P | A | Healthy | None |
| Light loading | B | Early loading | Monitor |
| Heavy loading, discoloured media | C | Clogging | Replace |
| Collapsed media, bypass open | D | Failed | Replace now; inspect bearings |
| Metal particles in media | D+ | Wear debris | Replace and inspect bearings and pump |

Metal particles in a clogged filter point beyond the filter to bearing or pump wear. Replace the cartridge and inspect the main bearings before returning to service [E].

chunks.section: 7. Sensor Inspection and Validation
chunks.text:
Table 13. Sensor inspection by channel [E]
| Channel | What to inspect | Reference | Acceptance | If it fails |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE (0 to 8 bar, 2 decimals) | Port, fitting, wiring, ripple signature | Reference gauge at the same port | Agrees within the transducer tolerance; ripple 0.12 bar and noise 0.03 bar visible | Replace or recalibrate |
| BEARING_VIBRATION_RMS (0 to 12 mm/s) and BEARING_SPECTRUM | Mount torque, cable, shielding | Handheld analyser at the same housing | RMS agrees; spectrum has 1X as largest bin; no mains lines | Refit, replace cable |
| MAIN_MOTOR_CURRENT (0 to 250 A) | Burden, wiring | Clamp meter | Agrees at idle (about 88 A) and in stroke (about 150 A) | Replace or recalibrate |
| Gateway time | synced true | SNTP | ts within 2 minutes | Fix NTP (UDP 123) |

chunks.section: 8. Component Condition Assessment > 8.1 Interpreting inspection findings against telemetry
chunks.text:
Table 14. Condition grades for the three components [E]
| Component | Grade A (good) | Grade B (watch) | Grade C (act) | Grade D (replace now) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lube filter | Clean; P 4.4 to 4.6 bar | Light loading; P60 4.30 bar or lower | Heavy loading; P60 at or below 3.6 bar | Bypass or collapse; P at or below 3.0 bar |
| Main bearings | V60 1.2 to 1.45 mm/s; no lines | V60 above 1.50; faint lines | Lines at least 4 x healthy; V60 above 2.0 | V60 above 2.5 mm/s with strong lines, noise or heat |
| Main drive motor | I60 within 3 percent of baseline | I60 above 1.05 x | Ipk above 175 A or heating | Trips, insulation failure |
| Lubrication unit (pump, relief valve) | P 4.5 bar with ripple | Ripple changed | P step or irregular | No pressure |
| Sensors | Agree with references | Drift within tolerance | Out of tolerance | Failed |

Table 15. Grade to action
| Grade | Action | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| A | Routine | OEM schedule |
| B | Add to next planned inspection | Next planned inspection |
| C | Plan the work and parts | Next planned stop |
| D | Replace | This shift or immediately |

Table 16. Inspection finding versus expected telemetry [E]
| Finding on inspection | Expected telemetry | If telemetry disagrees |
|---|---|---|
| Heavily loaded filter | P60 low, V60 up, HB300 up | Suspect transducer or a second cause |
| Clean filter | P60 normal | Pressure fall has another cause: pump, leak, valve, transducer |
| Metal in the filter or oil | V60 up with lines at defect orders; P may be normal | Sample oil; inspect pump too |
| Bearing noise or heat | V60 up; I60 up | Check alignment and lubrication |
| Loose fasteners | Integer harmonics of 1X | Tighten and re-measure |
| Worn coupling or misalignment | 1X and 2X up | Align |
| Damaged vibration cable | V spikes or mismatch | Replace and re-baseline |

chunks.section: 9. Troubleshooting Procedure > 9.1 Procedure steps; 9.2 Troubleshooting decision tree (text)
chunks.text:
Table 17. Troubleshooting procedure
| Step | Action | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Confirm the report: channel, value, window, level | If the data are not valid, go to Section 21 |
| 2 | Rule out the data path and sensors (Sections 7 and 21) | If a sensor or link is faulty, repair it first |
| 3 | Confirm the pressure trend over the last hour and the pump pulsation | Falling: lubrication path; normal: bearing or other |
| 4 | Confirm the spectrum shape: broadband or peaked | Broadband above 300 Hz: filter; peaked at defect orders: bearing |
| 5 | Confirm the other channels are normal | If current is the only abnormal channel, go to the process and drive checks |
| 6 | If the evidence is mixed, check the lubrication first | Replace the filter, then re-check the spectrum |
| 7 | Apply lock-out and tag-out, perform the inspection or repair | Record findings |
| 8 | Verify against the criteria of Section 14 | Return to service or reopen |

Table 18. Decision tree
| Question | Yes | No |
|---|---|---|
| Is the data valid (online, no gaps, RMS equals spectrum)? | Next question | Section 21; repair data path |
| Is the press running steadily? | Next question | Wait; suppress diagnosis |
| Is P60 at or below 4.30 bar? | Check the spectrum floor; go to filter | Next question |
| Are there discrete lines at defect orders? | Bearing inspection T2 | Next question |
| Is Ipk at or above 160 A with idle 88 A? | Process and drive T8 | Next question |
| Is any channel flat or implausible? | Sensor T4 to T6 | Trend and watch |

chunks.section: 9. Troubleshooting Procedure > 9.3 Observed condition to action
chunks.text:
Table 19. Observed condition, possible cause, inspection, corrective action, verification
| Observed condition | Possible cause | Inspection | Corrective action | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P60 at or below 3.6 bar, V60 at or above 2.5 mm/s, flat floor | Clogged filter (F01) | Cartridge, delta-P | Replace cartridge | P60 4.5 bar, V60 1.3 mm/s |
| P60 at or below 3.0 bar, V60 above 4.0 mm/s | Severe clog or starved bearing | Cartridge, then bearings and oil | Replace cartridge now; plan bearing check | P and V back; lines absent |
| V60 rising, P normal, lines at defect orders | Bearing wear (F02) | Handheld analyser, housing | Plan bearing replacement | Lines gone, V60 1.3 mm/s |
| V60 at 2.5 to 3.5 mm/s, P normal, no lines | Imbalance, looseness, sensor | Alignment, fasteners, mount | Correct | V60 1.3 mm/s |
| P low, V normal | Transducer, pump, leak, relief valve | Reference gauge, level, pump | Repair | P 4.5 bar with ripple |
| P above 4.65 bar, rising | Blocked nozzle or line after the transducer | Nozzles, relief valve | Clear restriction | P 4.5 bar |
| Ipk at or above 175 A, idle 88 A | Process or die load | Die, material, shut height | Correct setup | Ipk about 150 A |
| I60 above 8 percent, line-frequency lines | Motor or supply | Insulation, supply | Repair motor | I60 94.8 A |
| I flat or near zero, press cycling | Current sensor | Clamp meter | Repair sensor | Pulse to about 150 A |
| V10 at or above 7.0 mm/s, P and I normal | Mount or cable | Mount, shield | Refit or replace | V about 1.3 mm/s |
| RMS differs from spectrum | Decoding or data | Gateway, backend | Fix data path | RMS equals spectrum |
| Pressure drops but filter swap does not help | Pump, leak, relief valve, transducer | Level, pump, gauge | Repair | P 4.5 bar |
| V rises again after a bearing change | Lubrication or alignment | Filter, alignment | Correct | V 1.3 mm/s |
| Alarm appears only at stroke peaks | Per-sample classification | Window means | No repair | V10 inside limits |
| Pressure alarm after cold start | Cold oil | Oil temperature | Warm up | P 4.5 bar warm |
| Device stale | Network or power | diag, status | Fix link | status online |
| Identity conflict flagged | Board and simulator both announce press-stamp-01 | Stop one source | Stop the simulator or the board | Single source |
| Fault seems stuck | Simulated fault active | Faults tab | Choose Normal or send cmd/reboot | Values normal |

| V60 rising, P normal, lines at defect orders | Bearing wear (F02) | Handheld analyser, housing | Plan bearing replacement | Lines gone, V60 1.3 mm/s |
| V60 at 2.5 to 3.5 mm/s, P normal, no lines | Imbalance, looseness, sensor | Alignment, fasteners, mount | Correct | V60 1.3 mm/s |
| P low, V normal | Transducer, pump, leak, relief valve | Reference gauge, level, pump | Repair | P 4.5 bar with ripple |
| P above 4.65 bar, rising | Blocked nozzle or line after the transducer | Nozzles, relief valve | Clear restriction | P 4.5 bar |
| Ipk at or above 175 A, idle 88 A | Process or die load | Die, material, shut height | Correct setup | Ipk about 150 A |
| I60 above 8 percent, line-frequency lines | Motor or supply | Insulation, supply | Repair motor | I60 94.8 A |
| I flat or near zero, press cycling | Current sensor | Clamp meter | Repair sensor | Pulse to about 150 A |
| V10 at or above 7.0 mm/s, P and I normal | Mount or cable | Mount, shield | Refit or replace | V about 1.3 mm/s |
| RMS differs from spectrum | Decoding or data | Gateway, backend | Fix data path | RMS equals spectrum |
| Pressure drops but filter swap does not help | Pump, leak, relief valve, transducer | Level, pump, gauge | Repair | P 4.5 bar |
| V rises again after a bearing change | Lubrication or alignment | Filter, alignment | Correct | V 1.3 mm/s |
| Alarm appears only at stroke peaks | Per-sample classification | Window means | No repair | V10 inside limits |
| Pressure alarm after cold start | Cold oil | Oil temperature | Warm up | P 4.5 bar warm |
| Device stale | Network or power | diag, status | Fix link | status online |
| Identity conflict flagged | Board and simulator both announce press-stamp-01 | Stop one source | Stop the simulator or the board | Single source |
| Fault seems stuck | Simulated fault active | Faults tab | Choose Normal or send cmd/reboot | Values normal |

chunks.section: 11. Corrective Priorities and Replacement Criteria
chunks.text:
Table 22. Corrective priority
| Priority | Condition | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | LS: sensor or data fault | Avoids unnecessary mechanical work |
| 2 | L4 or P at or below 2.5 bar | Oil starvation |
| 3 | L3 with broadband floor | Cheap, high-benefit filter swap |
| 4 | L3 or L2 with lines (bearing) | Planned replacement; avoid failure in service |
| 5 | L2 process or electrical | Planned correction |
| 6 | L1 | Trend and inspection |

Table 23. Replacement criteria [E]
| Component | Replace when | Do not replace when |
|---|---|---|
| Lube filter cartridge | Loaded or bypassing (grade C or D), or P60 at or below 3.6 bar with broadband floor confirmed | Pressure low but spectrum peaked, or sensor not verified |
| Main bearing | Lines at defect orders at least 4 x healthy with rising V60, or metal in the oil, or noise or heat, or OEM limit reached | Single spike; sensor fault; integer-order pattern only (alignment first) |
| Pressure transducer | Disagrees with the reference gauge beyond tolerance | Pressure fall confirmed by V60 and HB300 |
| Vibration sensor | Disagrees with the handheld analyser or RMS differs from the spectrum | Vibration confirmed by handheld |
| Gear pump | No delivery or pulsation lost, filter excluded | Filter loaded |
| Oil | Contaminated or degraded per analysis | Not specified in repository: no interval given |

Replace parts only with the OEM-specified cartridge, bearings and fits [P]. The repository gives no part numbers.

chunks.section: 12. Task Procedures > 12.1 T1 Replace the lube filter cartridge (F01) [P]; 12.2 T2 Bearing inspection with a handheld analyser (F02) [P]; 12.3 T3 Replace the main bearings [P][E]
chunks.text:
Task procedures are generic engineering reference [E]. The OEM procedure takes precedence. Steps that are the repository's own statements are marked [P].

Table 24. T1: steps
| Step | Action | Check / record |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Confirm diagnosis: P60 falling, flat broadband floor, V60 rising | Record P60, V60, HB300, spectrum snapshot |
| 2 | Obtain permit; apply lock-out and tag-out; relieve line pressure [P] | Zero-energy verified |
| 3 | Open the filter housing per OEM; remove the cartridge | Inspect media: grade; metal particles? |
| 4 | Fit the specified cartridge [P]; reseat and close the housing | Cartridge ID recorded |
| 5 | Refill or bleed per OEM; remove locks; restore power | Area clear |
| 6 | Start; watch LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE rise | P about 4.5 bar [P] |
| 7 | Run the verification of Section 14 | V60 about 1.3 mm/s [P] |

Table 25. T2: steps
| Step | Action | Check / record |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | At the next planned stop, take the baseline from the sensor channel | Record V60 and spectrum |
| 2 | Measure at the housing in the same direction and position as the sensor | Compare RMS |
| 3 | Look for lines at about 88, 175, 263, 351, 439 Hz with sidebands at 24.7 Hz | Mark presence and amplitude |
| 4 | If lines present: plan bearing replacement; if absent: check alignment and sensor | Decision recorded |
| 5 | Do not run to alarm [P] | Schedule and parts per OEM |

Table 26. T3: steps
| Step | Action | Check / record |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Plan the stop; obtain bearings and fits specified by the OEM | Parts verified |
| 2 | Lock-out and tag-out before opening the main drive [P] | Zero-energy verified |
| 3 | Open and remove per OEM; inspect shaft and housing | Wear, damage recorded |
| 4 | Fit the specified bearings and fits [P]; reassemble; lubricate per OEM | Fit values recorded |
| 5 | Align and torque per OEM | Values recorded |
| 6 | Run-in at reduced speed and verify (Section 14) | V60 about 1.3 mm/s, lines absent |

chunks.section: 13. Calibration and Validation
chunks.text:
Table 32. Calibration and validation [E]
| Item | Method | Frequency basis | Acceptance |

chunks.section: 14. Post-Maintenance Testing > 14.1 Test steps; 14.2 Return-to-service criteria; 14.3 Service events and their effect on telemetry
chunks.text:
Table 33. Post-maintenance test
| Step | Test | Pass criterion | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Visual and leak check, guards in place | No leaks; guards fitted | [E] |
| 2 | Start at reduced speed or per OEM | No abnormal noise | [E] |
| 3 | P60 after 5 minutes of running | 4.35 to 4.65 bar with ripple | [P] about 4.5 bar |
| 4 | V60 after 10 minutes | 1.20 to 1.45 mm/s | [P] about 1.3 mm/s |
| 5 | Spectrum | 1X largest; no lines; HB300 at most 0.06 mm/s | [P] / [I] |
| 6 | I60 | Within 3 percent of 94.8 A | [I] |
| 7 | Steady run | 60 minutes without L1 or above | [I] |
| 8 | Data | status online, no gaps, RMS equals spectrum | [P] |

Table 34. Return-to-service criteria
| Criterion | Required | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Safety | Locks removed, guards fitted, area clear | Permit closed |
| Pressure | Restored within the band | P60 |
| Vibration | Back to baseline | V60, spectrum |
| Current | Within 3 percent of baseline | I60 |
| Data | Valid for 60 minutes | Data-quality checks |
| Records | Findings and parts recorded | Work record |
| Approval | Supervisor sign-off | Signature |

Table 35. If a criterion fails
| Failed criterion | Meaning | Next step |
|---|---|---|
| Pressure not restored | Other lubrication fault or sensor | T4, T7 |
| Vibration not restored after a filter swap | Bearing wear or mixed fault | T2 |
| Vibration not restored after bearing change | Alignment or lubrication | T1, alignment |
| Current high | Load or friction | T8 |

Table 36. Service events and expected telemetry [E] / [P]
| Event | Expected effect | Handling |
|---|---|---|
| Filter cartridge replaced | P steps up toward 4.5 bar within the circuit fill time; V settles to about 1.3 mm/s [P] | Compare with the verification band; update baseline |
| Bearing replaced | V returns to about 1.3 mm/s; lines vanish; I60 returns to about 94.8 A [P] / [D] | Run-in period at reduced speed; re-baseline |
| Oil changed or topped up | Pressure may change slightly with viscosity | Re-baseline P |
| Sensor replaced | Step change in that channel only | Re-baseline; check against reference |
| Die changed | Ipk and current baseline change; P and V unchanged | Re-baseline current |
| Gateway rebooted | bootId changes; seq restarts; simulated fault cleared | Restart window |

chunks.section: 15. Use of the Digital Twin During Maintenance
chunks.text:
Table 37. Twin elements [P]
| Element | Behaviour | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Mesh labelled Lubrication unit (suggested 090-stamping-press/1) | Amber on warn, pulsing red on alarm | Locate the pressure channel; the label says what it stands for |
| Mesh labelled Main bearing housing (suggested 090-stamping-press/ram/steel) | Same | Locate vibration |
| Mesh labelled Main drive motor (suggested 090-stamping-press/0) | Same | Locate current |
| Telemetry tab | Trend line per channel; spectrum with ticks at the shaft harmonics | Compare to the healthy signature |
| Faults tab (needs ENABLE_DEVICE_COMMANDS true) | Injects simulated faults | Do not use during real maintenance; choose Normal to reset |

The twin asset has no lubrication unit, motor or bearing housing as separate parts; the meshes are suggestions and docs/demo-bindings.json records no captured binding [P]. Keep the pressure and vibration meshes apart and large enough to read, because the fault demo tints both.

chunks.section: 21. Data-Path Troubleshooting
chunks.text:
Rule out these before a mechanical cause. They come from the repository's firmware README, MQTT contract and demo script [P].

Table 45. Data-path symptoms and likely causes [P]
| Symptom | Likely cause |
|---|---|
| Telemetry arrives but the twin shows nothing | Channel not bound to a mesh, or the machine not added to the twin |
| Device shown stale | No telemetry for max(5 s, 4 x intervalMs) |
| Device offline about 15 s after power loss | Last Will published by the broker |
| Identity conflict flagged | Board and simulator both announcing press-stamp-01 |
| A fault seems stuck | Choose Normal in the Faults tab, or send cmd/reboot |
| No Faults tab | ENABLE_DEVICE_COMMANDS is not true |
| wifi disconnect event, reason 201 | Network not found, or 5 GHz only |
| reason 202 or 15 | Wrong Wi-Fi password or unsupported security mode |
| mqtt connect failed (state 4) / state 5 | Wrong broker credentials / credential lacks permission |
| tls error -9984 | Clock wrong, or the CA file does not anchor the chain |
| clock not set after 15 s | Network blocks NTP (UDP 123) |
| Gaps in seq | Packet loss |

Table 46. Gateway health fields to inspect (diag) [P]
| Field | Healthy |
|---|---|
| uptimeS | Increasing |
| rssi | Stable |
| heapFree, heapMin | Stable minimum over a 30 minute soak |
| reset | Expected reason |
| wifiReconnects, mqttReconnects, restarts, publishFailures | Low and stable |
| tls | true |

chunks.section: 23. Summary, Safety, References and Revision > 23.1 Maintenance summary; 23.2 Key criteria; 23.3 Safety and escalation notes; 23.4 References and engineering basis; 23.5 Revision notes
chunks.text:
• Condition-based: filter replacement for broadband and falling pressure; planned bearing work for

discrete lines; sensors and data first when signals look wrong.

• Mixed evidence: lubrication first [P]. Filter swap is minutes; a bearing that fails in service costs

days [P].

• Verify: pressure about 4.5 bar, vibration about 1.3 mm/s, spectrum back to healthy shape [P].

Table 48. Key criteria
| Item | Value | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| Verification P60 | 4.35 to 4.65 bar | [P] / [I] |
| Verification V60 | 1.20 to 1.45 mm/s | [P] / [I] |
| HB300 after repair | At most 0.06 mm/s | [I] |
| Replace filter at | P60 at or below 3.6 bar with broadband floor | [P] / [E] |
| Bearing action | Lines at defect orders: plan replacement | [P] |

chunks.text:
TECHNICAL DIAGNOSTIC KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENT

Fault History, Case Scenarios and Diagnostic Evidence

Stamping press 01 (press-stamp-01) | Main drive and lubrication circuit

| Machine | Stamping press 01 (machine ID press-stamp-01, type press, area Press shop, site vit-lab), stamping press in a car plant |
|---|---|
| Sensors | MAIN_MOTOR_CURRENT (A), LUBE_OIL_PRESSURE (bar), BEARING_VIBRATION_RMS (mm/s) and the 64-bin spectrum BEARING_SPECTRUM (mm/s); sensor IDs PRESS-STAMP-01.<CHANNEL_KEY> |
| Components / subsystem | Press main drive and its pressure lubrication circuit: main drive motor, lubrication unit (gear pump, reservoir, lube filter) and main bearing housing; planned agent tags main_drive_motor, lube_filter, lubrication_unit, main_bearing_housing |
| Document title | Fault History, Case Scenarios and Diagnostic Evidence |
| Document ID | PS01-DOC-05 |
| Revision / date | 1.0 / 2026-10-08 |
| Purpose | Provides case-based diagnostic knowledge for press-stamp-01: eighteen worked scenarios showing how telemetry of the main drive motor current, lube oil pressure and bearing vibration is interpreted, differentiated, repaired and verified, with comparison tables of the evidence. |
| Scope | Simulated and illustrative cases only. The repository holds no real fault history; cases C01 to C06 and C15 to C18 are built from the repository's two simulated faults [P][D], the others are illustrative [I]. Limits are in Document 01, signatures in Document 02, the procedure in Document 03, maintenance in Document 04. |

Provenance tags used throughout this document

| [P] | Project value: taken from the repository or CONTEXT_PRESS_STAMP_01.md (catalog limits, simulation equations, topics, runbook stubs, tests). |
|---|---|
| [D] | Derived value: computed from the repository's own simulation model (seed 1, 2 Hz, 600 s per case) or algebraically from its equations, as recorded in the context file. |
| [E] | Engineering reference: general industrial practice for press drives, lubrication circuits and vibration diagnostics. Not a manufacturer value and not taken from the repository. |
| [I] | Illustrative / proposed prototype value: chosen by the authors for this knowledge base and meant to be refined with real plant data. |

Important: the telemetry for this machine is simulated. There is no physical press or transducer. An ESP32 gateway (or a software simulator) plays the press controller and generates values from documented equations. The repository describes its limits as illustrative constants chosen for the demo, not vendor values, and its runbooks as not an OEM manual. Values tagged [P] are therefore prototype values, not OEM specifications; values tagged [E] and [I] are not manufacturer-certified.

chunks.section: 1. Fault History Status and Use of the Cases > 1.1 Fault history; 1.2 Reproducing the project cases; 1.3 Case record format
chunks.text:
There are no recorded incidents, work orders, failure dates or repair records for press-stamp-01 in the repository, and stored telemetry expires after 48 h [P]. Every case in this document is a simulated or illustrative scenario. No case is a real plant event, and none may be cited as failure statistics.

Table 1. Basis of the cases
| Basis | Tag | Cases | How the numbers were obtained |
|---|---|---|---|
| Repository simulation (CLOGGED_FILTER, BEARING_WEAR) | [P] / [D] | C01 to C06, C15 to C18 | Equations and the 600 s derived tables of the context file; linear fits within about 0.05 mm/s for vibration means between tabulated r values |
| Illustrative scenarios of faults not modelled in the repository | [I] | C07 to C14 | Qualitative signatures from engineering practice with illustrative values, labelled in each case |

The simulator is seeded and can be accelerated. Cases C01 to C06 can be re-created with node server/scripts/simulate-devices.mjs --machines press-stamp-01 --scenario CLOGGED_FILTER --ramp 120 (or BEARING_WEAR), with --seed and --speed as needed, or from the Faults tab (needs ENABLE_DEVICE_COMMANDS true) or cmd/scenario [P]. The scenario and ramp are published only in diag.sim and served only by GET /devices/:machineId/sim; the case reasoning below uses channel evidence only [P].

Table 2. The 16 elements of every case
| # | Element | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Case ID | C01 to C18 |
| 2 | Machine state | Operating and gateway state |
| 3 | Sensor readings and pattern | Values and shape |
| 4 | Baseline | Healthy reference |
| 5 | Threshold comparison | Level against Document 01 |
| 6 | Symptoms | What an operator would notice |
| 7 | Candidate faults | From Document 03 step 8 |

| 9 | Evidence against alternatives | Why others are rejected |

| 12 | Recommended inspection | Document 04 task |
| 13 | Corrective action | Action |
| 14 | Expected post-maintenance telemetry | Values |
| 15 | Verification | Criteria |
| 16 | Basis | Tag and source |

| Candidate faults | F01 CLOGGED_FILTER, F16, F03, F04, F12, F02 |

chunks.text:
Table 21. C17: case record
| Element | Description |
|---|---|
| Case ID | C17 |
| Machine state | Running; data valid; ramp 600 s (the longest allowed) so changes are one fifth of the default speed |
| Sensor readings and pattern | Slopes of the 60 s means: P60 -0.20 bar/min, V60 +0.37 mm/s/min, I60 +0.28 A/min [D]; HB300 rises gradually from 0.03 mm/s |
| Baseline | P60 4.50 bar, V60 1.31 mm/s |
| Threshold comparison | V60 reaches Watch (1.50) at about 30 s, V60 2.5 at about 198 s, P60 3.6 bar at about 266 s, alarm limits at about 444 s [D] |
| Symptoms | None for several minutes; a low pressure reading later |
| Candidate faults | F01 early, F02 early, F12 |
| Evidence supporting each candidate | F01: both P60 and V60 move in the same time order; delta V / delta P about -1.8 mm/s per bar |
| Evidence against alternatives | F02 rejected (pressure falls); F12 rejected (V60 and HB300 follow) |
| Diagnostic reasoning | R-15 at 30 s, R-16 at 60 s, R-27 (P60 falls 0.3 bar in 10 minutes, here after about 90 s), R-29 estimates time to alarm from the slope |
| Final diagnosis | F01 CLOGGED_FILTER early, Medium confidence at first (score reaches High as P60 and V60 grow) |
| Recommended inspection | T1 at the next planned stop (L1 to L2) |
| Corrective action | Replace the cartridge at the next stop; the slow rate gives time to plan |
| Expected post-maintenance telemetry | As C01 |
| Verification | As C01 |
| Basis | [P][D]: times are r x 600 s |

Table 22. C18: case record
| Element | Description |
|---|---|
| Case ID | C18 |
| Machine state | Running; data valid; ramp 120 s |
| Sensor readings and pattern | V60 rises from 1.31 mm/s toward 2.89 mm/s; P60 4.50 bar; I60 rises toward 102.3 A; lines grow [P][D] |
| Baseline | V60 1.31 mm/s |
| Threshold comparison | Feature rule: V60 Watch at about 14 s (r about 0.12). Platform: first samples at or over 2.5 mm/s at about 72 s (r 0.6), over it most of the time from about 96 s (r 0.8), alarm never |
| Symptoms | Gradual noise |
| Candidate faults | F02, F10, F11 |
| Evidence supporting each candidate | F02: lines, P normal, dI/dV about 4.8 |
| Evidence against alternatives | F01 rejected (P normal) |
| Diagnostic reasoning | R-15 at 14 s, R-21, R-18 once the lines pass 4 x healthy |
| Final diagnosis | F02 BEARING_WEAR, High confidence once lines are present |
| Recommended inspection | T2 at the next planned stop |
| Corrective action | Plan replacement; the feature rule gives about 58 s of lead at the default ramp (about 288 s at 600 s) over the first platform warning [D] |
| Expected post-maintenance telemetry | As C03 |
| Verification | Section 14 |
| Basis | [P][D]; planned evaluation measure: detection lead time against a threshold-alarm baseline, which never fires for bearing wear [P] |

Table 26. Time to key events for ramp durations [D]
| Event (r) | 30 s ramp | 60 s ramp | 120 s ramp | 300 s ramp | 600 s ramp |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Clog V60 Watch (0.05) | 2 s | 3 s | 6 s | 15 s | 30 s |

chunks.section: 7. Lessons and Summary > 7.1 Lessons from the cases; 7.2 Key thresholds; 7.3 Safety and escalation notes; 7.4 References and engineering basis; 7.5 Revision notes
chunks.text:
• The vibration RMS alone cannot separate the two simulated faults (C15): use the pressure and the

spectrum shape.

• A threshold alarm alone misses bearing wear (C03, C04): use trend and shape [P].

• Window-based rules stop alarm flicker (C05) and rule out spikes (C11).

• Sensor and data checks come first (C08, C09, C14); a pressure alarm without a vibration response

is a sensor suspect.

• When the evidence is mixed, lubrication first (C07, C13) [P].

• Always verify against the baseline after a repair (C16).

Table 31. Key thresholds used in the cases
| Quantity | Value | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| V warn / alarm / critical | 2.5 / 4.0 / 7.0 mm/s | [P] / [P] / [I] |
| P warn / alarm / critical | 3.6 / 3.0 / 2.5 bar | [P] / [P] / [I] |
| I warn / alarm / critical | 175 / 195 / 220 A | [P] / [P] / [I] |
| Verification band | P60 4.35 to 4.65 bar; V60 1.20 to 1.45 mm/s | [P] / [I] |
| Margin rule | 4 clear, 2 to 3 ambiguous, 0 to 1 unresolved | [I] |

The cases are simulated or illustrative and are not plant history. This document is a capstone prototype, not an OEM manual. Follow the manufacturer's procedure and apply lock-out and tag-out before opening the lubrication circuit or the main drive. The agent cannot act on the machine.

• CONTEXT_PRESS_STAMP_01.md; the simulator equations and derived tables; docs/demo-script.md

for the C02 timeline; the two press runbooks [P].

• Cases C07 to C14 and the fail variant of C16 are illustrative engineering examples [I].

Table 32. Revision history
| Rev | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | 2026-10-08 | First issue |

chunks.section: 1. Document Control and Retrieval Guide > 1.1 Role of this document in the knowledge base
chunks.text:
This is the reference for normal and abnormal values of Sensor 1. Retrieve it first when the question is whether a value, a window of values or a trend is acceptable. It contains the project limits as declared by the machine, the derived healthy signature, the engineering-reference extensions needed for diagnosis (watch, early-degradation and critical levels, feature thresholds, rate-of-change classes), the persistence and escalation rules, and the sensor limitations that can make a reading misleading.

Naming is fixed across the five documents: Sensor 1 = AXIS_4_SERVO_TORQUE = axis 4 servo torque, measured in Nm. The component is the robot forearm (axis 4): the axis 4 servo drive and gearbox. The only fault scenario in the repository for this machine is GEARBOX_WEAR, and Sensor 1 is its primary indicator.

Table 1. Question-to-section map for retrieval
| Typical agent question | Answer location | Key numbers |
|---|---|---|
| Is this torque reading normal? | Sections 4, 5, 15 | Healthy sample range about 3 to 23 Nm; cycle peak 21.75 Nm [D] |
| What value triggers a warning or an alarm? | Sections 6, 7, 16 | warnHigh 26 Nm, alarmHigh 30 Nm [P]; proposed critical 34 Nm [I] |
| Is the machine drifting before any limit is crossed? | Sections 7, 8 | Cycle mean above 13.5 Nm = watch; harmonic A6 above 0.4 Nm [I] |
| How long may an abnormal value persist? | Sections 9, 16 | Peak-envelope rule: 2 cycles (16 s) to open, 2 cycles to clear [I] |
| Is this spike a transient? | Sections 8, 9 | Healthy step between samples up to about 7 Nm in 0.5 s [D] |
| What can legitimately change the reading? | Sections 10, 11 | Operating state, speed override, payload, temperature [E] |
| Can the sensor itself be wrong? | Section 12 | Value is a controller estimate; accuracy not specified [P] |
| What does this imply diagnostically? | Section 17 | GEARBOX_WEAR signature; see Documents 02 to 05 |

chunks.section: 3. Measurement Principle and Units > 3.1 What the value physically represents; 3.2 Units and encoding
chunks.text:
The repository treats the value as a controller-internal state, not a bolt-on transducer. In a real plant a robot controller computes axis torque from motor phase current (torque is approximately the motor torque constant multiplied by the quadrature-axis current, multiplied by the gear ratio and gearbox efficiency) and publishes it through OPC UA or MTConnect to a gateway [E]. In this project the ESP32 gateway generates the number from an equation that stands in for that controller. The measurement principle is therefore documented in two layers: the simulated generation law [P] and the engineering reality it imitates [E].

• Unit: Newton-metre (Nm). The value is the torque requested of axis 4 by the drive, positive in the

model throughout (the catalog clamp floor is 0 Nm, so negative torque is not represented) [P].

• Encoding: one decimal place in the telemetry message field m.AXIS_4_SERVO_TORQUE, for

example 17.5. Quantisation is therefore 0.1 Nm, small compared with the healthy noise standard deviation of 0.45 Nm [P][D].

• Sampling: one value every 500 ms. The cycle (8 s) is sampled 16 times. The highest frequency that

can be observed is 1 Hz (Nyquist), so the fourth harmonic (0.5 Hz) and the sixth harmonic (0.75 Hz) are observable but anything faster, such as gear-mesh frequency, is not [D][E].

• Timestamps: epoch ms from the gateway clock; if synced is false or the stamp is more than two

minutes from server time, the backend stamps its own receive time, which blurs the cycle phase [P].

Table 4. Generation law for NORMAL operation
| Term | Expression | Meaning | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mean torque | 13.0 Nm | Average load on axis 4 over the cycle | [P] |
| Fundamental | 7.0 sin(2 pi p), p = (t mod 8 s)/8 s | Once-per-cycle swing from the forearm moving through its stroke (0.125 Hz) | [P] |
| Fourth harmonic | 2.2 sin(8 pi p) | Four-times-per-cycle component (0.5 Hz) | [P] |
| Noise | 0.45 x Gaussian | Standard deviation 0.45 Nm | [P] |
| Clamp | 0 to 45 Nm | Values outside are limited | [P] |

chunks.section: 4. Healthy Operating Signature > 4.1 Waveform of one weld cycle; 4.2 Harmonic content
chunks.text:
Healthy torque is a repeating 8 s waveform. It has a noise-free minimum of 4.25 Nm, a noise-free maximum of 21.75 Nm at about 2.4 s into the cycle (phase about 0.30), a cycle mean of 13.0 Nm and noise of 0.45 Nm standard deviation [D]. The weld window (4.4 to 6.0 s) falls in the low-torque part of the cycle: noise-free torque there lies between 4.2 and 12.9 Nm with a mean of 7.4 Nm [D]. Therefore limit crossings caused by gearbox wear appear before the weld window, not during it.

Figure 1. Noise-free torque over one 8 s cycle for healthy operation and two fault severities, with the project limits [D].

Table 5. Phase-resolved torque, noise-free (Nm) [D]
| Time in cycle (s) | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Healthy (r = 0) | 13.0 | 17.9 | 20.0 | 17.9 | 13.0 | 8.1 | 6.0 | 8.1 |
| Fault severity 0.5 | 18.2 | 21.7 | 25.2 | 24.7 | 18.2 | 11.8 | 11.2 | 14.8 |
| Fault severity 1.0 | 23.5 | 25.4 | 30.5 | 31.4 | 23.5 | 15.6 | 16.5 | 21.6 |
| Weld gun state | off | off | off | off | off (on from 4.4) | on | on to 6.0 | off |

The healthy signal contains exactly two deterministic components: the cycle fundamental (7.0 Nm at 0.125 Hz) and the fourth harmonic (2.2 Nm at 0.5 Hz). Any energy at the sixth harmonic (0.75 Hz) is absent in a healthy axis and is the cleanest early indicator of gear-mesh damage in this dataset. See Figure 1 in Document 02 for the spectrum by severity.

Table 6. Healthy spectral lines of Sensor 1
| Line | Frequency | Amplitude (Nm) | Healthy? | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mean (DC) | 0 | 13.0 | Yes | [P] |
| 1x cycle | 0.125 Hz | 7.0 | Yes | [P] |
| 4x cycle | 0.5 Hz | 2.2 | Yes | [P] |
| 6x cycle | 0.75 Hz | 0 (estimator floor 0.1 to 0.2 with noise) | Absent when healthy | [D] |
| Broadband noise | all | sigma 0.45 | Yes | [P] |

chunks.section: 6. Threshold System > 6.1 Project limits and what they mean; 6.2 Five-level threshold model used by this knowledge base
chunks.text:
The machine declares two upper limits in its birth message: warnHigh 26 Nm and alarmHigh 30 Nm [P]. A sample is classified warn when its value reaches 26 Nm and alarm when it reaches 30 Nm (comparison is greater-than-or-equal; alarm wins over warn). No low limits are declared for this channel, so a low torque is never flagged by the platform. The classification is applied to each sample independently, with no hysteresis, delay or latching [P].

Consequence for interpretation: because the signal is cyclic and the limits are per sample, status flickers once per cycle and the marker is not steady. The warning limit is crossed only near the cycle peak (about 2 to 3.5 s into the cycle). Persistence must therefore be judged on the per-cycle peak envelope, not on consecutive raw samples.

The task of a diagnostic agent needs more levels than the two the machine declares. The levels below keep the project warn and alarm limits unchanged and add a lower limit, a watch level and a critical level around them. Each level states what it means and what must be done.

Table 10. Threshold definitions for Sensor 1 torque (per sample)
| Level | Value (Nm) | Basis | Meaning | Required response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lower limit / minimum | 0 (clamp floor); expected healthy minimum 3.1 | [P][D] | Below 3.0 Nm in production cycle is outside the healthy envelope | Treat as possible sensor or signal fault; see Section 12 and Document 02 (sensor faults) |
| Normal | 3.1 to 23.1 | [D] | Healthy production cycle | None |
| Watch (advisory) | 23.2 to 25.9, or feature watch levels in Section 7 | [D][I] | Above anything a healthy axis produces but below the warn limit | Flag, increase trend monitoring, compare with baseline |
| Warning | 26.0 to 29.9 | [P] | warnHigh reached; status warn, amber on twin | Open investigation, schedule inspection at next planned stop |
| Alarm | 30.0 to 33.9 | [P] | alarmHigh reached; status alarm, red pulsing on twin | Intervention required; reduce duty, plan stop, do not run to failure |
| Critical | 34.0 and above, or alarm persisting beyond escalation time | [I] | Above the full-severity peak of the modeled fault (32.3 Nm) plus noise margin; outside the modeled envelope | Immediate escalation; stop at a safe point; specialist inspection |
| Catalog maximum | 45 | [P] | Values clamp here | Any sustained value near 45 Nm implies saturation or sensor fault |

chunks.section: 6. Threshold System > 6.3 Why 34 Nm is proposed as the critical threshold
chunks.text: The modeled fault saturates at a noise-free peak of 32.28 Nm at severity 1 [D]. Adding three noise standard deviations at full severity (3 x 1.125 = 3.4 Nm) to the plateau of the worst case gives about 35.7 Nm as an extreme sample; a threshold of 34 Nm is crossed by roughly the upper tail of full-severity cycles (the 95th percentile of the per-cycle peak is 33.4 Nm [D]). A sample at or above 34 Nm therefore indicates a cycle at or beyond the maximum modeled severity and is the proposed trigger for immediate escalation [I]. If the real robot has a rated or peak torque for axis 4, that figure replaces this proposal.

chunks.section: 7. Feature-Based Thresholds
chunks.text:
Sample limits alone detect wear late: the warning limit is only reached at severity 0.48, when the cycle mean has already risen by 5 Nm. The agent should therefore compute four window features and compare them with the thresholds below. Features are evaluated over a window of at least one full cycle (16 samples) and preferably five cycles (40 s, 80 samples) aligned to the 8 s cycle [I]. Severity index S = (M - 13.0) / 10.5 converts a cycle mean M into the equivalent fault severity; it is computed from telemetry and must not be confused with the simulator ground truth, which is hidden from the agent [D].

Table 11. Feature thresholds for Sensor 1 (5-cycle window)
| Feature | Healthy | Watch | Early degradation | Warning-eq uivalent | Alarm-equiv alent | Critical-equi valent | Unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cycle mean M | 12.5 to 13.5 | 13.5 to 15.0 | 15.0 to 18.0 | 18.0 to 21.6 | 21.6 to 23.5 | 23.5 and above | Nm |
| Severity index S | -0.05 to 0.05 | 0.05 to 0.19 | 0.19 to 0.48 | 0.48 to 0.82 | 0.82 to 1.0 | 1.0 and above | - |
| Cycle minimum (mean of per-cycle sample minimum) | about 4.3 | 5.0 to 6.5 | 6.5 to 10.0 | 10.0 to 13.2 | 13.2 to 15.0 | 15.0 and above | Nm |
| Mean of per-cycle sample peak | 21.7 | 22.5 to 23.5 | 23.5 to 26.0 | 26.0 to 29.7 | 29.7 to 32.0 | 32.0 and above | Nm |
| Sixth-harmonic amplitude A6 | 0 to 0.2 | 0.4 to 0.6 | 0.6 to 1.5 | 1.5 to 2.5 | 2.5 to 3.0 | 3.0 and above | Nm |
| Noise standard deviation (after removing mean and cycle template) | 0.40 to 0.55 | 0.55 to 0.62 | 0.62 to 0.77 | 0.77 to 1.0 | 1.0 to 1.125 | 1.125 and above | Nm |
| Fraction of cycles with a sample at or above 26 Nm | 0 percent | 0 percent | 0 to 9 percent | 41 to 100 percent | 100 percent | 100 percent | - |
| Fraction of cycles with a sample at or above 30 Nm | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 to 5 percent | 31 to 100 percent | 100 percent | - |

The feature bands are derived from the model equations at severity values 0.05, 0.19, 0.48, 0.82 and 1.0 [D]; the boundaries between bands are proposals [I]. The bands overlap in meaning, not in value: M is the most robust single feature because noise averages out (standard deviation 0.05 Nm over five cycles), A6 is the most specific because it is absent in a healthy axis, and the peak-based features connect directly to the project limits.

chunks.section: 8. Rate-of-Change Limits
chunks.text:
Two different rates matter. The within-cycle rate is the normal motion of the robot and must not be mistaken for a fault. The trend rate is the speed at which a feature (mean, A6, noise) moves from one window to the next and carries the diagnostic meaning.

Table 13. Within-cycle rate of change (noise included, 2 Hz samples) [D]
| Condition | Maximum noise-free slope (Nm/s) | 99th percentile step per 0.5 s (Nm) | Maximum observed step per 0.5 s (Nm) | Standard deviation of step (Nm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Healthy | 12.4 | 5.8 | 7.2 | 3.0 |
| Severity 0.5 | 19.5 | not computed | not computed | - |
| Severity 1.0 | 26.5 | 11.7 | 14.5 | 5.1 |

IF a single sample-to-sample step exceeds 8 Nm AND the next sample returns to within 6 Nm of the cycle template for that phase THEN classify it as a transient or glitch; IF steps larger than 8 Nm occur repeatedly at the same cycle phase over 3 consecutive cycles THEN treat as a recurring feature of the process and evaluate it against Section 9.

Table 14. Trend rate of change of cycle mean M: interpretation classes
| Class | Rate of M | Time to move 1 Nm | Typical meaning | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Step change | 1 Nm or more within one cycle (8 s) | at most 8 s | Process change, payload change, program change, collision, brake or enable event, sensor offset; not gradual wear | [E] |
| Fast ramp | 0.05 to 1 Nm per minute | 1 to 20 min | Simulator fault injection with rampSec 5 to 120 s (0.0875 Nm/s at 120 s equals 5.25 Nm per min); real-world analogue is acute damage or lubrication loss | [D][E] |
| Slow ramp | 0.5 to 5 Nm per hour | 12 min to 2 h | Fast-developing degradation; simulator rampSec 600 s is 1.05 Nm per min | [D][E] |
| Gradual drift | 0.02 to 0.5 Nm per day | 2 to 50 days | Typical progressive gearbox wear in operation | [E][I] |
| Seasonal or thermal | less than 0.5 Nm per hour, reversible | - | Warm-up or ambient dependence, returns when conditions return | [E] |

Simulator ramp arithmetic [D]: the mean rises by 10.5 Nm over rampSec, so dM/dt = 10.5 / rampSec. For rampSec = 120 s this is 0.0875 Nm/s; for 600 s it is 0.0175 Nm/s; for 5 s it is 2.1 Nm/s. With the default ramp the first warn peak appears after about 58 s and the first alarm peak after about 98 s [D].

chunks.section: 9. Transient and Sustained Behaviour > 9.1 Normal transient behaviour; 9.2 Sustained abnormal behaviour
chunks.text:
Table 15. Expected transient behaviour of Sensor 1
| Transient | Typical appearance | Duration | Normal? | How to recognise |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cycle peak | Rise to about 21.75 Nm at about 2.4 s | about 1 s above 20 Nm | Yes | Repeats every 8 s at the same phase |
| Weld window trough | Fall to about 4 to 8 Nm near 5 to 6.5 s | about 2 s | Yes | Coincides with gun energised 4.4 to 6.0 s |
| Noise spike | Single sample 2 to 3 sigma (0.9 to 1.4 Nm) away from template | 1 sample (0.5 s) | Yes | Next sample returns; template residual only |
| Isolated large outlier | Residual above 2.5 Nm (about 5.5 sigma) in one sample | 1 sample | Not expected in the model | Treat as glitch if isolated; see Section 12 |
| Start of fault injection | Mean starts to rise from the baseline, ripple appears | seconds to minutes | No | Not a transient; it is the onset of GEARBOX_WEAR |
| Return to NORMAL after reset | Mean returns to 13.0 Nm at once | one cycle | Yes after command NORMAL or reboot | Ack message shows scenario NORMAL |
| Telemetry gap | Missing samples, seq jumps | seconds | Link issue, not a torque effect | seq gaps counted as packet loss; new bootId with seq 0 is a reboot |

Table 16. Sustained abnormal patterns and thresholds for persistence [I]
| Pattern | Detection test | Minimum persistence to classify | Classification |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mean shift | M above 13.5 Nm | 5 cycles (40 s) simulator; 1 week real [I] | Baseline shift; evaluate fault candidates |
| Warning peaks | Per-cycle peak at or above 26 Nm | 2 consecutive cycles (16 s) | Warning condition opened |
| Alarm peaks | Per-cycle peak at or above 30 Nm | 2 consecutive cycles (16 s) | Alarm condition opened |
| Critical sample | Any sample at or above 34 Nm | 1 sample, confirmed by the next cycle | Critical escalation |
| Ripple present | A6 at or above 0.4 Nm over 5 cycles | 5 cycles (40 s) | Gear-mesh ripple confirmed |
| Clearing | Peak envelope below limit minus 1 Nm | 2 consecutive cycles (16 s) | Condition cleared (hysteresis) |

The planned Phase 5 detector in the repository uses a 10 s dwell for threshold opening and clearing, a rolling z-score above 3 for 30 s for drift, a sustained positive slope of the 60 s mean over 10 minutes, and a 10 minute cooldown with one open investigation per machine [P, planned, not built]. Since the 8 s cycle means that raw samples above the limit appear for at most about 1.4 s per cycle even at full severity [D], a dwell of 10 s on raw samples would never be satisfied. The proposal above applies the same dwell to the per-cycle peak envelope: two cycles is 16 s, which is consistent with the repository's intention of a 10 s dwell.

The planned Phase 5 detector in the repository uses a 10 s dwell for threshold opening and clearing, a rolling z-score above 3 for 30 s for drift, a sustained positive slope of the 60 s mean over 10 minutes, and a 10 minute cooldown with one open investigation per machine [P, planned, not built]. Since the 8 s cycle means that raw samples above the limit appear for at most about 1.4 s per cycle even at full severity [D], a dwell of 10 s on raw samples would never be satisfied. The proposal above applies the same dwell to the per-cycle peak envelope: two cycles is 16 s, which is consistent with the repository's intention of a 10 s dwell.

chunks.section: 10. Operating States and Load-Dependent Behaviour
chunks.text:
The repository simulator has no idle, startup or shutdown state: whenever the gateway is online, the 8 s weld cycle runs continuously and the Gaussian noise is always present. The states below are engineering-reference extensions [E] that the agent needs when interpreting a real robot, and each is marked as not modeled by the simulator. A diagnostic conclusion must never be drawn from torque in a state other than production cycle without applying the correction in this table.

Table 17. Operating-state comparison
| State | Description | Sensor 1 behaviour | Typical level (Nm) | Use for diagnosis? | Modeled in repository ? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Production cycle (steady) | 8 s weld cycle at programmed speed and payload | 8 s waveform with mean 13.0, swing 7.0, harmonic 2.2 | 3 to 23 healthy | Yes: the reference state for every threshold | Yes [P] |
| Warm-up (first minutes or first cycles after long stop) | Grease cold, higher viscous friction | Mean shifted up, relaxing over minutes [E] | +0.5 to +1.5 Nm above steady mean [I] | Only after warm-up | No |
| Idle, servo enabled, stationary | Axis holds posture against gravity | Nearly constant value equal to holding torque of the posture; low noise | Posture dependent, illustrative 2 to 8 [I] | No (cycle features undefined) | No |
| Brake engaged / servo off | Holding by mechanical brake | Torque about 0 or not reported | 0 | No | No |
| Jog or teach | Manual slow motion | Irregular, not cyclic, low speed | 0 to 15 [I] | No | No |
| Speed override below 100 percent | Production at reduced speed | Same shape stretched in time, lower dynamic component, same gravity component [E] | Peak lower than 21.75 | Only with scaling by speed | No |
| Payload or tool change | Different forearm payload | Mean and swing change, ripple does not appear [E] | Mean shift of several Nm | Re-baseline | No |
| Fault state GEARBOX_WEAR | Ramp r from 0 to 1 | Mean +10.5 r, ripple 3.0 r at 0.75 Hz, noise x (1 + 1.5 r) | mean 13.0 to 23.5 | Yes | Yes [P] |
| Gateway offline / stale | No telemetry for max(5 s, 4 x interval) | No data | - | No | Yes [P] |

chunks.section: 10. Operating States and Load-Dependent Behaviour > 10.1 Startup and shutdown behaviour; 10.2 Load dependence
chunks.text:
• Gateway startup (modeled): the board connects to Wi-Fi, synchronises its clock by SNTP, publishes

birth, status online and then telemetry. The first telemetry messages may carry synced false and be stamped by the server on receipt. Do not compute cycle-aligned features until at least one full cycle (8 s) of synced samples exists [P].

• Robot startup (not modeled): after power-up and brake release the axis holds posture; treat the

first production cycle after enable as warm-up and exclude it from baseline [E].

• Shutdown (modeled at gateway level): a power cut produces status offline about 15 s later through

the Last Will; the last samples before that must not be read as a drop in torque [P].

• Stop at end of cycle (not modeled): torque falls to the holding value and the cyclic features

disappear. A flat trace close to the holding torque is idle, not a failed sensor, if the status is online and the robot program is not running [E].

Axis 4 torque scales with the mass carried beyond the axis, the acceleration of the motion and the orientation of the axis relative to gravity [E]. In the simulator the load is fixed, and therefore the mean of 13.0 Nm and the cycle swing of 7.0 Nm are constants of the healthy baseline. On a real machine a payload change shifts the mean and the swing in proportion, whereas gearbox wear shifts the mean and adds the ripple but does not change the swing amplitude (the 7.0 Nm fundamental is unchanged in the model [D]). The agent should therefore use the pair mean-shift plus ripple, not mean-shift alone, to attribute a change to wear.

Table 18. Load-dependent interpretation
| Change in operating load | Effect on mean M | Effect on cycle swing | Effect on A6 | Effect on noise | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Heavier tool or payload [E] | Up in proportion | Up in proportion | None | Little | Process change, not wear |
| Higher speed or acceleration [E] | Little | Up (dynamic part) | None | Little | Program change |
| Lower speed override [E] | Little | Down | None | Little | Operator action |
| GEARBOX_WEAR [P] | Up by 10.5 r | Unchanged (7.0) | Up by 3.0 r | Up by factor 1 + 1.5 r | Fault |

chunks.section: 11. Environmental Influences
chunks.text:
The repository models no environmental effect on torque: WELD_GUN_TEMP has an ambient of 32 degC but it does not feed back into the torque equation and GEARBOX_WEAR does not change gun temperature [P]. The influences below describe what a real robot would show and how to avoid misreading it [E].

Table 19. Environmental and operational influences on Sensor 1
| Influence | Mechanism | Direction and size [E][I] | Reversible? | Diagnostic handling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ambient temperature (cold start) | Grease viscosity raises friction | +0.5 to +1.5 Nm for a cold gearbox | Yes, within minutes of running | Exclude warm-up cycles |
| Sustained high ambient or hot weld cell | Thinner lubricant, thermal expansion of gear backlash | Small decrease in friction, possible increase of ripple at high wear | Yes | Compare at similar temperature |
| Gun temperature (weld heat radiation) | Heat near flange and wrist | Negligible on axis 4 torque [E] | Yes | Use gun temperature only to exclude a thermal event, as in the simulator |
| Supply voltage dip | Drive limits current, torque estimate clipped or noisy | Dips in torque reading during acceleration | Yes | Cross-check drive fault log |
| Contamination (spatter, dust) | Cable dressing or seal drag | Slow rise of mean and noise | No (needs cleaning) | Inspect dress pack and seals |
| Humidity and washdown | Seal degradation, corrosion | Long-term | No | Inspect seals |
| Vibration from adjacent equipment (press) | Mechanical coupling through floor | Added noise at low frequency | Yes | Check whether the press is running |
| Payload / tooling change | Mass change | Mean and swing change | Yes | Re-baseline after the change |
| Program or path change | Different accelerations | Waveform shape changes | Yes | Use program ID in context |

chunks.section: 12. Sensor Limitations and Measurement Uncertainty > 12.1 Limitations; 12.2 Measurement uncertainty
chunks.text:
• Not an independent transducer: the number is computed inside the controller (modeled by an

equation). A failure of the drive, of the current measurement or of the controller model biases the reading without any mechanical cause [E].

• Torque is an estimate, not a gear-tooth measurement: gear-mesh frequencies and bearing defect

frequencies are far above the 1 Hz observable limit at 2 Hz sampling, so only low-order cycle harmonics are visible [D][E].

• Per-sample limits and a cyclic signal: a sample crosses a limit only at the cycle peak, so severity

must be inferred from features rather than from the proportion of time in warn [D].

• Quantisation of 0.1 Nm, noise 0.45 Nm healthy, clamp at 0 and 45 Nm: saturation hides values

above 45 Nm [P].

• Cycle phase is not published: the agent must infer the phase from the 8 s periodicity or from the

weld gun trace; using server receive time instead of gateway time degrades alignment [P].

• Accuracy, calibration, rated torque and gear ratio are not specified in the repository [P].

Table 20. Uncertainty budget for Sensor 1 features [D][E]
| Quantity | Source | 1 sigma | Effect on diagnosis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Single sample | Noise | 0.45 Nm healthy, 1.125 Nm at full severity | Single sample can differ from the template by about 1 Nm; do not diagnose from one sample |
| Quantisation | 1 decimal | 0.03 Nm (0.1 / sqrt(12)) | Negligible |
| Cycle mean over 1 cycle | 16 samples | 0.11 Nm (healthy), 0.28 Nm (full severity) | Detects 1 Nm shifts with about 9 sigma confidence |
| Cycle mean over 5 cycles | 80 samples | 0.05 Nm (healthy) | Detects shifts of 0.3 Nm (S 0.03) |
| A6 over 1 cycle | 16 samples | estimator floor 0.20 mean, 95th percentile 0.39 Nm (healthy) | Reliable only above 0.4 Nm |
| A6 over 5 cycles | 80 samples | floor 0.09, 95th percentile 0.18 Nm (healthy) | Reliable above 0.2 Nm |
| Gateway clock and phase | SNTP, receive time fallback | unspecified | Phase error blurs A6; use gateway ts when synced true |
| Real-sensor accuracy | Controller estimate | Not specified in repository (engineering assumption of 2 to 5 percent of rated torque [E]) | Add margin to thresholds on a real robot |

chunks.section: 13. Baseline Establishment and Data Quality > 13.1 Building the healthy baseline
chunks.text:
Every feature threshold in this document is anchored to the healthy baseline of the specific robot. In the simulator the baseline is known exactly; on a real robot it must be measured. The procedure below is the engineering-reference method [E][I] and is also what the diagnostic agent should apply when a baseline record is requested.

Table 21. Baseline procedure
| Step | Action | Acceptance criterion | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Confirm gateway status online, synced true, no seq gaps in the window | No gap longer than 2 intervals (1 s); synced true on every message | Clean window |
| 2 | Confirm production cycle at 100 percent speed override, payload unchanged, warm-up complete | At least 3 cycles since warm-up (about 24 s in the simulator, 15 to 30 min on a real robot [E]) | Valid operating state |
| 3 | Collect at least 20 consecutive cycles (160 s, 320 samples) | Cycle length 8.0 s within 1 percent | Baseline sample set |
| 4 | Fold samples by cycle phase into 16 bins of 0.5 s and compute the mean per bin | Bin mean standard error below 0.15 Nm (sigma 0.45 / sqrt 20) | Cycle template |
| 5 | Compute baseline M, per-cycle peak, per-cycle minimum, noise sigma (residual to template), A6 (projection onto the 6th harmonic) | M within 12.5 to 13.5 Nm and A6 below 0.2 Nm for the simulated robot | Baseline feature vector |
| 6 | Store baseline with timestamp, program ID and payload | - | Baseline record |

For the simulated robot the expected baseline is M = 13.0 Nm, template peak 21.75 Nm at 2.4 s, minimum 4.25 Nm, sigma 0.45 Nm and A6 near 0 [D]. If a measured baseline differs materially from these values, either the robot is not in the NORMAL scenario (a fault may already be injected) or the sample window is not in the healthy state.
