chunks.section: 11. Fault-Specific Diagnostic Checklists
chunks.text:
Table 26. Checklist: confirm, refute and decisive test per fault
| Fault | Confirm when all hold | Refute when any holds | Decisive test |
|---|---|---|---|
| F01 gearbox wear | dM at least 1 Nm; A6 at least 0.4 and A6/dM 0.2 to 0.4; kN near 1 + 0.143 dM; dTCP positive; swing unchanged; gun unchanged; ramp onset | Idle offset large; swing changed; M reversible with temperature; A6 below 0.2 with dM above 3 | Oil particles, backlash |
| F02 lubrication | dM at least 1; A6 below 0.4; larger when cold; idle offset small | A6/dM above 0.2; metal in oil | Lubricant condition and warm/cold comparison |
| F03 brake drag | Idle offset at least 1 Nm; mean up; A6 absent; brake warm | Idle offset absent; brake cool | Brake voltage and release timing |
| F04 bearing | Noise rise with sparse spikes; A6 low; dM small | Clear 0.75 Hz line; no spikes | Bearing play, temperature |
| F05 looseness | Spikes at the same 1 or 2 phases; dTCP high relative to dM | Mean shift above 3 Nm with ripple | Fastener torque, backlash |
| F06 external drag | Bump in one phase window; rest unchanged | Whole-cycle shift | Dress pack check |
| F07 overload/collision | Step or spike; swing changed (payload) or TCP step (collision) | Gradual ramp with ripple | Visual, tool data, event log |
| F08 drive fault | Offset at idle; no TCP change; non-harmonic lines | Brake warm; TCP changed | Drive diagnostics |
| F09 thermal | M follows temperature; reversible | Irreversible shift | Temperature trend |
| F10 program change | Step at program boundary; shape change | No program change | Program log |
| F11 sensor fault | Flat, clipped or burst; other channels normal | Periodic cycle present | Raw gateway log |
| F12 data path | Gaps, stale, synced false, all channels | Complete data | Gateway diag |

chunks.section: 12. Reporting, Concurrent Faults and Alert Classification > 12.1 Alert classification table; 12.2 Concurrent faults and conflicting evidence; 12.3 Questions the agent may ask when context is missing
chunks.text:
Table 27. Alert classification
| Leve l | Name | Trigger | Twin appearance (project behaviour) | Agent behaviour | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L0 | Normal | Features healthy | Normal tint | Log | None |
| L1 | Watch | M 13.5 to 15.0 or A6 0.4 to 0.6 | Normal tint (no platform state) | Note in report; no alert | Trend |
| L2 | Warning | Peak at least 26 for 2 cycles | Amber tint #d98400 steady; triangle marker | Open investigation | Inspect at next stop |
| L3 | Alarm | Peak at least 30 for 2 cycles | Red tint #b3261e pulsing; square marker; status message | Investigation with intervention | Intervene in shift |
| L4 | Critical | Sample at least 34, M at least 23.5, alarm over 10 min | Same as alarm; agent highlight planned | Escalate | Immediate |
| LS | Sensor suspect | Flat, clipped, or noisy signal | Marker unchanged | Data-path report | Check path |

• Superposition: when a step change and a ramp occur together, explain and subtract the step first

(F10 or F07), then re-evaluate the residual drift for A6 and noise.

• Conflicting channels: if TCP is high but Sensor 1 is normal, evaluate F05 (looseness) and mastering

errors before wear; if Sensor 1 is high but TCP and A6 are normal, favour F02, F03, F09.

• A fault can mask another: an offset fault (F08, F11) shifts M and can make wear appear more

severe; check idle offset before computing S.

• Never combine the severity of a data fault with a mechanical fault into one score; report them

separately.

Table 28. Clarifying questions
| Missing information | Question | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Operating state | Is the robot in production at full speed and warmed up? | Gates the thresholds |
| Program | Was the program, payload or tool changed in the last shift? | Distinguishes F10 and F07 from wear |
| Events | Was there a collision, emergency stop or brake fault? | F07, F03 |
| Maintenance | When was axis 4 last lubricated and what grade? | F02 |
| Temperature | What are the gearbox and ambient temperatures? | F09 |
| Idle | What is the holding torque at standstill? | F03, F08 |

Example structured diagnostic report component_tag : robot_forearm_axis_4 (resolved via ROBOT-WELD-01.AXIS_4_SERVO_TORQUE; needs_binding if unbound) level : L2 warning severity: medium window : 40 s (5 cycles), synced true, 0 percent missing features : M 18.2 Nm (S 0.50), Pbar 26.1 Nm, A6 1.5 Nm, sigma 0.79 Nm, dTCP +0.27 mm diagnosis : GEARBOX_WEAR (F01) developing, stage 3 confidence: High (14 points, margin 6) evidence for : mean shift, 0.75 Hz ripple in ratio 0.29, noise ratio 1.76, TCP rise, swing unchanged, gun temperature un evidence vs : none material; F04 bearing is second (8 points) but has no spikes inspection : gearbox oil sample and magnetic plug, backlash at flange (Document 04) action : inspect at next planned stop; do not run to alarm; OEM procedure and lock-out apply verification : M 12.5 to 13.5 Nm, A6 at most 0.2 Nm, peak at most 23.1 Nm, status normal for 600 s citations : Document 01 Section 7; Document 02 F01; Document 03 R-21

Table 30. Pseudocode of the Sensor 1 diagnostic procedure def diagnose(window, ctx): if ctx.status in (offline, stale) or ctx.identity_conflict: return report_data_path() if missing_fraction(window) > 0.10: flag_incomplete() if not ctx.synced: skip(A6) if ctx.state != production_steady: return report_state_gate(ctx.state) f = features(window) # M, S, Pbar, Minbar, A6, sigma, step, dTCP, idle level = classify_level(f) # L0..L4, LS (persistence on peak envelope) if level == L0: return log_normal() pattern = classify_pattern(f) # P0..P8 score = {fault: sum(weights[e][fault] for e in evidence(f)) for fault in F01..F11} if f.sigma < 0.1: score[F11] += 4 # R-19 top, second = ranked(score)[:2] margin = score[top] - score[second] conf = confidence(score[top], margin, data_quality(window)) plan = inspections(top, second, margin) # priority table, decisive tests return report(level, pattern, top, second, conf, plan, verification_criteria(top))

chunks.section: 13. Edge Cases, False-Positive Control and Verification Runs > 13.1 Window length, false positives and detection power; 13.2 Edge cases
chunks.text:
A shorter window reacts faster but produces more false watch indications. The values below come from replicating the Sensor 1 equations with noise (300 seeded windows per case) [D]; they justify the 5-cycle default window for feature evaluation.

Table 31. Window length trade-off for the watch features [D]
| Window | M standard deviation (healthy) | A6 healthy mean / 95th percentile | A6 at S 0.1 mean | Chance a healthy window shows A6 at least 0.4 Nm | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 cycle (8 s, 16 samples) | 0.11 Nm | 0.20 / 0.39 Nm | 0.35 Nm | about 5 percent | Preliminary only; flag as low confidence |
| 5 cycles (40 s, 80 samples) | 0.05 Nm | 0.09 / 0.18 Nm | 0.30 Nm | well below 1 percent | Default feature window |
| 10 cycles (80 s, 160 samples) | 0.04 Nm | 0.07 / 0.12 Nm | 0.30 Nm | negligible | Trend confirmation; real-robot baseline |

Table 32. Edge cases and how the procedure handles them
| Situation | Risk of misdiagnosis | Handling |
|---|---|---|
| Window straddles a fault injection or a program change | Mixed statistics, false ripple | Split the window at the change point; evaluate each part |
| Gateway reboot inside window (new bootId) | Phase discontinuity | Restart window after reboot; do not compute A6 across the boundary |
| Clock not synced at start | Receive-time stamps jitter | Wait for synced true; use M, peak, sigma |
| Publish interval changed to 250 ms or 5000 ms | Wrong samples per cycle | Recompute N = 8 s / interval; skip A6 at 5000 ms |
| Per-sample status flickers between normal and warn | Operator assumes noise | Use per-cycle envelope; if M is above 15 Nm treat as persistent warning |
| Peak at 26.1 Nm but M in healthy band | Isolated outlier mistaken for wear | Require 2 consecutive cycles and M above 13.5 |
| TCP high, torque normal | Wear or mastering error assumed | Check dTCP/dM; evaluate F05 and mastering first |
| Torque high, TCP normal and A6 absent | Gearbox wear assumed | Evaluate F02, F03, F09, F08 |
| Gun temperature rising while torque normal | Wrong channel blamed | Gun temperature is not affected by GEARBOX_WEAR; evaluate the gun channel separately |
| Simulator and board both running | Identity conflict | Stop one source |
| Binding absent on the twin | No highlight | Report needs_binding; diagnosis continues |
| Retained birth message limits differ from this document | Wrong thresholds | Use the live birth limits for platform status and keep this document's feature thresholds |

chunks.section: 13. Edge Cases, False-Positive Control and Verification Runs > 13.3 Corroboration scenarios; 13.4 Verification run procedure
chunks.text:
Table 33. Torque level against corroborating channels
| Sensor 1 level | TCP rising, gun normal | TCP normal, gun normal | Gun abnormal (TCP any) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Watch (L1) | Early F01 likely; keep trending | F02, F03, F09, F10 more likely; check idle | Process or thermal event; evaluate gun first |
| Warning (L2) | F01 likely (high confidence if A6 present) | Friction family; inspect lubricant | Mixed; separate the channels |
| Alarm (L3) | F01 stage 4; intervene | Friction or overload; inspect urgently | Escalate; possible process fault |
| Critical (L4) | F01 beyond model or F07; stop | F07 collision or sensor saturation; stop | Stop; specialist |

Table 34. Verification run after maintenance
| Step | Action | Pass criterion |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Remove lock-out per site procedure; restore the robot to production mode at 100 percent speed | Robot in production cycle |
| 2 | Warm up for at least 3 cycles (24 s in the simulator; 15 to 30 minutes on a real robot [E]) | Warm-up complete |
| 3 | Collect 20 cycles (160 s) of Sensor 1, TCP and gun temperature | Window complete, synced true |
| 4 | Compute features and compare with the post-maintenance criteria | All criteria met |
| 5 | Run 600 s and confirm no warn or alarm samples | Status normal |
| 6 | Recheck after 24 h of production | Criteria met again |
| 7 | Update baseline record and close the investigation | Baseline stored |

chunks.section: 14. Response Playbooks by Level
chunks.text:
Each playbook lists what the agent reports, what it asks the maintenance organisation to do, and what data it must collect so that a later investigation can reuse the evidence.

Table 35. Playbook L1 Watch
| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Trigger | M 13.5 to 15.0 Nm, or A6 0.4 to 0.6 Nm, or sigma above 0.55 Nm, for 5 cycles, no platform warn |
| Immediate agent actions | Log observation with feature values; fetch TCP and gun temperature; compute S; store window for baseline comparison |
| Report content | Stage 1 incipient; candidate list ranked; statement that no limit is crossed; time-to-threshold estimate if three windows are available |
| Maintenance request | None yet; add to the next planned inspection list; ask whether lubrication is due |
| Data to preserve | Raw samples of the window, TCP mean, state context |
| Re-evaluation | Every 5 cycles in the simulator; every shift on a real robot [I] |
| Escalation condition | M increases by 1 Nm or more between consecutive windows, or A6 exceeds 0.6 Nm, or the watch persists for 7 days [I] |

Table 36. Playbook L2 Warning
| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Per-cycle peak at or above 26 Nm and below 30 Nm for 2 consecutive cycles |
| Immediate agent actions | Open one investigation (10 min cooldown); compute candidate scores; check TCP, idle, temperature |
| Report content | Level, stage 3 or earlier, diagnosis with confidence, evidence for and against, time-to-alarm estimate |
| Maintenance request | Inspection at the next planned stop; list the first inspection from the priority table |
| Operational advice | Continue production only if the stop is planned within the estimated time to alarm; avoid increasing speed or payload |
| Data to preserve | Window features, ratios, TCP trend |
| Escalation condition | Peak at or above 30 Nm, M rise of 3 Nm or more since the investigation opened, or confidence Low with F07 candidate |

Table 37. Playbook L3 Alarm
| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Per-cycle peak at or above 30 Nm and below 34 Nm for 2 consecutive cycles |
| Immediate agent actions | Raise the alarm in the investigation; confirm data validity; compute severity score |
| Report content | Stage 4; diagnosis; recommend intervention in the shift; reduced duty; planning of the stop and of spare parts (gear set, lubricant, seals) |
| Maintenance request | Intervention within the shift; lock-out and OEM procedure |
| Operational advice | Reduce speed override or duty if the process allows; do not run to failure |
| Data to preserve | Full window, TCP trend, alarm time, event log |
| Escalation condition | Sample at or above 34 Nm, alarm for 10 minutes, or noise or temperature rising rapidly |

Table 38. Playbook L4 Critical
| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Any confirmed sample at or above 34 Nm, or M at or above 23.5 Nm, or alarm longer than 10 minutes, or suspected collision |
| Immediate agent actions | Escalate to specialist and safety officer; mark investigation critical |
| Report content | Possible damage; stop at a safe point; do not restart before inspection |
| Maintenance request | Immediate lock-out; full mechanical inspection |
| Data to preserve | Everything; avoid overwriting history (telemetry TTL 48 h in the platform [P], so export evidence) |
| Escalation condition | Not applicable; restart only after verification criteria are met |

chunks.section: 15. Reasoning Chains for Retrieval
chunks.text:
The chains below state complete diagnostic reasoning in sentence form so that a retrieval system can return them as supporting evidence.

Table 40. Reasoning chains
| Observation | Reasoning | Conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| M 17 Nm, A6 1.2 Nm, TCP 0.33 mm, gun unchanged, swing 7.0 Nm | The mean rise of 4 Nm gives S 0.38; expected A6 is 3.0 x 0.38 = 1.14 Nm and expected TCP mean is 0.104 + 0.55 x 0.38 = 0.31 mm; both match, the swing is unchanged and the gun is unaffected | Gearbox wear (F01) at stage 2, no platform limit yet; inspect gearbox at a planned stop |
| M 17 Nm, A6 0.1 Nm, TCP 0.11 mm | Mean rise without the expected ripple (1.14 Nm) or TCP rise (0.31 mm) is inconsistent with the F01 ratios | Friction family (F02, F03, F09); not F01 |
| Peak 27 Nm in one cycle only, M 13.1 Nm | A single peak with a healthy mean cannot be a baseline shift; healthy peaks reach at most 23.1 Nm so it is an outlier | Transient; recheck 5 cycles; check data path |
| Peak 27 Nm every cycle, M 19.4 Nm | M of 19.4 Nm is S 0.61 and the peak of 27.2 Nm matches the model at S 0.6 (27.36 Nm) | Warning stage 3; investigate for F01 |
| Platform shows warn/normal flicker once per cycle | Per-sample classification flickers because only the peak crosses 26 Nm; this occurs at S 0.4 to 0.6 | Persistent early warning, not noise |
| Torque trace flat at 13.0 Nm, sigma 0 | A healthy axis shows sigma 0.45 Nm and a swing of 7 Nm; zero variance means the value is not following the axis | Sensor or data fault (F11), not a healthy axis |
| Torque 0 to 2 Nm for hours, program stopped, status online | No cycle and a low holding torque | Idle, not a fault |
| M +6 Nm and swing +30 percent after a program change | Mean and swing change together and no ripple | F10 or F07 payload; re-baseline after confirming |
| Spikes of 5 Nm at 2.4 s and 6.0 s every cycle, M 13.3 Nm | Spikes lie at the torque reversal phases; mean unchanged | Backlash or looseness (F05) |
| Bump of 3 Nm at 1.2 s only | One phase window, rest unchanged | External drag (F06) |
| M 16 Nm after cold start, falls to 14 Nm in 20 minutes | Reversible friction component | Thermal or lubrication (F09, F02 warm-up part) |
| Sample at 38 Nm followed by baseline, TCP step +0.3 mm | Single impulsive event with kinematic step | Collision (F07); stop and inspect |
| Torque, TCP and gun all constant, seq gaps | All channels affected at once | Data path (F12) |
| Alarm after repair with M 13.0 Nm and A6 0.1 Nm | Features healthy but alert not cleared | Alert clearing latency or stale state; verify 2-cycle clear rule and status |

chunks.section: 16. IF/THEN Rule Library
chunks.text:
Table 41. Consolidated IF/THEN rule library
| Rule | IF | THEN |
|---|---|---|
| R-01 | status offline or stale | stop; report data-path state |
| R-02 | more than 10 percent samples missing | mark incomplete; lower confidence |
| R-06 | state not production steady | do not apply thresholds |
| R-09 | peak at least 26 Nm for 2 cycles | WARNING; evaluate candidates |
| R-10 | peak at least 30 Nm for 2 cycles | ALARM; intervene |
| R-11 | sample at least 34 Nm confirmed | CRITICAL; escalate |
| R-12 | M step of 1 Nm or more in one cycle | check program, payload, collision first |
| R-13 | M ramp with proportional A6 | F01 developing; extrapolate time to threshold |
| R-21 | A6 at least 0.4 AND A6/dM in 0.2 to 0.4 AND dTCP positive AND swing unchanged AND gun temperature unchanged | leading diagnosis F01, high confidence if points at least 9 |
| R-22 | dM at least 1 Nm AND A6 below 0.2 AND swing unchanged AND M follows temperature | F09 or F02 warm-up component |
| R-23 | dM at least 1 Nm AND A6 below 0.2 AND idle offset at least 0.5 Nm | F03 brake drag or F08 drive offset |
| R-24 | spikes at least 3 Nm at the same 1 or 2 phases for 3 cycles AND dM below 1 Nm | F05 backlash or looseness |
| R-25 | bump at one phase window AND the rest of the cycle unchanged | F06 external drag |
| R-26 | mean and swing both change proportionally AND A6 below 0.2 | F07 payload or F10 program |
| R-27 | one sample above 30 Nm followed by baseline AND TCP step | F07 collision; escalate |
| R-28 | dM at least 1 Nm AND TCP unchanged AND A6 below 0.2 AND idle offset | F08 or F11 offset |
| R-29 | TCP mean above 0.25 mm AND torque not yet in warn | early wear signal; open L1 or L2 watch on F01 |
| R-30 | TCP above 0.5 mm AND dM above 8.6 Nm | alarm-equivalent F01 |
| R-31 | status flickers warn/normal at cycle rate AND M above 15 Nm | not noise; treat as L2 persistent warning |
| R-32 | only the warn flag is on while M is in the healthy band | check for glitch or per-sample outlier; no wear |
| R-33 | component not bound on the twin | report needs_binding, no highlight |
| R-34 | repair done AND verification criteria not met | reopen; do not clear alert |

chunks.section: 1. Maintenance Philosophy > 1.1 Condition-based approach
chunks.text:
The repository provides no inspection intervals, lubricant specifications, backlash limits, spare-part numbers, torque values or mean time between failures for axis 4 [P]. This document therefore does not invent intervals. Maintenance is triggered by condition: the Sensor 1 level (L1 to L4, LS), the stage of the gear train (stages 0 to 5) and the confirmed diagnosis. Routine inspections follow the OEM maintenance schedule and the site plan, which are referenced here but not reproduced.

PRINCIPLE: compare the channel to its own baseline and look at the shape of the signal; do not run a drifting component to alarm; schedule inspection at the next planned stop (carried over from the repository's press runbook stubs, applied here by analogy [P][E]).

Table 1. Condition-based maintenance triggers
| Sensor 1 condition | Level / stage | Maintenance response | Timing basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Healthy: M 12.5 to 13.5 Nm, A6 at most 0.2 Nm | L0 / stage 0 | Routine inspections per OEM schedule | OEM schedule (not specified in repository) |
| M 13.5 to 15.0 Nm or A6 0.4 to 0.6 Nm | L1 / stage 1 | Add to next planned inspection; check lubrication records; trend | Next planned inspection |
| M 15.0 to 18.0 Nm, no warn | L1 to L2 / stage 2 | Plan gearbox inspection (oil, backlash, fasteners, dress pack) | Within days (real) [I] |
| Peak at or above 26 Nm for 2 cycles | L2 / stage 3 | Inspection at the next planned stop | Next planned stop |
| Peak at or above 30 Nm for 2 cycles | L3 / stage 4 | Intervention in the shift; plan repair and parts | Within shift [I] |
| Sample at or above 34 Nm, or collision | L4 / stage 5 | Immediate stop; full inspection | Immediate |
| Flat, clipped or noisy signal | LS | Data-path and signal inspection first | Within shift |

chunks.section: 2. Safety Considerations
chunks.text:
This document is a capstone prototype. It does not replace the robot manufacturer's manual, the plant's lock-out and tag-out procedure or site safety rules. Follow the manufacturer's procedure and apply lock-out and tag-out before opening the drive, gearbox or brake. Only qualified persons may perform the tasks below.

Table 3. Hazards and controls for axis 4 work
| Hazard | Where | Control [E] |
|---|---|---|
| Gravity fall of the forearm when the brake is released or the drive is opened | Axis 4 and attached wrist, tool and gun | Support the arm mechanically or move it to the OEM service pose; never release the brake without support |
| Stored electrical energy in the drive | Servo drive, DC link | Lock-out and tag-out; wait for the capacitor discharge time stated by the OEM; verify zero energy |
| Unexpected motion | Whole robot | Lock-out the controller; enabling device in hand; cell guarding closed or fenced |
| Hot surfaces and lubricant | Gearbox, motor, brake | Allow cooling; use gloves; handle hot lubricant carefully |
| Pressure in the gearbox | Gearbox housing | Release pressure per OEM before opening plugs |
| Pinch points and crush | Forearm, tool, gun | Keep body outside the swept range |
| Weld gun and cabling | Spot weld gun and dress pack | Isolate welding power; discharge capacitors; remove tip pressure |
| Electrical shock | Motor and brake supply | Qualified electrician; use rated meters |
| Chemical exposure | Grease, oil, cleaners | Safety data sheets, gloves, eye protection |
| Restart after maintenance | Controller | Verification run at reduced speed first; clear the cell |

chunks.section: 2. Safety Considerations > 2.1 Pre-work checklist
chunks.text:
• Confirm the machine ID (robot-weld-01), axis (4) and the level from the agent report.

• Obtain the OEM manual, the maintenance permit and the lock-out and tag-out plan.

• Park the robot in the service pose, support the forearm and verify zero energy.

• Record the baseline readings before the work: Sensor 1 features, TCP mean, gun temperature,

backlash if measurable.

• Prepare spare parts and lubricants identified from the OEM documentation, not from this

document.

chunks.section: 3. Preventive Inspection Checklist
chunks.text:
The checklist is organised by component. The interval column states the basis, not a number, because intervals are OEM-specific. A telemetry trigger can advance any inspection.

Table 4. Preventive inspection checklist for the axis 4 drive train
| Item | What to check | Interval basis | Telemetry trigger that advances it | Record |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gearbox lubricant | Level, colour, odour, metallic particles, leakage | OEM schedule | M above 13.5 Nm or A6 above 0.4 Nm | Level, condition, sample ID |
| Seals and breather | Weeping, cracks, blocked breather | OEM schedule | Noise rise | Condition |
| Fasteners (gearbox to arm, motor to gearbox) | Marks intact, torque check per OEM | OEM schedule; after any collision | Spikes at reversals | Torque values |
| Backlash at flange | Dial indicator measurement | OEM schedule; baseline at commissioning | dTCP above 0.15 mm | Value, direction, date |
| Brake | Release click, supply voltage, drag by hand | OEM schedule | Idle offset above 0.5 Nm | Voltage, timing |
| Motor and cable | Connector tightness, insulation, no chafing | OEM schedule | Offset or non-harmonic lines | Condition |
| Dress pack and hoses | Routing, slack, wear, spatter | Each planned stop | Phase-locked bump | Condition |
| Covers and spatter shields | Spatter build-up | Each planned stop | Slow rise of M | Cleaned |
| Gateway and data path | status online, synced true, no seq gaps, diag fields | Weekly for the prototype [I] | Stale or gaps | diag snapshot |
| Sensor 1 baseline | Recompute M, A6, sigma, template | After any repair or program change | Any L1 | Baseline record |
| TCP accuracy | Mean deviation | After any collision or repair | dTCP rising | Mean in mm |

chunks.section: 4. Visual and Mechanical Inspection > 4.1 Visual inspection; 4.2 Mechanical inspection
chunks.text:
Table 5. Visual inspection table
| Item | Look for | Finding | Meaning (link to Sensor 1) | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gearbox housing | Oil weeping, stains, cracks | Wet seal, dark streaks | Lubrication loss (F02) leading to F01 | Clean, find leak path, relubricate |
| Gearbox plug or magnetic plug | Metallic fines or flakes | Metal on magnet | Wear (F01, F04) | Take oil sample; plan gear inspection |
| Fasteners and torque marks | Marks broken or shifted | Misaligned marks | Looseness (F05) | Retorque and replace damaged fasteners |
| Dress pack | Rub marks, kinks | Tension at a pose | External drag (F06) | Re-dress |
| Brake area | Discolouration, dust | Hot marks | Brake drag (F03) | Electrical and mechanical brake check |
| Cables and connectors | Chafing, burn marks | Damaged insulation | Electrical fault (F08) | Replace and test |
| Tool and gun | Deformation, loose parts, collision marks | Damage | Overload or collision (F07) | Inspect the gear train |
| Cooling | Dust on fins, fan operation | Blocked | Thermal (F09) | Clean |
| Weld spatter | Build-up near seals | Spatter | Drag, seal damage | Clean and shield |

Table 6. Mechanical inspection table
| Component / test | Method | Indicator of fault | Acceptance basis | Linked fault |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gearbox backlash | Dial indicator at the output flange, servo off and brake per OEM procedure | Backlash above OEM limit or increased by more than 50 percent from commissioning value [I] | OEM limit (not specified) | F05, F01 |
| Output shaft play | Radial and axial movement by hand and indicator | Detectable play | OEM limit | F04 |
| Noise at low speed | Slow axis move with all other axes still, listen with stethoscope | Roughness or periodic knock | Qualitative; compare with healthy axis | F01, F04 |
| Oil or grease sample | Collect per OEM; send to laboratory or screen visually and magnetically | Metal flakes, colour change, increase of iron content versus previous sample [E] | OEM or laboratory limit | F01, F02 |
| Temperature | Contact thermometer or IR on gearbox and motor housing at steady state | Higher than neighbouring axes or than previous record | OEM limit | F02, F03, F09 |
| Torque to turn by hand (servo off, brake released with support) | Where permitted by OEM, feel resistance | Notchy or tight | Qualitative | F01, F03, F04 |
| Fastener torque | Calibrated torque wrench | Below specification | OEM torque table | F05 |
| Coupling or key | Inspect for fretting and play | Wear | OEM | F05 |
| Mastering position | Compare mastering marks and readings | Offset after collision | OEM | F07 |

chunks.section: 5. Electrical, Sensor and Wiring Inspection > 5.1 Electrical inspection; 5.2 Sensor inspection: the Sensor 1 data path
chunks.text:
Table 7. Electrical inspection table
| Item | Test | Healthy | Fault indication | Linked fault |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Brake supply | Voltage at brake terminals during release | Within OEM specification | Low voltage, late release | F03 |
| Brake release timing | Controller log or scope | Release before motion | Late release | F03 |
| Motor phase currents | Clamp meter or drive diagnostic | Balanced phases | Imbalance | F08 |
| Current sensor offset | Drive diagnostic with motor idle | Zero current reads zero | Offset | F08 |
| Encoder signal | Drive diagnostic | No errors | Noise or dropouts | F08, F04 |
| Motor cable and connectors | Insulation test, visual | Within OEM | Low insulation, burn | F08 |
| Grounding and shielding | Continuity | Within OEM | Poor ground | F08, F11 |
| Drive temperature and faults | Drive log | Normal | Over-temperature or alarms | F08, F09 |

Sensor 1 is a controller-internal value, not a separate transducer. Inspection therefore concerns the value path: controller estimate, gateway, broker and backend. In the prototype the ESP32 generates the value from an equation, so a data-path check is the first step when a reading looks implausible.

Table 8. Sensor validation table
| Validation | Method | Expected result | Pass criterion | Failure means |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Value follows the cycle | View 16 samples per cycle | 8 s waveform, swing 7 Nm, mean 13 Nm in healthy state | Autocorrelation peak at 8 s | F11 or F10 |
| Variance | Compute sigma at same phase | 0.45 Nm (healthy) | 0.40 to 0.55 Nm | Flat or burst signal |
| Range | Min and max | 3.1 to 23.1 Nm (healthy) | Within range | Clipping, offset |
| Offset at idle | Torque with axis holding | Posture-dependent hold value | Matches previous record within 0.5 Nm | F08, F11, F03 |
| Cross-check with independent current measurement | Clamp-on current at the motor, convert with torque constant (OEM) | Within about 5 percent after conversion [E][I] | Agreement | Controller estimate error |
| Known-load check | Move with and without a known load per OEM | Torque change proportional to load | Proportional | Gain error |
| Gateway health | diag fields uptimeS, rssi, heapFree, heapMin, reset, wifiReconnects, mqttReconnects, restarts, publishFailures, tls | Stable minimum heap over a 30 minute soak; no reconnects | No growth | Gateway fault (F12) |
| Sequence continuity | seq counter | No gaps (reboot shows new bootId with seq 0) | Gaps below 1 percent | Network loss |
| Clock | synced flag | true | true | NTP blocked |
| Cross-channel consistency | Compare torque with TCP and gun temperature | Moves as expected for scenario | Consistent | Identity or path error |

chunks.text:
• Controller to gateway link: connector seating, cable condition and shield termination (real plant:

OPC UA or MTConnect link and the gateway power supply) [E].

• Gateway power and Wi-Fi: stable supply, 2.4 GHz network, signal strength (rssi) not marginal; the

prototype ESP32 runs on a USB or bench supply [P].

• Broker access: credentials with permission to publish on cdo/v1/vit-lab/robot-weld-01/...; TLS clock

requirement [P].

• Motor power, brake and encoder cables of axis 4: connectors tight, no chafing in the dress pack,

shield continuity [E].

chunks.section: 6. Component Condition Assessment > 6.1 Lubrication and service considerations
chunks.text:
Table 9. Component condition grades and their relation to Sensor 1 stages
| Grade | Definition | Axis 4 gearbox evidence | Sensor 1 stage | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A Good | No wear indications | Clean lubricant, backlash at baseline, no noise | Stage 0 (M 12.5 to 13.5 Nm, A6 at most 0.2) | Continue; routine |
| B Watch | Early indications | Slight discolouration, backlash increase below 25 percent [I] | Stage 1 to 2 | Trend; plan inspection |
| C Degraded | Confirmed wear | Fines on magnet, backlash rise above 50 percent [I], noise | Stage 3 | Repair at next stop |
| D Failed or failing | Damage affecting function | Chipped teeth, large play, heavy debris | Stage 4 to 5 | Replace before return to service |

The grades combine measurements and Sensor 1 evidence: a grade C component with Sensor 1 still in stage 2 shows that telemetry lags physical wear; the physical finding governs. Conversely stage 3 or higher in Sensor 1 with grade A physical findings points to a measurement or non-gearbox cause and requires rechecking the data path and the friction candidates.

• Grade, quantity, fill procedure and replacement conditions come from the OEM manual; they are

not specified in the repository [P].

• Never mix incompatible greases; record grade and batch at every service.

• After lubricant service, run warm-up cycles and recapture the Sensor 1 baseline; a new offset after

service suggests over-fill or wrong grade.

• If metallic particles are found, the diagnosis moves from lubrication (F02) to wear (F01); a simple

relubrication is no longer sufficient.

• Keep drains and breathers clean to avoid pressure and contamination; check seals whenever the

lubricant is changed.

chunks.section: 6. Component Condition Assessment > 6.2 Alignment and installation checks; 6.3 Component inspection table
chunks.text:
Table 10. Alignment and installation checks
| Check | Method | Why it matters | Linked fault |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gearbox-to-arm mounting | Fastener torque marks; flatness of interface | Looseness gives reversal spikes | F05 |
| Motor-to-gearbox coupling | Concentricity per OEM | Misalignment loads bearings | F04, F05 |
| Mastering (zero position) of axis 4 | Master per OEM after repair or collision | Position error appears as TCP deviation | F07, F01 |
| Tool and payload data | Controller tool data matches real mass and centre of gravity | Wrong data gives wrong torque feedforward and payload faults | F10, F07 |
| Dress pack routing | Slack across stroke | Drag bump | F06 |
| Bracket and gun mounting | Torque and play | Added load or vibration | F07 |

Table 11. Component inspection table for the axis 4 drive train
| Component | Inspection method | Healthy finding | Fault finding | Corrective action | Linked Sensor 1 pattern |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Axis 4 gearbox gear mesh | Oil and magnet check, noise, backlash | Clean lubricant, backlash at baseline | Flakes, chips, noise, backlash rise | Replace gear set or gearbox | Mean up, A6 above 0.4, noise up, TCP up |
| Gearbox lubricant | Level, colour, sample | Correct level, clear | Dark, milky, low | Replace or top up | Mean up, A6 absent |
| Gearbox and motor seals | Visual | Dry | Weeping | Replace seals | Slow mean rise |
| Output and motor bearings | Play, temperature, noise | No play, normal temperature | Play, hot, rumble | Replace bearings | Noise up, sparse spikes |
| Holding brake | Voltage, timing, drag, temperature | Releases fully | Drag, hot | Repair or replace | Mean up, idle offset |
| Servo drive and current sensors | Diagnostic log, balance | Balanced, no offset | Offset, imbalance | Replace or calibrate | Offset at idle, non-harmonic lines |
| Motor cable, encoder cable | Visual, continuity | Intact | Chafed, loose | Replace or reseat | Erratic noise, offset |
| Mounting and coupling | Torque, play | Marks aligned | Loose, fretting | Retorque or replace | Spikes at reversals, TCP up |
| Dress pack | Routing, slack | Free | Tight, worn | Re-dress | Bump at one phase |
| Tool and gun | Mass data, damage | Matches data | Damage or wrong data | Correct | Step, swing change |
| ESP32 gateway (data path) | diag fields | Stable heap, no reconnects | Reconnects, restarts | Fix network or firmware | Gaps, stale, flat |

| Activity | When | Procedure | Result recorded |

chunks.section: 8. Troubleshooting Procedure > 8.1 Procedure steps; 8.2 Observed condition to action
chunks.text:
Table 13. Troubleshooting procedure for an abnormal Sensor 1
| Step | Action | Decision | Next |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Read the agent report: level, pattern, diagnosis, confidence | Is the data path valid? | If no: Section 12 |
| 2 | Confirm the abnormal reading on a second view (twin, history) and check operating state | Is state production and steady? | If no: do not diagnose; correct context |
| 3 | Check for recent events: collision, program or tool change, lubrication, repair | Event found? | Check F07, F10, F02 first |
| 4 | Perform the first inspection from the priority table | Finding confirms? | If yes: corrective action; if no: next |
| 5 | Perform the decisive test for the second candidate | Finding confirms? | As above |
| 6 | Implement corrective action in priority order | - | Section 9 |
| 7 | Run verification (Section 10) | Criteria met? | If no: reopen and escalate |
| 8 | Record findings and update baseline | - | Close |

Table 14. Troubleshooting table: observed Sensor 1 condition, cause, inspection, corrective action, verification
| Observed Sensor 1 condition | Possible cause | Inspection | Corrective action | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M 13.5 to 15.0 Nm, A6 0.4 to 0.6, no limit | Incipient gear wear or early friction | Review lubrication records; take oil sample at next stop | Trend; relubricate if due | M back within 12.5 to 13.5 and A6 at most 0.2 after service or stable trend |
| M 15 to 18 Nm, A6 0.6 to 1.5, TCP rising, status normal | Gearbox wear stage 2 (F01) | Oil, magnet, backlash, noise | Plan gear replacement; reduce duty | Features healthy after repair |
| Peak 26 to 30 Nm each cycle, A6 1.5 to 2.5 | Gearbox wear stage 3 | Same plus full gearbox inspection | Replace gear set or gearbox at next stop | Peak at most 23.1 Nm |
| Peak 30 Nm or above each cycle | Gearbox wear stage 4 or overload | Immediate inspection | Intervene; replace | Status normal for 600 s |
| Sample at or above 34 Nm | Collision or beyond-model wear | Stop; damage check | Specialist repair | Full verification |
| M high, A6 absent, idle offset | Brake drag or drive offset | Brake voltage, release timing; drive log | Repair brake or sensor | Idle offset zero |
| M high after cold start, falls with warm-up | Cold viscosity or lubricant degradation | Lubricant grade and condition; temperature | Service lubricant | Warm-up offset at most 0.5 Nm |
| M high, A6 absent, no idle offset, swing unchanged | Friction (F02), external drag (F06) or thermal | Lubricant, dress pack, temperature | Correct | M within band |
| M and swing both changed | Payload or program change | Tool data, program log | Correct tool data or re-baseline | New baseline |
| Spikes at reversals | Backlash or looseness | Fasteners, backlash, coupling | Retorque or replace | Spikes absent |
| Bump at one phase | Dress pack drag | Routing, slack | Re-dress | Bump absent |
| Noise rise with sparse spikes | Bearing degradation | Play, temperature, grease | Replace bearing | Noise 0.40 to 0.55 Nm |
| Flat constant signal | Signal fault, gateway freeze | diag fields, controller state | Restart gateway; fix path | Cycle returns |
| Values at 0 or 45 Nm | Saturation or scaling error | Scaling, drive | Fix scaling | Normal range |
| Torque normal but TCP rising | Backlash, mastering, other axis | Backlash, mastering | Correct | TCP at 0.10 mm |
| Torque warn but gun temperature high | Process or thermal event | Gun channel | Separate gun fault | Both normal |
| No data, device stale | Network or power | Gateway diag, power | Restore | Online |
| seq gaps | Packet loss | rssi, network | Improve link | No gaps |
| Alarm not cleared after repair | Alert latency or residual fault | Recheck features; 2-cycle clear rule | Reevaluate | Normal 600 s |

chunks.section: 9. Corrective Actions, Replacement Criteria and Priorities
chunks.text:
Table 15. Fault-to-maintenance-action matrix
| Fault | Primary action | Secondary action | Parts or consumables (OEM) | Skill level | Typical downtime [I] |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F01 gearbox wear | Replace gear set or gearbox | Replace lubricant and seals; re-master; re-baseline | Gearbox or gear set, seals, lubricant | Specialist | Several hours to a shift |
| F02 lubrication | Relubricate or replace lubricant | Replace seals; clean breather | Lubricant, seals | Technician | 1 to 2 hours |
| F03 brake drag | Repair or replace brake | Verify release timing | Brake assembly | Electrician and technician | 1 to 3 hours |
| F04 bearing | Replace bearings | Relubricate; check shaft | Bearing set | Specialist | Several hours |
| F05 looseness | Retorque; replace coupling | Measure backlash | Fasteners, coupling | Technician | 1 to 2 hours |
| F06 external drag | Re-dress, clean | Replace guides | Clamps, covers | Technician | 30 to 60 min |
| F07 overload or collision | Inspect, repair damage, re-master | Check tool data | Depends | Specialist | Variable |
| F08 drive fault | Replace sensor or drive module | Recalibrate | Drive, sensor, cable | Electrician | 1 to 3 hours |
| F09 thermal | Restore cooling; reduce duty | Allow warm-up | Filters | Technician | 30 min |
| F10 program change | Re-baseline | Update tool data | None | Programmer | 15 min |
| F11 sensor fault | Fix signal path | Restart gateway | Firmware or wiring | Controls engineer | 30 to 60 min |
| F12 data path | Fix network, clock, identity | Restart | None | IT or controls | 15 to 60 min |

Table 16. Corrective-action priority table
| Priority | Condition | Reason | Action first |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Safety | L4, suspected collision, brake or drive fault | Risk to persons and equipment | Stop, lock-out, inspect |
| 2 Damage prevention | L3 alarm, noise and temperature rising | Gearbox failure risk | Intervene in shift |
| 3 Quality | L2 warning, TCP above 0.25 mm | Weld position quality | Plan inspection at next stop |
| 4 Condition | L1 watch | Early detection | Plan, trend, check lubrication |
| 5 Data | LS, F12 | Blind spots | Fix path in parallel |

| 1 Safety | L4, suspected collision, brake or drive fault | Risk to persons and equipment | Stop, lock-out, inspect |
| 2 Damage prevention | L3 alarm, noise and temperature rising | Gearbox failure risk | Intervene in shift |
| 3 Quality | L2 warning, TCP above 0.25 mm | Weld position quality | Plan inspection at next stop |
| 4 Condition | L1 watch | Early detection | Plan, trend, check lubrication |
| 5 Data | LS, F12 | Blind spots | Fix path in parallel |

chunks.section: 10. Task Procedures
chunks.text:
The task procedures below are engineering-reference outlines [E]. Quantities, tools, torque values, lubricant grades and sequences must be taken from the OEM manual. Each task ends with the data that must be recorded so that Sensor 1 features can later be compared with physical findings.

Table 18. Task T1: gearbox lubricant sampling and magnetic plug inspection
| Step | Action | Check | Record |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Obtain permit; lock-out; support forearm; verify zero energy | Permit and lock-out in place | Permit number |
| 2 | Clean around the sampling or drain point to avoid contamination | No debris near the opening | - |
| 3 | Open the plug or sampling port per OEM (release pressure first) | Pressure released | Lubricant state |
| 4 | Collect sample into a clean labelled container (about the volume the laboratory requests) | Sample from mid-flow, not from the sump bottom | Sample ID, axis, date, operating hours if known |
| 5 | Inspect magnetic plug: fines (fine grey paste) versus flakes or chips | Fines: normal run-in or slow wear; flakes or chips: damage | Photo, description |
| 6 | Check colour, odour, milkiness (water) and grit between fingers (gloved) | Dark, burnt odour, milky or gritty | Description |
| 7 | Refit plug with new seal per OEM; clean | No leak | Torque value used |
| 8 | Send sample to laboratory for wear metals and viscosity (limits per laboratory and OEM) | Report received | Results and date |

Table 19. Interpretation of lubricant findings in relation to Sensor 1
| Finding | Interpretation [E] | Sensor 1 link | Next step |
|---|---|---|---|
| Clean lubricant, no particles | Lubricant and gears in good condition | Mean shift without ripple points to friction, brake or sensor | Check brake, drive, temperature |
| Fines on magnet only | Normal run-in or slow wear | Stage 0 to 1 if M unchanged | Trend |
| Flakes, chips or glittering metal | Surface fatigue or tooth damage | Matches stage 2 to 4 with A6 present | Plan gear inspection and replacement |
| Dark, burnt or oxidised lubricant | Overheating or ageing | F02, F09; M up without ripple | Replace lubricant; find heat source |
| Milky lubricant | Water ingress | F02 with seal fault | Replace lubricant and seals |
| Wear metal level rising versus previous sample | Active wear | Trend confirms F01 | Shorten sampling interval; plan repair |

Table 20. Task T2: backlash measurement at the axis 4 flange
| Step | Action | Check | Record |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Lock-out; support forearm per OEM; use the OEM method for holding the motor side | Motor side held per OEM | - |
| 2 | Mount a dial indicator on a rigid reference at the measurement radius | Indicator stable, perpendicular to motion | Radius |
| 3 | Apply a small reversing force to the output side and read free movement | Repeat 3 times | Readings |
| 4 | Convert to angular backlash using the radius (OEM method) | Within the OEM limit | Value in arc-minutes |
| 5 | Compare with commissioning baseline | Increase above 50 percent triggers evaluation [I] | Ratio |
| 6 | Repeat at a second posture if permitted | Consistent | Posture |

chunks.section: 10. Task Procedures
chunks.text:
Table 21. Task T3: brake release and drag test
| Step | Action | Check | Record |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Measure brake supply voltage at the terminals during release command | Within OEM specification | Voltage |
| 2 | Observe release click or use controller log for timing | Release before motion | Delay in ms |
| 3 | With servo off and brake released under support, assess resistance of the axis by hand where the OEM allows | Free movement without drag | Subjective rating |
| 4 | Measure brake and motor temperature after a run | No local hot spot | Temperature |
| 5 | Inspect disc and armature for wear and contamination if accessible | No glazing or oil | Findings |

Table 22. Task T4: fastener and coupling verification
| Step | Action | Check | Record |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Inspect torque marks on gearbox and motor fasteners | Marks aligned | Marks status |
| 2 | Apply the OEM torque with a calibrated wrench in the OEM sequence | Reaches torque without turning | Torque and tool ID |
| 3 | Replace any damaged fasteners and use thread-locking only if the OEM calls for it | - | Parts |
| 4 | Inspect coupling or key for fretting | No play | Findings |
| 5 | Apply new torque marks | - | - |

Table 23. Task T5: dress pack and external drag inspection
| Step | Action | Check | Record |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Move the axis through the stroke at low speed after lock-out release under a safe procedure | Cables move freely | Posture where tight |
| 2 | Check slack at the extreme postures | Slack per OEM routing | Measurement |
| 3 | Look for rub marks and kinks | None | Photo |
| 4 | Clean spatter from covers and seals | Clean | - |
| 5 | Re-route or replace guides | - | Parts |

Table 24. Task T6: Sensor 1 data-path validation
| Step | Action | Check | Record |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Open device status and diag for robot-weld-01 | online; uptimeS growing; no reconnect growth | diag snapshot |
| 2 | Check seq continuity over 5 minutes | Gaps below 1 percent | Gap count |
| 3 | Check synced | true | - |
| 4 | Compare Sensor 1 with TCP and gun temperature | Plausible, not frozen | - |
| 5 | Compute sigma and the autocorrelation at 8 s | sigma 0.40 to 0.55 Nm and periodic | Values |
| 6 | If the signal is suspect, send ping and check ack; if needed reboot the gateway | ack received | ack detail |

Table 25. Task T7: outline for gearbox replacement (per OEM manual only)
| Step | Action | Control | Record |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Plan: order parts and tools; schedule downtime; assign specialist | Parts verified against serial numbers | Work order |
| 2 | Lock-out; discharge energy; support forearm; disconnect motor and brake cables | Zero energy verified | Permit |
| 3 | Drain lubricant; remove motor and arm interface per OEM sequence | Parts labelled | Lubricant state |
| 4 | Inspect shafts, bearings, seals and mating surfaces | Damage assessed | Findings |
| 5 | Install new gear set or gearbox; torque in OEM sequence; fill with the OEM lubricant | Correct torque and quantity | Torque values, lubricant batch |
| 6 | Reconnect cables; remove supports; run brake and drive tests | Tests pass | Test log |
| 7 | Master axis 4 and verify TCP accuracy | Mastering within OEM | Mastering data |
| 8 | Run Post-Maintenance Testing (Section 10) | Criteria met | Baseline |

chunks.section: 11. Using the Digital Twin During Maintenance
chunks.text:
Table 27. Twin behaviour relevant to maintenance [P]
| Twin element | Behaviour | Maintenance use |
|---|---|---|
| Sensor binding ROBOT-WELD- 01.AXIS_4_SERVO_TORQUE | Binds the channel to one mesh, suggested 105-six-axis-welding-robot/arm-swing, label Robot forearm (axis 4) | Locate the forearm on the 3D model; the mesh is a suggestion and the operator confirms the correct part |
| Warn state | Mesh tinted amber #d98400 steady; marker becomes a triangle | Prioritise axis 4 inspection at next stop |
| Alarm state | Mesh tinted red #b3261e pulsing; marker becomes a square; status message announced | Intervene |
| Bind flash | Mesh flashes green for about 1.6 s on successful binding | Confirm the correct mesh after rebinding |
| Unbound channel | Agent reports needs_binding instead of a highlight | Bind before relying on spatial pointing |
| Selecting a bound channel | Camera focuses on its mesh | Use for briefing the technician |
| Agent highlight tone | Built but unused until Phase 5, priority above alarm | Planned: highlight of the diagnosed component |
| Machine removed from twin | Bindings of its channels retired (kept as history) | Rebind after re-adding the machine |
| Telemetry retention | 48 h time-series TTL | Export evidence early |

chunks.section: 15. Service Events and Their Effect on Sensor 1
chunks.text:
Table 32. Expected Sensor 1 response to service events [E][I]
| Service event | Expected short-term effect | What it means if the effect is absent or opposite | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Relubrication of axis 4 gearbox | M falls by 0.5 to several Nm after warm-up if friction was the cause | No change: friction was not the cause; suspect wear (A6 present?) or brake | Re-run differentiation |
| Lubricant over-fill | Offset rise of 0.5 to 2 Nm for a period, noise slightly up | Persisting: churning losses; correct level | Correct level and re-baseline |
| Replacement of the gear set | M returns to baseline within 0.5 Nm; A6 at most 0.2 Nm; run-in may add a transient | M still high: friction from new parts, brake drag, or wrong tool data | Warm-up; recheck brake and payload |
| Brake repair | Idle offset removed | Idle offset persists: drive offset | Drive tests |
| Retorque of fasteners | Reversal spikes disappear | Spikes persist: backlash or coupling wear | Backlash measurement |
| Dress pack adjustment | Phase bump disappears | Bump persists: other drag source | Check seals and cover contact |
| Tool or payload change | M and swing change, then new baseline | Ripple appears: separate wear | Recheck |
| Mastering | TCP back to about 0.10 mm | TCP high: backlash or kinematic data | Check parameters |
| Gateway reboot or reflash | Brief gap, new bootId | Torque pattern changed: not the mechanics | Check firmware version (1.0.0 in contract examples) [P] |

chunks.section: 16. Failure Prevention and Operating Practices
chunks.text:
Table 33. Prevention measures and monitoring indicators [E]
| Practice | Prevents | Indicator in Sensor 1 |
|---|---|---|

| Clean spatter from covers and seals | Drag, seal damage | No slow M rise |

| Keep gateway clock and network healthy | Misdiagnosis | synced true; no gaps |

chunks.section: 17. Text Decision Trees for Troubleshooting
chunks.text:
TREE 1 (mean high): IF M is above 13.5 Nm THEN check data path; IF data path valid THEN check state; IF state valid THEN check A6; IF A6 at least 0.4 and ratio 0.2 to 0.4 THEN go to gearbox inspection (T1, T2); ELSE check idle offset; IF idle offset at least 0.5 Nm THEN brake and drive tests (T3, electrical inspection); ELSE check temperature dependence; IF reversible THEN thermal and lubricant checks; ELSE lubricant, dress pack and tool data checks (T1, T5).

TREE 2 (spike or bump): IF an isolated spike at least 30 Nm appears once THEN check event log for collision and TCP step; IF collision suspected THEN stop and inspect; ELSE log and recheck after 5 cycles. IF spikes repeat at the same phase THEN fasteners and backlash (T4, T2); IF a smooth bump repeats THEN dress pack (T5).

TREE 3 (flat, clipped or missing): IF the value is constant or clipped THEN data-path validation (T6); IF other channels are also affected THEN gateway and network; IF only Sensor 1 is affected THEN signal scaling and controller interface; IF the program is stopped THEN treat as idle.

chunks.section: 18. Maintenance Mistakes That Corrupt Diagnosis
chunks.text:
Table 34. Common mistakes and consequences
| Mistake | Consequence for Sensor 1 interpretation | Prevention |
|---|---|---|
| Recording the baseline before warm-up | M too high; later normal values look low | Warm up first |
| Changing tool data without re-baselining | Step in M interpreted as wear | Re-baseline after any change |
| Ignoring a single high peak because the mean is normal | Missing a collision | Check event log |
| Using per-sample status only | Missing early warning (flicker) | Use per-cycle features |
| Servicing without recording lubricant grade | Unexplained offset later | Record grade and batch |
| Closing the alert before the 600 s soak | False clearing | Follow verification |
| Swapping the simulator and the board without stopping one | Identity conflict | Stop one source |
| Treating TCP rise as proof of wear | Looseness or mastering missed | Apply ratios |

chunks.section: 22. Data-Path Troubleshooting for Sensor 1
chunks.text:
An implausible or missing Sensor 1 reading must be tested against the data path before any mechanical work. The table reproduces the repository's documented symptoms [P].

Table 39. Data-path symptoms and causes [P]
| Symptom | Likely cause | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Telemetry arrives but the twin shows nothing | Channel not bound to a mesh, or machine not added to the twin | firmware README, cheat sheet |
| Device shown stale | No telemetry for max(5 s, 4 x intervalMs) | MQTT contract |
| Device offline about 15 s after power loss | Last Will published by the broker | firmware README |
| Identity conflict flagged | Board and simulator both announcing robot-weld-01 | demo script |
| A fault seems stuck | Choose Normal in the Faults tab or send cmd/reboot | demo script |
| No Faults tab | ENABLE_DEVICE_COMMANDS is not true | demo script |
| wifi disconnect event, reason 201 | Network not found, or 5 GHz only | firmware README |
| reason 202 or 15 | Wrong Wi-Fi password or unsupported security mode | firmware README |
| mqtt connect failed (state 4) or state 5 | Wrong broker credentials, or credential lacks permission | firmware README |
| tls error -9984 | Clock wrong, or CA file does not anchor the chain | firmware README |
| clock not set after 15 s | Network blocks NTP (UDP 123) | firmware README |
| Gaps in seq | Packet loss (a new bootId with seq 0 is a reboot, not loss) | MQTT contract |

chunks.section: 25. Summary, Safety Notes, References and Revision > 25.1 Maintenance summary; 25.2 Safety and escalation notes; 25.3 References and engineering basis; 25.4 Revision notes
chunks.text:
• Maintenance is condition-based: Sensor 1 levels and gear-train stages decide what to do; OEM

intervals apply to routine work.

• First checks for wear suspicion: oil and magnet, backlash, fasteners, dress pack; first checks for

friction suspicion: lubricant, brake, temperature; first checks for data suspicion: diag, seq, synced.

• Key numbers: warn 26 Nm, alarm 30 Nm, critical 34 Nm (proposed); healthy M 12.5 to 13.5 Nm; A6

at most 0.2 Nm; TCP at most 0.15 mm; 600 s soak.

Lock-out and tag-out, OEM procedure and site safety rules apply to every task. Support the forearm before brake release. This document is a capstone training stub, not a replacement for the OEM manual.

• Repository: runbook stubs for the stamping press (pattern and safety wording), firmware README

and MQTT contract (data-path), Phase 5 blueprint.

• General industrial robot maintenance practice and ISO 10218 safety context [E]; all OEM-specific

values to be taken from the robot manual.

chunks.section: 1. Fault History and Evidence Status > 1.1 What fault history exists for this machine; 1.2 How cases were built
chunks.text:
The repository contains no recorded incidents, work orders, failure dates, repair records or field case studies for Robot Weld 01 [P]. Stored telemetry expires after 48 hours in the platform, so no long history is retained either. Every case in this document is therefore a simulated or illustrative scenario and must never be cited as plant history. The cases of the project fault are reproducible: the simulator is seeded and can be accelerated, so a run can be regenerated.

Table 1. Fault history record for Robot Weld 01
| Item | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Recorded failures of axis 4 | None in repository | [P] |
| Work orders, repairs | None in repository | [P] |
| Field case studies | None in repository | [P] |
| Simulated fault runs | GEARBOX_WEAR (ramp 5 to 600 s); NORMAL | Reproducible with seed and speed options |
| Long-term telemetry | Not retained (48 h TTL) | Export evidence if needed |
| Planned evaluation | Root-cause accuracy, detection lead time, alerts collapsed, citation faithfulness, grounding, needs_binding rate | Gearbox wear is one of four evaluated scenarios [P] |

• Project cases (C01, C02, C03, C16): the torque and TCP equations of the repository were replicated

with a seeded random generator in 40 to 136 s runs [D]. The numbers are consistent with the equations; they differ in detail from any run of the repository's own generator because the random sequence differs.

• Illustrative cases (C04 to C15): numerical features are chosen to be consistent with the engineering

signatures of Document 02 [E][I].

• Reproduction of project cases: node server/scripts/simulate-devices.mjs --machines robot-weld-01

--scenario GEARBOX_WEAR --ramp 120 (options --speed, --seed, --crash) or inject GEARBOX_WEAR from the Faults tab with ENABLE_DEVICE_COMMANDS=true; choose Normal to reset [P].

• Ground truth (the active scenario and ramp) is hidden from the agent; each case reasons from

channel evidence only [P].

Table 2. How to read a case
| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Telemetry window | Samples used; 2 Hz; features computed as in Document 03 |
| S | Severity index (M - 13.0) / 10.5 |
| Level | L0 to L4, LS, as in Document 01 |
| Score | Evidence points from Document 03 matrix |
| Basis | [P][D] project and derived; [E][I] illustrative |

The repository contains no recorded incidents, work orders, failure dates, repair records or field case studies for Robot Weld 01 [P]. Stored telemetry expires after 48 hours in the platform, so no long history is retained either. Every case in this document is therefore a simulated or illustrative scenario and must never be cited as plant history. The cases of the project fault are reproducible: the simulator is seeded and can be accelerated, so a run can be regenerated.

Table 1. Fault history record for Robot Weld 01
| Item | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Recorded failures of axis 4 | None in repository | [P] |
| Work orders, repairs | None in repository | [P] |
| Field case studies | None in repository | [P] |
| Simulated fault runs | GEARBOX_WEAR (ramp 5 to 600 s); NORMAL | Reproducible with seed and speed options |
| Long-term telemetry | Not retained (48 h TTL) | Export evidence if needed |
| Planned evaluation | Root-cause accuracy, detection lead time, alerts collapsed, citation faithfulness, grounding, needs_binding rate | Gearbox wear is one of four evaluated scenarios [P] |

• Project cases (C01, C02, C03, C16): the torque and TCP equations of the repository were replicated

with a seeded random generator in 40 to 136 s runs [D]. The numbers are consistent with the equations; they differ in detail from any run of the repository's own generator because the random sequence differs.

• Illustrative cases (C04 to C15): numerical features are chosen to be consistent with the engineering

signatures of Document 02 [E][I].

• Reproduction of project cases: node server/scripts/simulate-devices.mjs --machines robot-weld-01

--scenario GEARBOX_WEAR --ramp 120 (options --speed, --seed, --crash) or inject GEARBOX_WEAR from the Faults tab with ENABLE_DEVICE_COMMANDS=true; choose Normal to reset [P].

• Ground truth (the active scenario and ramp) is hidden from the agent; each case reasons from

channel evidence only [P].

Table 2. How to read a case
| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Telemetry window | Samples used; 2 Hz; features computed as in Document 03 |
| S | Severity index (M - 13.0) / 10.5 |
| Level | L0 to L4, LS, as in Document 01 |
| Score | Evidence points from Document 03 matrix |
| Basis | [P][D] project and derived; [E][I] illustrative |

chunks.document: Fault History Case Scenarios and Diagnostic Evidence
chunks.section: 3. Detailed Cases: Project Fault GEARBOX_WEAR > 3.1 C01 Gradual degradation under the default 120 s ramp [P][D]
chunks.text:
Table 4. C01 case record
| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| 1. Case ID | C01. Simulated GEARBOX_WEAR injected at t = 0 with rampSec = 120. Replicated run, seeded. |
| 2. Machine operating condition | Production cycle at 100 percent speed, warmed-up, program unchanged, payload unchanged; gun normal. |
| 3. Sensor reading / time-series pattern | Eight 16 s windows (2 cycles each). See the telemetry table below: M rises from 13.8 to 23.2 Nm, per-cycle peak from 22.0 to 31.1 Nm, A6 from about 0.5 to 2.9 Nm, TCP mean from 0.14 to 0.65 mm. |
| 4. Baseline comparison | Healthy baseline M 13.0, peak 21.7, A6 below 0.2, sigma 0.45, TCP 0.104. By window 3 (t = 32 s) M is 3.6 Nm above baseline (S 0.34) and A6 is 1.1 Nm. |
| 5. Threshold comparison | First sample at or above 26 Nm occurs in window t = 48 to 64 s (peak 26.06 Nm). First sample at or above 30 Nm occurs in window t = 112 to 128 s (4 samples). Feature thresholds are crossed earlier: M above 15.0 at about t = 16 to 32 s; TCP above 0.25 at about t = 32 s. |
| 6. Relevant operating state | Production cycle, steady, valid data (synced true, no gaps). |
| 7. Symptoms | Rising TCP deviation, no mechanical alarm initially, warn then alarm on the twin (amber then red). |
| 8. Candidate faults | F01 gearbox wear; F02 lubrication loss; F04 bearing; F05 looseness; F10 program change. |
| 9. Evidence supporting each candidate | F01: mean rise, A6 growing in ratio 0.25 to 0.3 of dM, noise growth, TCP rise with ratio about 0.055 mm per Nm, swing unchanged, gun unchanged, ramp onset. F02: mean rise only. F04: noise rise. F05: TCP rise. |
| 10. Evidence against alternatives | F02, F03, F09: A6 would be absent. F10, F07: swing would change and onset would be a step. F05: spikes would be at reversal phases, not smooth ripple. F11, F12: signal varies and other channels are normal. |
| 11. Diagnostic reasoning | At t = 64 s the mean shift is 6.0 Nm, giving expected A6 about 1.7 Nm (observed 1.48), expected TCP shift about 0.31 mm (observed 0.34 mm) and swing unchanged. All ratios fall inside the accept ranges. The platform status remained normal until t about 50 s, but the feature evidence was available about 30 s earlier. Ramp onset excludes step causes. |
| 12. Final diagnosis | GEARBOX_WEAR (F01): damaged gear mesh in axis 4 gearbox. Stage 2 at t = 32 s, stage 3 at t = 64 s, stage 4 at t = 112 s. Confidence high (14 points, margin 6 over F04). |
| 13. Recommended inspection | At the first L1 (t about 16 s): lubricant sample, magnetic plug and trend request. At L2: gearbox oil, magnet, backlash, fasteners, noise (Document 04 tasks T1 and T2). |
| 14. Corrective action | Replace gear set or gearbox if confirmed; lubricant and seals; re-master; recapture baseline. |
| 15. Expected post-maintenance telemetry | M 12.5 to 13.5 Nm, A6 at most 0.2 Nm, sigma 0.40 to 0.55 Nm, peak at most 23.1 Nm, TCP at most 0.15 mm, status normal. |
| 16. Verification result | Simulated: sending the NORMAL scenario returns the mean to 13.0 Nm within one cycle; ack shows scenario NORMAL (project behaviour). |

chunks.text:
Table 5. C01 telemetry by 16 s window (replicated run, ramp 120 s) [D]
| Window start (s) | Mean r | M (Nm) | S | Per-cycle peak (Nm) | A6 (Nm) | TCP mean (mm) | Samples warn / alarm | Level |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.06 | 13.76 | 0.07 | 21.99 | 0.53 (floor) | 0.14 | 0 / 0 | L0 to L1 |
| 16 | 0.20 | 14.98 | 0.19 | 22.85 | 0.76 | 0.21 | 0 / 0 | L1 |
| 32 | 0.33 | 16.58 | 0.34 | 24.17 | 1.11 | 0.29 | 0 / 0 | L1 to L2 features |
| 48 | 0.46 | 17.83 | 0.46 | 25.49 | 1.33 | 0.36 | 1 / 0 | L2 begins |
| 64 | 0.60 | 18.99 | 0.57 | 26.61 | 1.48 | 0.44 | 4 / 0 | L2 |
| 80 | 0.73 | 20.65 | 0.73 | 28.46 | 1.82 | 0.51 | 7 / 0 | L2 |
| 96 | 0.86 | 21.67 | 0.83 | 29.31 | 2.03 | 0.58 | 10 / 0 | L2 to L3 |
| 112 | 0.98 | 23.19 | 0.97 | 31.07 | 2.93 | 0.65 | 7 / 4 | L3 to L4 (M near 23.5) |

Note: A6 over a 16 s window has a noise floor of about 0.15 to 0.4 Nm and the ramp changes r during the window, so early A6 values are not exact. The trend and the later windows are consistent with 3.0 r Nm [D].

Figure 1. Replicated 240 s run: GEARBOX_WEAR injected at t = 0 with the default 120 s ramp; cycle peaks cross 26 Nm at about 58 s and 30 Nm at about 98 s [D].

Table 6. C02 case record
| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| 1. Case ID | C02. Simulated GEARBOX_WEAR held at severity r = 0.15, 40 s window (5 cycles), seeded. |
| 2. Machine operating condition | Production cycle, steady, warmed up. |
| 3. Sensor reading / time-series pattern | M 14.59 Nm, per-cycle peak mean 22.89 Nm (maximum sample 24.2 Nm), minimum mean 6.22 Nm, A6 0.62 Nm, sigma 0.55 Nm, TCP mean 0.19 mm. |
| 4. Baseline comparison | dM +1.6 Nm (S 0.15), peak +1.2 Nm, minimum +1.9 Nm, A6 above 0.4 watch, sigma 0.55 at the watch boundary, TCP +0.086 mm. |
| 5. Threshold comparison | No sample reaches 26 Nm; platform status normal throughout. Feature thresholds: M above 13.5 (watch), A6 above 0.4 (watch), peak below 23.5. |
| 6. Relevant operating state | Production cycle, steady, valid data. |
| 7. Symptoms | None visible to operators; TCP slightly above baseline. |
| 8. Candidate faults | F01 incipient wear; F02 lubrication; F03 brake drag; F09 thermal; F10 minor program change. |
| 9. Evidence supporting each candidate | F01: A6 / dM = 0.39, (kN - 1) / dM = 0.14, dTCP / dM = 0.054 mm per Nm, swing unchanged. F02 and F03 explain the mean only. F09 explains it if M is reversible. |
| 10. Evidence against alternatives | F03: no idle offset recorded. F09: M not reversible with temperature. F10: no program change in log. A6 and TCP ratios are not expected from friction faults. |
| 11. Diagnostic reasoning | The three locked ratios all fall inside the accept ranges even though the platform status is normal, so the evidence is specific rather than noise: M exceeds the healthy band by 10 sigma of the 5-cycle mean (0.05 Nm). A6 exceeds the 5-cycle healthy 95th percentile of 0.18 by a factor of 3. |
| 12. Final diagnosis | Incipient GEARBOX_WEAR (F01, stage 1). Level L1 watch, severity low, confidence medium to high (score 14, but baseline not independently confirmed). |
| 13. Recommended inspection | At next planned stop: lubricant sample and magnetic plug (T1); backlash baseline (T2); check lubrication records. |
| 14. Corrective action | Trend each shift; relubricate if due per OEM; schedule gear inspection if M exceeds 15 Nm. |
| 15. Expected post-maintenance telemetry | After successful service M returns to 12.5 to 13.5 Nm and A6 to at most 0.2 Nm; if A6 persists the wear is real. |
| 16. Verification result | Platform shows no state change either before or after; verification by features only. |

chunks.section: 3. Detailed Cases: Project Fault GEARBOX_WEAR > 3.3 C03 Sustained threshold violation: persistent warning [P][D]
chunks.text:
Table 7. C03 case record
| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| 1. Case ID | C03. Simulated GEARBOX_WEAR held at r = 0.6, 80 s (10 cycles), seeded. |
| 2. Machine operating condition | Production cycle, steady, valid data. |
| 3. Sensor reading / time-series pattern | M 19.31 Nm, per-cycle peak mean 27.12 Nm (maximum sample 27.9 Nm), minimum mean 11.4 Nm, A6 1.70 Nm, sigma 0.82 Nm, TCP mean 0.43 mm; 22 of 160 samples (13.8 percent) at or above 26 Nm; none at or above 30 Nm; 9 of 10 cycles contain a sample at or above 26 Nm. |
| 4. Baseline comparison | dM +6.3 Nm (S 0.60), peak +5.4 Nm, TCP +0.33 mm. |
| 5. Threshold comparison | Peak above warnHigh 26 for at least 2 consecutive cycles: WARNING opened (rule R-09). Below alarmHigh 30 Nm (maximum 27.9, margin 2.1 Nm). |
| 6. Relevant operating state | Production cycle, steady. |
| 7. Symptoms | Weld position scatter possible; amber on the twin each cycle. |
| 8. Candidate faults | F01 stage 3; F02; F07 payload; F05 looseness. |
| 9. Evidence supporting each candidate | F01: A6 / dM = 0.27, (kN - 1) / dM = (0.82 / 0.45 - 1) / 6.3 = 0.13, dTCP / dM = 0.052, swing unchanged. F02: only mean. F07: swing would change. F05: TCP shift per Nm would be much larger. |
| 10. Evidence against alternatives | No program or payload change; no step in M; spikes absent. |
| 11. Diagnostic reasoning | The platform flickers warn once per cycle because the peak crosses 26 Nm for 0.5 to 1 s per cycle. Persistence is satisfied on the peak envelope (9 of 10 cycles). With ratios in range, the leading diagnosis is F01. |
| 12. Final diagnosis | GEARBOX_WEAR stage 3; level L2 warning; severity medium; confidence high. |
| 13. Recommended inspection | Inspection at the next planned stop: oil, magnet, backlash, noise, fasteners. |
| 14. Corrective action | Schedule gear replacement; reduce duty if time to alarm is short. With slope 0.0875 Nm/s the alarm-equivalent M of 21.6 Nm is 26 s away at this simulator rate; for a real drift of 0.1 Nm per day it is about 23 days [D][E]. |
| 15. Expected post-maintenance telemetry | M 12.5 to 13.5, A6 at most 0.2, peak at most 23.1. |
| 16. Verification result | Platform shows normal for 600 s after repair. |

chunks.section: 3. Detailed Cases: Project Fault GEARBOX_WEAR > 3.4 C16 Severe and critical condition: gearbox wear beyond the modeled envelope [P][D][I]
chunks.text:
Table 8. C16 case record
| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| 1. Case ID | C16. Simulated GEARBOX_WEAR held at r = 1.0 (40 s window) with an additional isolated sample of 35.2 Nm [I]. |
| 2. Machine operating condition | Production cycle, alarm active for 10 minutes. |
| 3. Sensor reading / time-series pattern | M 23.54 Nm, per-cycle peak mean 32.51 Nm, maximum sample 33.7 Nm in the replicated window; one later sample 35.2 Nm; minimum mean 15.18 Nm; A6 3.34 Nm; sigma 1.13 Nm; TCP 0.66 mm; 10 samples warn and 17 alarm of 80 (12.5 and 21 percent). |
| 4. Baseline comparison | dM +10.5 Nm (S 1.0), minimum +10.9 Nm, TCP +0.56 mm. |
| 5. Threshold comparison | Per-cycle peak above 30 every cycle; M at 23.5 (critical-equivalent); sample at or above 34 Nm confirmed in the next cycle; alarm persistence longer than 10 minutes: CRITICAL by three independent criteria. |
| 6. Relevant operating state | Production cycle at full speed. |
| 7. Symptoms | Noise at axis 4, weld position error above tolerance, red pulsing mesh. |
| 8. Candidate faults | F01 stage 5; F07 overload or collision damage; F04 bearing; F05 looseness. |
| 9. Evidence supporting each candidate | F01: all ratios in range at full severity (A6 / dM 0.32, TCP / dM 0.053). F07 would explain 35.2 Nm only as a spike. |
| 10. Evidence against alternatives | Gradual onset and locked ratios exclude F07 as the primary cause; F11 excluded because the cycle pattern is present. |
| 11. Diagnostic reasoning | Every criterion for critical is met; the modeled fault saturates at a noise-free peak of 32.3 Nm, so a sample at 35.2 Nm is a tail event of full-severity noise (about 2.6 sigma above the peak) or a damage event; either way the machine is at the end of its modeled life. |
| 12. Final diagnosis | F01 beyond model, critical; confidence high; treat as probable tooth or bearing damage until inspection says otherwise. |
| 13. Recommended inspection | Stop at a safe point; lock-out; gearbox opening by specialist; inspect teeth, bearings, shaft. |
| 14. Corrective action | Replace gearbox; inspect motor and brake; re-master; verification run. |
| 15. Expected post-maintenance telemetry | After repair features return to the healthy band. |
| 16. Verification result | Return to service only after 600 s normal status and TCP at most 0.15 mm. |

chunks.document: Fault History Case Scenarios and Diagnostic Evidence
chunks.section: 4. Detailed Cases: Event, Intermittent and Non-Fault Conditions > 4.1 C04 Sudden abnormal spike: collision [E][I]
chunks.text:
Table 9. C04 case record
| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| 1. Case ID | C04. Illustrative collision of the weld gun with a fixture during one cycle of Robot Weld 01. |
| 2. Machine operating condition | Production cycle at 100 percent speed, warmed up, program unchanged until the event; the robot stops through its safety function after the contact. |
| 3. Sensor reading / time-series pattern | One sample of 41.3 Nm at 2.5 s of one cycle, with healthy values before and after it. In the following cycles after restart M is 13.8 Nm (+0.8), sigma 0.52 Nm, A6 0.14 Nm. TOOL_CENTER_POINT_DEVIATION mean steps from 0.10 to 0.35 mm within the same minute. |
| 4. Baseline comparison | Spike 19.6 Nm above the healthy peak of 21.75 Nm; M +0.8 Nm; sigma +0.07 Nm; TCP +0.25 mm (dTCP / dM = 0.31 mm per Nm, six times the F01 ratio). |
| 5. Threshold comparison | The sample exceeds alarmHigh 30 Nm and the proposed critical level 34 Nm. The per-cycle peak envelope falls back below 26 Nm in the next cycle, so no persistence-based alarm would open: the event is detected only by the single-sample rule. |
| 6. Relevant operating state | Production, then safety stop and restart. Thresholds apply to the cycles before and after, not to the stop itself. |
| 7. Symptoms | Controller collision or safety stop event; visible contact marks on the fixture or gun; weld position error afterwards. |
| 8. Candidate faults | F07 collision; F11 isolated spike; F12 data glitch; F05 looseness released by the impact; F01 sudden tooth damage. |
| 9. Evidence supporting each candidate | F07: isolated spike (3), TCP step large for the torque shift (1), other channel affected (1), step onset (3), unchanged swing and gun, event log shows collision (5): total 14. F05: TCP rise large for dM (3) plus baseline items: total 6. F11: isolated spike (2), step (3), gun unchanged (1): 6. |
| 10. Evidence against alternatives | F01: onset is a step, not a ramp, and A6 is unchanged at 0.14 Nm. F11 and F12: seq is continuous, the device is online and TCP changes consistently with the spike. |
| 11. Diagnostic reasoning | Rule R-11 alone would classify a single unconfirmed sample as a transient; rule R-27 overrides it because the spike is accompanied by a TCP step and an event log entry. The residual mean rise and noise increase after the event show that damage cannot be excluded, so the case stays at L4 until the mechanical inspection is complete. |
| 12. Final diagnosis | F07 overload by collision, possible secondary damage to the axis 4 gear train or coupling. Level L4 critical until inspected; confidence high for the event, medium for the extent of damage. |
| 13. Recommended inspection | Visual damage to tool and gun; tool data; fastener torque and torque marks; backlash at the flange; gearbox noise; mastering marks of axis 4 (Document 04 tasks T4 and T2). |
| 14. Corrective action | Repair or replace damaged parts; replace the coupling or gearbox if play or debris is found; re-master axis 4; re-baseline Sensor 1 and TCP. |
| 15. Expected post-maintenance telemetry | M 12.5 to 13.5 Nm, sigma 0.40 to 0.55 Nm, A6 at most 0.2 Nm, TCP mean at most 0.15 mm; no sample above 23.1 Nm. |
| 16. Verification result | Illustrative pass: 600 s with no spike; TCP back to 0.10 mm; backlash within the OEM limit; baseline stored. |

chunks.document: Fault History Case Scenarios and Diagnostic Evidence
chunks.section: 4. Detailed Cases: Event, Intermittent and Non-Fault Conditions > 4.2 C05 Intermittent abnormality: backlash spikes at reversals [E][I]
chunks.text:
Table 10. C05 case record
| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| 1. Case ID | C05. Illustrative worn coupling with free play between motor and gearbox of axis 4. |
| 2. Machine operating condition | Production cycle at 100 percent speed, steady; condition developed over several weeks. |
| 3. Sensor reading / time-series pattern | M 13.3 Nm; A6 0.35 Nm; sigma 0.50 Nm. In about 60 percent of cycles a spike of 4 to 6 Nm appears at about 2.5 s and at about 6.0 s of the cycle, the phases at which the torque reverses direction of change. TCP mean 0.21 mm. |
| 4. Baseline comparison | dM +0.3 Nm; dTCP +0.11 mm, so dTCP / dM = 0.37 mm per Nm, about seven times the F01 ratio of 0.052. No change of swing. |
| 5. Threshold comparison | No sample at or above 26 Nm except in about 5 percent of cycles where the 2.5 s spike reaches 27 Nm, so the per-cycle envelope never satisfies the two-cycle persistence rule. Platform status is normal almost all the time. |
| 6. Relevant operating state | Production, steady, valid data. |
| 7. Symptoms | Audible clunk at direction changes, weld position scatter, repeatability complaints from the quality team. |
| 8. Candidate faults | F05 backlash or looseness; F04 bearing degradation; F01 early wear; F06 dress pack drag. |
| 9. Evidence supporting each candidate | F05: spikes locked to the reversal phases (4), TCP rise large for the torque shift (3), swing unchanged (1), gun unchanged (1), gradual onset (1): total 10. F04: sparse spikes and noise but not phase-locked: 4. F01: 4. |
| 10. Evidence against alternatives | F01: dM is only +0.3 Nm and A6 is 0.35 Nm, below the 0.4 watch level and not in ratio with the TCP shift. F06: the disturbance is impulsive, not a smooth bump. F04: spikes are repeatable at fixed phases, not random. |
| 11. Diagnostic reasoning | Intermittency arises because the free play is only crossed when the load torque reverses sign through zero under certain combinations of speed and temperature. Phase-locking to the torque reversals, together with a TCP shift that is far larger than the mean torque shift suggests, is the discriminator that separates looseness from wear. |
| 12. Final diagnosis | F05 backlash or mechanical looseness; level L1 watch with quality risk; severity medium; confidence medium to high. |
| 13. Recommended inspection | Fastener torque of gearbox and motor mounting, coupling and key condition, backlash at the flange (Document 04 tasks T4 and T2). |
| 14. Corrective action | Retorque to the OEM specification; replace coupling or key if worn; adjust or replace the gear set if backlash exceeds the OEM limit; re-master axis 4 afterwards. |
| 15. Expected post-maintenance telemetry | Spikes absent over 20 cycles; A6 at most 0.2 Nm; TCP mean about 0.10 mm; M 12.5 to 13.5 Nm. |
| 16. Verification result | Illustrative pass: spike count zero over 20 cycles and 600 s with no warn; backlash measurement recorded as the new baseline. |
