chunks.document: Fault History Case Scenarios and Diagnostic Evidence
chunks.section: 4. Detailed Cases: Event, Intermittent and Non-Fault Conditions > 4.3 C06 False alarm after a program change [E][I]
chunks.text:
Table 11. C06 case record
| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| 1. Case ID | C06. Illustrative start of a new product program on Robot Weld 01, payload unchanged. |
| 2. Machine operating condition | Production with a new program ID, speed override 100 percent, warm-up complete. |
| 3. Sensor reading / time-series pattern | M steps from 13.0 to 15.8 Nm within one cycle; cycle swing grows to 8.6 Nm (from 7.0); per-cycle peak 26.4 Nm in several consecutive cycles; A6 0.12 Nm; sigma 0.47 Nm; TCP mean 0.10 mm. The waveform shape also differs from the stored template. |
| 4. Baseline comparison | dM +2.8 Nm; swing +23 percent; A6 and TCP at baseline; sigma at baseline. |
| 5. Threshold comparison | Per-cycle peak at or above 26 Nm for three consecutive cycles: a warning would open on thresholds alone (rule R-09), and the twin shows an amber flicker once per cycle. |
| 6. Relevant operating state | Production, but with a changed program: the baseline of Document 01 does not apply to the new motion. |
| 7. Symptoms | None on the machine; the operator knows the program changed. |
| 8. Candidate faults | F10 program change; F07 payload or tool data change; F01 early wear; F02 lubrication. |
| 9. Evidence supporting each candidate | F10: step onset (3), swing changed (3), other channels may change (1), event log shows planned program change (5), dM (1): total 13. F07: swing changed (3), step (3), dM (2), other (1), event log (2): 11. |
| 10. Evidence against alternatives | F01: A6 absent and TCP unchanged, swing changed (F01 leaves the swing unchanged). F02 and F03: swing would not change and no idle offset is reported. |
| 11. Diagnostic reasoning | A step in mean with a change of swing and no ripple is the signature of a load or program change, not of wear (rule R-12 and R-26). The margin between F10 and F07 is 2 points, so the agent must confirm from the tool data that the payload did not change before closing the case as a program change. |
| 12. Final diagnosis | F10 program change: not a fault. The threshold alert is a false alarm for gearbox wear. Confidence medium until tool and payload data are confirmed. |
| 13. Recommended inspection | Check the program log and tool and payload data only; no mechanical inspection. |
| 14. Corrective action | Re-baseline Sensor 1 for the new program and store it with the program ID; adjust the watch levels if the new program is permanent. |
| 15. Expected post-maintenance telemetry | New baseline stable over 20 cycles; A6 at most 0.2 Nm; sigma 0.40 to 0.55 Nm. |
| 16. Verification result | Illustrative result: the alert is closed with the note program change; no wear conclusion; the old baseline is kept for the old program. |

chunks.document: Fault History Case Scenarios and Diagnostic Evidence
chunks.section: 4. Detailed Cases: Event, Intermittent and Non-Fault Conditions > 4.4 C07 Non-fault: cold-start warm-up [E][I]
chunks.text:
Table 12. C07 case record
| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| 1. Case ID | C07. Illustrative restart after a weekend stop, gearbox at ambient temperature. |
| 2. Machine operating condition | First 20 minutes of production after the restart, program unchanged. |
| 3. Sensor reading / time-series pattern | M is 14.4 Nm in the first cycles and falls steadily to 13.2 Nm after 20 minutes; A6 stays at 0.10 Nm; sigma 0.47 Nm; TCP 0.10 mm throughout. |
| 4. Baseline comparison | dM starts at +1.4 Nm and decays to +0.2 Nm; no change in A6, sigma or TCP. |
| 5. Threshold comparison | M is above the 13.5 Nm watch level only during the first minutes; no sample reaches 26 Nm; the per-cycle peak stays below 23.5 Nm. |
| 6. Relevant operating state | Warm-up after a long stop. Thresholds and baselines must not be evaluated in this state (rule R-06). |
| 7. Symptoms | None. |
| 8. Candidate faults | F09 cold viscosity; F02 lubrication degradation; F01 incipient wear. |
| 9. Evidence supporting each candidate | F09 and the warm-up component of F02: the offset is reversible and decays with running time. |
| 10. Evidence against alternatives | F01: A6 and TCP are unchanged and wear does not decay after restart. F02 persistent part: the offset disappears fully. |
| 11. Diagnostic reasoning | A reversible offset with a time constant of minutes, no ripple and no TCP effect is explained by lubricant viscosity. The state gate applies first; the agent should not open an investigation. If the offset does not decay, the case becomes C10. |
| 12. Final diagnosis | Warm-up effect (normal operation). No fault; level L1 only during the first minutes. |
| 13. Recommended inspection | None. |
| 14. Corrective action | None. Exclude the warm-up cycles from baseline and trend calculations. |
| 15. Expected post-maintenance telemetry | M within 12.5 to 13.5 Nm after warm-up. |
| 16. Verification result | Illustrative result: no alert; the stable M after 20 minutes confirms that the effect is thermal. |

| 6. Relevant operating state | Warm-up after a long stop. Thresholds and baselines must not be evaluated in this state (rule R-06). |
| 7. Symptoms | None. |
| 8. Candidate faults | F09 cold viscosity; F02 lubrication degradation; F01 incipient wear. |
| 9. Evidence supporting each candidate | F09 and the warm-up component of F02: the offset is reversible and decays with running time. |
| 10. Evidence against alternatives | F01: A6 and TCP are unchanged and wear does not decay after restart. F02 persistent part: the offset disappears fully. |
| 11. Diagnostic reasoning | A reversible offset with a time constant of minutes, no ripple and no TCP effect is explained by lubricant viscosity. The state gate applies first; the agent should not open an investigation. If the offset does not decay, the case becomes C10. |
| 12. Final diagnosis | Warm-up effect (normal operation). No fault; level L1 only during the first minutes. |
| 13. Recommended inspection | None. |
| 14. Corrective action | None. Exclude the warm-up cycles from baseline and trend calculations. |
| 15. Expected post-maintenance telemetry | M within 12.5 to 13.5 Nm after warm-up. |
| 16. Verification result | Illustrative result: no alert; the stable M after 20 minutes confirms that the effect is thermal. |

chunks.text:
Table 13. C08 case record
| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| 1. Case ID | C08. Illustrative controller interface that stops updating the torque value while the robot continues to move. |
| 2. Machine operating condition | Program running, robot moving normally, no controller alarms. |
| 3. Sensor reading / time-series pattern | Torque constant at 13.0 Nm for 60 s; sigma 0.0 Nm; TCP deviation shows its normal 0.008 mm noise around 0.10 mm; gun temperature follows its weld cycle. |
| 4. Baseline comparison | Variance zero versus 0.45 Nm; swing 0 versus 7.0 Nm; no 8 s periodicity. |
| 5. Threshold comparison | Status normal; no limit is crossed, so a threshold-only agent would report a healthy axis. |
| 6. Relevant operating state | Production (the program is running). |
| 7. Symptoms | The twin shows a steady colour and no cycle trace; operators see nothing abnormal at the robot. |
| 8. Candidate faults | F11 flatline; F12 stale data; idle state; F10 program change. |
| 9. Evidence supporting each candidate | F11: flatline (4), step onset (3), gun unchanged (1), and rule R-19 for sigma below 0.1 Nm (4): total 12. The other channels move normally and the program is running. |
| 10. Evidence against alternatives | F12: seq is continuous, the device is not stale and the other channels update. Idle: the program is running. F10: the swing would still be present in a changed program. |
| 11. Diagnostic reasoning | A healthy axis shows sigma 0.45 Nm and a swing of 7 Nm; a perfectly constant value is physically impossible while the arm moves. The state of the other channels excludes a data-path failure. |
| 12. Final diagnosis | F11 signal fault, level LS; no mechanical conclusion. |
| 13. Recommended inspection | Data-path validation (Document 04 task T6): controller interface, scaling, gateway diag fields. |
| 14. Corrective action | Correct the interface or scaling; restart the gateway or controller task if needed. |
| 15. Expected post-maintenance telemetry | Cycle trace returns with sigma about 0.45 Nm and the 8 s periodicity. |
| 16. Verification result | Illustrative pass: autocorrelation peak at 8 s restored; features within baseline. |

chunks.document: Fault History Case Scenarios and Diagnostic Evidence
chunks.section: 4. Detailed Cases: Event, Intermittent and Non-Fault Conditions > 4.6 C09 Measurement issue: data loss hides peaks [E][I]
chunks.text:
Table 14. C09 case record
| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| 1. Case ID | C09. Illustrative weak Wi-Fi link on the ESP32 gateway while real wear is developing. |
| 2. Machine operating condition | Production cycle; underlying wear at S about 0.55. |
| 3. Sensor reading / time-series pattern | 35 percent of the samples are missing; the observed per-cycle peak is 24.8 Nm while the true peak is about 26.5 Nm; seq has gaps; diag shows rising wifiReconnects and a low rssi. |
| 4. Baseline comparison | The observed peak underestimates the true peak by about 1.7 Nm; the observed M is stable but noisy. |
| 5. Threshold comparison | No sample at or above 26 Nm is seen in 4 of 5 cycles: the platform shows normal although the true warn limit is crossed in about half of the cycles. |
| 6. Relevant operating state | Production, steady. |
| 7. Symptoms | Gaps in the twin trace and in the history chart. |
| 8. Candidate faults | F12 data-path fault; masked F01 wear. |
| 9. Evidence supporting each candidate | F12: gaps in seq, reconnect counters rising, low rssi. F01: the surviving samples still show a mean shift and TCP rise. |
| 10. Evidence against alternatives | F11: the signal varies and other channels also have gaps. |
| 11. Diagnostic reasoning | Missing samples can remove the one or two samples near the cycle peak, which are the only ones that cross the limit, so a data-loss window under-reports severity. Rule R-02 marks the window incomplete and lowers the confidence; the mean, TCP and A6 of the surviving samples must still be evaluated. |
| 12. Final diagnosis | F12 data-path fault with a possible masked F01; confidence medium. |
| 13. Recommended inspection | Network and gateway check (rssi, reconnects, band); then a complete window. |
| 14. Corrective action | Improve the Wi-Fi link (2.4 GHz, signal strength), restart the gateway, and re-evaluate with a complete window. |
| 15. Expected post-maintenance telemetry | No seq gaps; peak and features reflect the true state. |
| 16. Verification result | Illustrative result: with a complete window the true peak of 26.5 Nm is seen and the case becomes a C03-type warning. |

chunks.document: Fault History Case Scenarios and Diagnostic Evidence
chunks.section: 5. Detailed Cases: Friction, Brake, Drag and Transitions > 5.1 C10 Friction family: lubrication loss [E][I]
chunks.text:
Table 15. C10 case record
| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| 1. Case ID | C10. Illustrative overdue relubrication of the axis 4 gearbox. |
| 2. Machine operating condition | Production, steady, after warm-up; the lubrication record shows the last service is beyond the OEM schedule. |
| 3. Sensor reading / time-series pattern | M 17.0 Nm (S 0.38); A6 0.12 Nm; sigma 0.52 Nm; TCP 0.11 mm; idle torque +1.1 Nm above the earlier record; M is 1.0 Nm higher right after a cold start. |
| 4. Baseline comparison | dM +4.0 Nm; A6 / dM = 0.03 (F01 expects 0.29); dTCP / dM = 0.002 (F01 expects 0.052). |
| 5. Threshold comparison | Per-cycle peak mean 24.4 Nm; no sample at or above 26 Nm; level L1 to L2 by features, platform status normal. |
| 6. Relevant operating state | Production. |
| 7. Symptoms | Warm gearbox housing, grease discolouration at the vent. |
| 8. Candidate faults | F02 lubrication loss; F03 brake drag; F09 thermal; F01 wear. |
| 9. Evidence supporting each candidate | F02: gradual onset (1), idle offset (1), reversible part (1), swing and gun unchanged (2), dM (2): 7, with the lubrication record as extra context. F03 and F09 also score 7 on the matrix. |
| 10. Evidence against alternatives | F01: A6 and TCP ratios absent. F03: the brake is cold and the idle offset is smaller than the mean shift. F09: only part of the offset is reversible. |
| 11. Diagnostic reasoning | The mean shift without ripple or TCP effect indicates friction. Three friction candidates tie, so the decisive tests are ordered by cost: lubricant check (cheapest and supported by the overdue record), then warm-up comparison, then brake voltage. |
| 12. Final diagnosis | F02 lubrication degradation; level L2 by features; severity medium; confidence low until the lubricant is inspected, then medium to high. |
| 13. Recommended inspection | Lubricant level, colour and sample; magnetic plug; seals (Document 04 task T1). |
| 14. Corrective action | Relubricate or replace the lubricant per the OEM grade; replace seals if leaking; run a warm-up and re-baseline. |
| 15. Expected post-maintenance telemetry | M 12.5 to 13.5 Nm; warm-up offset at most 0.5 Nm; A6 at most 0.2 Nm. |
| 16. Verification result | Illustrative pass: warm-up offset 0.3 Nm after service; features healthy; no particles in the sample. |

chunks.document: Fault History Case Scenarios and Diagnostic Evidence
chunks.section: 5. Detailed Cases: Friction, Brake, Drag and Transitions > 5.2 C11 Brake drag [E][I]
chunks.text:
Table 16. C11 case record
| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| 1. Case ID | C11. Illustrative holding brake that releases late and drags during motion. |
| 2. Machine operating condition | Production cycle; condition appears after a power event. |
| 3. Sensor reading / time-series pattern | M 16.2 Nm; A6 0.1 Nm; sigma 0.47 Nm; idle torque +3.2 Nm above the earlier record; brake housing hotter than neighbouring axes; TCP 0.12 mm. |
| 4. Baseline comparison | dM +3.2 Nm and idle offset +3.2 Nm: equal within measurement error. |
| 5. Threshold comparison | No sample at or above 26 Nm; level L1 to L2 by features. |
| 6. Relevant operating state | Production and idle both show the offset. |
| 7. Symptoms | Brake release click absent, warm housing, higher drive current at standstill. |
| 8. Candidate faults | F03 brake drag; F08 drive offset; F02 lubrication loss. |
| 9. Evidence supporting each candidate | F03: idle offset (3), brake locally hot (3), step onset (2), dM (2), swing and gun unchanged (2): total 12. F08: idle offset (3), step (2), dM (1) and others: 8. |
| 10. Evidence against alternatives | F08: the brake is hot, which a pure measurement offset would not cause. F02: idle offset would be smaller than the mean shift and the housing would not be hot. |
| 11. Diagnostic reasoning | A constant Coulomb torque from a dragging brake adds the same torque during motion and at idle, so the equal offsets are the discriminator. The temperature rise confirms energy dissipation in the brake. |
| 12. Final diagnosis | F03 brake drag; level L2; severity medium to high because overheating can follow. |
| 13. Recommended inspection | Brake supply voltage during release, release timing, disc and armature (Document 04 task T3). |
| 14. Corrective action | Correct the supply voltage or wiring; replace the brake if worn; verify release timing in the controller. |
| 15. Expected post-maintenance telemetry | Idle offset zero; M 12.5 to 13.5 Nm; brake temperature normal. |
| 16. Verification result | Illustrative pass: idle torque back to the earlier hold value; 600 s with normal status. |

chunks.document: Fault History Case Scenarios and Diagnostic Evidence
chunks.section: 5. Detailed Cases: Friction, Brake, Drag and Transitions > 5.3 C12 External drag: dress pack bump [E][I]
chunks.text:
Table 17. C12 case record
| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| 1. Case ID | C12. Illustrative tight dress pack after a tool change. |
| 2. Machine operating condition | Production cycle, steady, program unchanged. |
| 3. Sensor reading / time-series pattern | A bump of +3.4 Nm appears at about 1.2 s in every cycle; M 13.6 Nm; A6 0.2 Nm; sigma 0.46 Nm; TCP 0.10 mm. |
| 4. Baseline comparison | Residual to the template is 3.4 Nm in one window about 1 s wide and below 0.5 Nm elsewhere. |
| 5. Threshold comparison | No limit is crossed: the peak stays below 23.5 Nm because the bump lies on the rising part of the cycle, not at the maximum. |
| 6. Relevant operating state | Production, steady. |
| 7. Symptoms | Visible cable tension at one pose; jerky motion at that pose. |
| 8. Candidate faults | F06 external drag; F05 looseness; F01 early wear. |
| 9. Evidence supporting each candidate | F06: smooth bump in one phase window (4), swing and gun unchanged (2), step onset after the tool change (1): total 7. F05: 4. F07: 5. |
| 10. Evidence against alternatives | F05: the disturbance is smooth, not an impulse at a reversal. F01: the shift is local, not whole-cycle, and A6 is below 0.4 Nm. |
| 11. Diagnostic reasoning | Posture-dependent drag affects only the segment of the stroke where the cable is tensioned; its position in the cycle tells which pose. |
| 12. Final diagnosis | F06 external drag; level L1; severity low to medium (cable damage risk). |
| 13. Recommended inspection | Dress pack routing and slack across the whole stroke; seal and cover contact (Document 04 task T5). |
| 14. Corrective action | Re-route the dress pack, adjust slack, replace worn guides, clean spatter. |
| 15. Expected post-maintenance telemetry | Bump removed; M 12.5 to 13.5 Nm. |
| 16. Verification result | Illustrative pass: residual below 1 Nm in every phase of the cycle. |

chunks.section: 5. Detailed Cases: Friction, Brake, Drag and Transitions > 5.4 C13 Similar patterns, different causes: wear versus friction [E][I]
chunks.text:
Table 18. C13 case record
| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| 1. Case ID | C13. Two windows from two periods on the same robot: W-A (gearbox wear) and W-B (lubrication loss). |
| 2. Machine operating condition | Both in production, steady, warmed up (W-B also analysed cold). |
| 3. Sensor reading / time-series pattern | W-A: M 18.1, peak 26.3, A6 1.6, sigma 0.78, TCP 0.41 mm, idle offset 0. W-B: M 18.0, peak 26.2, A6 0.10, sigma 0.55, TCP 0.11 mm, idle +1.4 Nm, M falls by 1.2 Nm after warm-up. |
| 4. Baseline comparison | Both have dM about +5.0 Nm (S about 0.48). |
| 5. Threshold comparison | Both are at the warning boundary: peaks 26.2 and 26.3 Nm. |
| 6. Relevant operating state | Production, steady. |
| 7. Symptoms | W-A: TCP drift and weld position scatter. W-B: warm housing. |
| 8. Candidate faults | F01 versus F02, with F03 and F09 as further friction candidates. |
| 9. Evidence supporting each candidate | W-A: A6 / dM 0.32 and dTCP / dM 0.061 within the F01 ranges, kN 1.73. W-B: A6 / dM 0.02, dTCP / dM 0.001, reversible warm-up part, idle offset. |
| 10. Evidence against alternatives | W-A excludes F02 because ripple and TCP rise are present; W-B excludes F01 because they are absent. |
| 11. Diagnostic reasoning | The mean and the peak are identical, so a threshold-only view cannot separate them. The ratios A6 / dM and dTCP / dM, the idle offset and the warm-up behaviour separate them reliably. |
| 12. Final diagnosis | W-A is F01 gearbox wear (stage 3); W-B is F02 lubrication loss (stage 2, friction family). |
| 13. Recommended inspection | W-A: gearbox oil, magnet, backlash. W-B: lubricant level and condition. |
| 14. Corrective action | W-A: plan gearbox replacement. W-B: relubricate. |
| 15. Expected post-maintenance telemetry | Each returns to baseline after its own repair; W-A also needs the TCP back at 0.10 mm. |
| 16. Verification result | Illustrative pass for both; applying the wrong repair would leave the other window unchanged. |

| 10. Evidence against alternatives | W-A excludes F02 because ripple and TCP rise are present; W-B excludes F01 because they are absent. |
| 11. Diagnostic reasoning | The mean and the peak are identical, so a threshold-only view cannot separate them. The ratios A6 / dM and dTCP / dM, the idle offset and the warm-up behaviour separate them reliably. |
| 12. Final diagnosis | W-A is F01 gearbox wear (stage 3); W-B is F02 lubrication loss (stage 2, friction family). |
| 13. Recommended inspection | W-A: gearbox oil, magnet, backlash. W-B: lubricant level and condition. |
| 14. Corrective action | W-A: plan gearbox replacement. W-B: relubricate. |
| 15. Expected post-maintenance telemetry | Each returns to baseline after its own repair; W-A also needs the TCP back at 0.10 mm. |
| 16. Verification result | Illustrative pass for both; applying the wrong repair would leave the other window unchanged. |

chunks.section: 5. Detailed Cases: Friction, Brake, Drag and Transitions > 5.5 C14 Transition from lubrication loss to wear [E][I]
chunks.text:
Table 19. C14 case record
| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| 1. Case ID | C14. Illustrative continuation of C10 after relubrication. |
| 2. Machine operating condition | Production, steady, three days after the lubricant service. |
| 3. Sensor reading / time-series pattern | After service M falls from 17.0 to 15.2 Nm but not to baseline; A6 rises from 0.12 to 0.70 Nm; TCP 0.17 mm; the oil sample taken during service showed fines on the magnet. |
| 4. Baseline comparison | dM +2.2 Nm; A6 / dM = 0.32; dTCP / dM = 0.03. |
| 5. Threshold comparison | No limit crossed; M above the 15.0 Nm early-degradation boundary. |
| 6. Relevant operating state | Production. |
| 7. Symptoms | None noticed. |
| 8. Candidate faults | F01 emerging wear; residual F02; F04. |
| 9. Evidence supporting each candidate | F01: with the friction part removed the remaining mean shift carries the ripple ratio of F01 (A6 / dM 0.32), swing unchanged. Matrix score F01 12, F04 6. |
| 10. Evidence against alternatives | A purely friction fault would have returned to baseline after service. |
| 11. Diagnostic reasoning | Removing the friction contribution exposes the underlying wear: the part of the shift that did not respond to lubrication is the part with ripple. |
| 12. Final diagnosis | Emerging GEARBOX_WEAR (F01) stage 1 to 2. |
| 13. Recommended inspection | Oil particle analysis and backlash (tasks T1 and T2); trend A6. |
| 14. Corrective action | Plan gear inspection and replacement before alarm; shorten the oil sampling interval. |
| 15. Expected post-maintenance telemetry | Features return to baseline only after gear replacement. |
| 16. Verification result | Illustrative result: replacement planned at the next stop; A6 trend monitored until then. |

chunks.text:
Table 20. C15 case record
| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| 1. Case ID | C15. Illustrative return of axis 4 to production after replacement of the gear set. |
| 2. Machine operating condition | Warm-up complete, program unchanged, payload unchanged. |
| 3. Sensor reading / time-series pattern | 20 cycles: M 13.04 Nm, per-cycle peak mean 21.8 Nm, minimum mean 4.3 Nm, A6 0.10 Nm, sigma 0.46 Nm, TCP 0.10 mm. During the first 3 cycles of run-in M was 13.9 Nm. |
| 4. Baseline comparison | Within the healthy tolerance on every feature. |
| 5. Threshold comparison | Below all thresholds; no sample at or above 23.1 Nm. |
| 6. Relevant operating state | Production after verification. |
| 7. Symptoms | None. |
| 8. Candidate faults | Residual fault (F02, F03, F08) after the repair; verified repair. |
| 9. Evidence supporting each candidate | All Document 03 verification criteria are met; the run-in transient decays within 3 cycles. |
| 10. Evidence against alternatives | A residual friction fault would keep M above 13.5 Nm and a residual wear would leave A6 above 0.2 Nm. |
| 11. Diagnostic reasoning | Every verification criterion is inside its band over 20 cycles, and the status stays normal for 600 s. |
| 12. Final diagnosis | Verified repair; the baseline is stored with the new gearbox serial and program ID. |
| 13. Recommended inspection | No further inspection; confirm after 24 h of production. |
| 14. Corrective action | None. |
| 15. Expected post-maintenance telemetry | M 12.5 to 13.5 Nm; A6 at most 0.2; sigma 0.40 to 0.55; peak at most 23.1; TCP at most 0.15 mm. |
| 16. Verification result | Illustrative pass: 600 s soak normal and the 24 h recheck within band. |

chunks.section: 7. Summary, Safety Notes, References and Revision > 7.1 Diagnostic summary; 7.2 Key decision criteria; 7.3 Safety and escalation notes; 7.4 References and engineering basis; 7.5 Revision notes
chunks.text:
• Cases C01 to C03 and C16 show that the project fault is recognisable from features about 40 s

before the first platform warning at the default ramp, and that the three locked ratios separate it from friction, event and data faults.

• Cases C04 to C15 show how events, non-fault states, sensor faults and data loss produce

thresholds crossings or normal status that can mislead a threshold-only agent.

• warn 26 Nm, alarm 30 Nm [P]; critical 34 Nm [I]; M band 12.5 to 13.5 Nm; A6 watch 0.4 Nm; ratios

A6 / dM 0.2 to 0.4, (kN - 1) / dM about 0.14, dTCP / dM about 0.052 mm per Nm.

All inspections require lock-out and tag-out and the OEM procedure. L4 conditions and suspected collisions require a safe stop and specialist inspection. The cases are illustrations for a prototype and not plant history.

• Repository simulation equations and tests [P]; Documents 01 to 04 of this suite; general condition

monitoring practice [E].
